```text
           └┬──────────┬─────────┬──────────┬─────────┬┘
            0         103       206        309      412 
```

---

### 4. Acceptance Criteria & Target Metrics

| Parameter / Metric | Acceptance Specification Target | Control Limits (LCL / UCL) | Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Residual ILD Thickness ($\bar{t}$)** | $400.0\text{ nm}$ | $[380.0\text{ nm},\ 420.0\text{ nm}]$ ($\pm 5\%$) | $\text{nm}$ | 49-point SE Cauchy regression ($\lambda = 240 - 800\text{ nm}$) |
| **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU, $1\sigma$)** | $\le 3.0\%$ | $\text{UCL} = 3.5\%$ | $\%$ | $\left(\frac{\sigma}{\bar{t}}\right) \times 100\%$ ($R \le 97\text{ mm}$, $3\text{ mm}$ edge excl.) |
| **Goodness-of-Fit / Regression Quality ($\text{MSE}$)** | $\le 1.50$ | $\text{UCL} = 2.00$ | dimensionless | Levenberg-Marquardt residual fit to $\Psi / \Delta$ curves |
| **Max Peak-to-Valley Planarity Range ($\Delta t_{\max}$)** | $\le 25.0\text{ nm}$ | $\text{UCL} = 30.0\text{ nm}$ | $\text{nm}$ | $(t_{\max} - t_{\min})$ over 49 metrology sites |

---

### 5. Verified Literature & Context Citations

- **[SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid](./docs/context.yaml)**:
  - Minimum poly gate length: $150\text{ nm}$ ($0.15\ \mu\text{m}$); minimum poly gate spacing: $0.21\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Minimum contact hole dimension: $0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Lithography & Focus Budget: DUV $248\text{ nm}$ KrF laser with $\text{NA} = 0.65$, $k_1 = 0.40$ yielding $152\text{ nm}$ half-pitch limit; tight post-CMP residual ILD thickness control is mandatory to prevent depth-of-focus (DOF) defocus margins during subsequent contact hole printing.
- **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench](./docs/context.yaml)**:
  - Transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Drain contact connection via tungsten plug (W-plug) to stacked capacitor (crown polysilicon/MIM). ILD oxide height must maintain strict uniformity across memory array and peripheral logic to prevent tungsten punch-through or incomplete contact etch.
- **[Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity](./docs/context.yaml)**:
  - Contact resistance characterization ($R_c$, $\rho_c$, $L_T$) on metal-diffusion interfaces relies directly on uniform ILD oxide opening and subsequent plug fill.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-CMP ellipsometry integration must account for systematic optical model drift caused by underlying topography and optical interference from multi-layer stacks (ILD oxide over Si3N4 etch stop and polysilicon gates in 180nm DRAM). Relying solely on a single-layer Cauchy or Sellmeier model over patterned test pads risks cross-correlation errors between film thickness and refractive index (n, k). The recipe must mandate dedicated, unpatterned scribe-line macro-sites (>80x80 um) or calibrated multi-layer Bruggeman Effective Medium Approximation (BEMA) fitting with fixed sub-layer optical dispersion tables.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometry across 250 nm to 850 nm is sensitive to residual sub-nanometer organic surfactant films, post-CMP slurry particle contamination (colloidal silica), and moisture adsorption layers on hydrophilic polished SiO2 surfaces. Measuring immediately post-CMP without standard post-CMP megasonic cleaning and Marangoni drying induces phase angle Delta shifts exceeding 2.5 degrees, yielding artifactual within-wafer non-uniformity (WIWNU) readings and apparent surface roughness (sigma_roughness > 1.2 nm). An automated Mean Squared Error (MSE) threshold of <= 2.0 must be enforced for valid point acquisition.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: High-throughput inline spectroscopic ellipsometers (e.g., KLA ASET-F5x or Therma-Wave Opti-Probe class) depend on high-stability broadband Xenon/Deuterium arc lamps, which exhibit spectral irradiance degradation after 1,000 to 1,200 operating hours. Uncalibrated lamp drift alters UV signal-to-noise ratio, inflating standard deviation in 49-point wafer mapping. Sourcing certified NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration wafers (100 nm and 1,000 nm SiO2/Si standards) and spare polarizers/compensators is essential to prevent fab line stoppages.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: To maintain fab cycle time and tight Q-time windows ahead of post-CMP contact lithography, the 49-point wafer mapping protocol must execute within <= 95 seconds per wafer, including robotic handling, pattern recognition alignment, and automated regression fitting. The metrology step must output automated SPC charts for Removal Rate (RR) and WIWNU (1-sigma percentage) directly to the MES to dynamically adjust CMP downforce and carrier zone backpressures for subsequent lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Optical dispersion parameter correlation failure where thickness (t) and refractive index (n) become mathematically degenerate due to poor spectral bandwidth or improper parameter floating, leading to systematic thickness offsets of >15 nm.
1. Post-CMP slurry residue/water-mark crystallization on optical measurement pads causing beam scattering, light depolarisation, and regression fit blowouts (MSE > 10.0), masking severe edge roll-off or center-fast polish non-uniformities.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-2-3-01` | **49-Point Post-ILD Oxide CMP Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Thickness and WIWNU Verification** | Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (spectral range 240-800 nm, 70-degree angle of incidence, micro-spot size <= 30x40 um) with motorized automated r-theta stage and NIST-traceable calibration standard. | 1. Load 200mm post-CMP production/DoE wafer onto the vacuum chuck. 2. Perform automated optical notch alignment and pattern recognition on designated scribe-line dielectric test pads (100x100 um). 3. Execute 49-point polar map (concentric rings: center, 0.3R, 0.6R, 0.85R, and 0.95R with 3mm edge exclusion). 4. Measure spectral Psi(lambda) and Delta(lambda) from 250 nm to 800 nm with 200 ms integration time per site. 5. Fit experimental data using calibrated Sellmeier model (SiO2 on Si substrate). 6. Calculate mean remaining oxide thickness (T_mean), standard deviation (sigma), and percentage Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity using formula: WIWNU (%) = (sigma / T_mean) * 100. | `Target remaining oxide thickness T_mean = 550.0 nm +/- 25.0 nm; WIWNU (1-sigma) <= 3.5%; Mean Squared Error (MSE) of regression fit <= 2.50 across all 49 measured sites; Zero sites reporting depolarization > 2.0%.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-2-3-02` | **High-Density Radial Edge-Exclusion (EER) Profile and Roll-Off Gradient Metrology** | High-Resolution Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer configured with high-precision edge-handling stage and knife-edge beam-shaping optics (micro-spot 20x30 um). | 1. Load wafer and execute alignment. 2. Define linear radial scan along wafer diameter at 0, 90, 180, and 270 degrees across the wafer edge zone from r = 85 mm to r = 98 mm in 0.5 mm steps (down to 2.0 mm edge exclusion). 3. Measure spectral polarization change and extract thickness using validated Cauchy model. 4. Compute thickness gradient delta_T/delta_r across the outer 5 mm annular band. | `Radial thickness roll-off gradient |delta_T / delta_r| <= 8.0 nm/mm in the r = 92 mm to 97 mm zone; Remaining oxide thickness at r = 97 mm must not deviate by more than +/- 45.0 nm from wafer center thickness; Fit quality goodness-of-fit R^2 >= 0.990.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required during handling), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses (protection against Xenon/Deuterium lamp broadband emission), Standard antistatic ESD-compliant cleanroom smock, hood, and conductive footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to IPA: Rinse cautiously with sterile eyewash solution for 15 minutes. Inhalation of inert gas (N2 displacement): Relocate victim immediately to fresh air; administer artificial respiration or oxygen if breathing is labored. UV Lamp exposure: Cease exposure, consult medical staff if skin erythema or corneal flash occurs.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Metrology equipment enclosure must maintain positive laminar air flow (HEPA filtered, Class 1 / ISO 3 mini-environment). Arc lamp assembly requires dedicated mechanical heat and ozone exhaust ducting with continuous negative pressure differential monitoring (>= 0.05 kPa).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA maintenance wipes must be segregated into sealed, airtight, grounded, flame-retardant solvent waste bins. Spent Xenon/Deuterium arc discharge lamps contain pressurized trace gases and heavy metal electrodes; decommissioned lamps must be depressurized per OEM instructions and collected as hazardous e-waste.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (Purge/Float)** | `7727-37-9` | Semiconductor Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (Stage/Wafer Chuck Surface Cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic/VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic polished SiO2 surface, post-megasonic DIW rinse and spin dry, zero slurry precipitate, residual particulate defect density < 0.05 defects/cm2 (>0.18 um).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Dry, contamination-free, stable surface oxide with passivated native chemical oxide interface, staged for post-CMP clean review or contact lithography coating.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air Q-time causes ambient airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption, notably volatile organic compounds (VOCs) and moisture/silanol condensation, which artificially shifts the optical phase angle Delta by > 3 degrees and leads to erroneous film thickness calculations, or causes irreversible moisture absorption into porous low-k/ILD oxide requiring vacuum bake.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Completion of 49-point automated spectroscopic ellipsometry mapping on post-CMP ILD oxide wafers confirming target thickness, Prestonian removal rate compliance, within-wafer non-uniformity (WIWNU), and automated regression fit validity across the full 200mm diameter.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `METROLOGY_POST_CMP_49PT_MAP_LOT7102.csv`
- [ ] `ILD_OXIDE_CMP_WIWNU_CONTOUR_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `ELLIPSOMETRY_DISPERSION_FIT_RESIDUALS.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean remaining post-CMP ILD oxide thickness across 49 wafer mapping points** | `550.0 nm` | +/- 20.0 nm | Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometry regression analysis utilizing Sellmeier dispersion model over 250-800 nm spectral window. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU 1-sigma percentage) across 49 measured sites with 3mm edge exclusion** | `2.8%` | <= 3.5% | Statistical calculation: (Standard Deviation of 49 points / Mean Thickness of 49 points) * 100. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Goodness of fit regression Mean Squared Error (MSE) across all 49 measurement locations** | `1.40` | <= 2.00 | Levenberg-Marquardt nonlinear regression fit comparison between experimental and modeled Psi and Delta spectral data. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 49 wafer mapping points successfully acquired with zero pattern-recognition failures; calculated WIWNU <= 3.5%; mean thickness within 550.0 +/- 20.0 nm; MSE <= 2.00 across all sites; deliverable CSV and contour PDF generated and signed off by Metrology Module Lead and CMP Process Engineer.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Post-CMP Removal Rate (MRR) Extraction, WIWNU Analysis & Surface Defectivity Inspection

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-CMP metrology must tightly close the feedback loop with the Prestonian polishing module; any drift in material removal rate (MRR) or within-wafer non-uniformity (WIWNU) directly degrades photolithography depth-of-focus (DoF) margins at subsequent 180nm contact and metal-1 masking steps.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometry modeling on polished ILD oxide requires a dual-layer Cauchy or Sellmeier formulation to decouple refractive index shifts caused by mechanical sub-surface damage from actual physical film thickness variation, while 49-point polar mapping is required to accurately capture edge roll-off effects.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology throughput is bounded by automated stage stepping and cassette-to-cassette wafer handling; secondary calibration standards (NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration wafers) and cleanroom nitrogen purges must have redundant stocking to prevent idle down-time.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Ensure inspection recipes and automated wafer maps are locked into the MES with automated go/no-go interlocks prior to running production-grade split lots, preventing uninspected oxide wafers from advancing into tungsten plug contact etch.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry drying and irreversible colloidal silica agglomeration forming micro-scratches during post-CMP queue delay before metrology inspection
1. Optical dispersion model mismatch due to CMP-induced mechanical stress/damage layer, yielding systematic thickness measurement offsets > 5 nm
1. Severe edge roll-off / edge exclusion failure (> 5mm zone) skewing WIWNU calculations and masking center-to-edge polish non-uniformity

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-01` | **Automated 49-Point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness and WIWNU Determination** | Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (polarizer-sample-analyzer configuration, spectral range 240-800 nm, 3mm edge exclusion) and NIST-traceable 100nm SiO2/Si calibration standard | 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck of automated spectroscopic ellipsometer. 2. Align wafer notch to 0 degrees and verify auto-focus reflectivity. 3. Execute automated 49-point polar map recipe measuring Psi (ψ) and Delta (Δ) from 240 nm to 800 nm. 4. Fit measured spectra using pre-calibrated SiO2-on-Si Cauchy dispersion model (An=1.457, Bn=0.0035 um^2). 5. Compute mean post-CMP thickness (T_post), Mean Removal Rate: MRR = (T_pre - T_post) / Polish_Time, and 1-sigma Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity: WIWNU (%) = (sigma_thickness / mean_thickness) * 100. | `Target MRR = 250 nm/min ± 25 nm/min (225 - 275 nm/min); 1-sigma WIWNU <= 4.5% across 49-point map; Cauchy regression goodness-of-fit R^2 >= 0.992 across all points.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-02` | **Darkfield Laser Scattering Surface Defectivity and Micro-Scratch Density Metrology** | Automated Darkfield Laser Surface Particle and Defect Scanner (405nm diode laser, 0.15 um PSL sensitivity, 3mm edge exclusion) | 1. Transfer wafer into clean inspection chamber under ISO Class 1 laminar flow. 2. Initialize high-sensitivity darkfield laser raster scan across the entire wafer surface. 3. Classify detected scattering anomalies into micro-scratches, slurry particle agglomerations, and pit defects based on spatial aspect ratio and polarization scattering signature. 4. Generate defect distribution map and compute total defect density per cm^2. | `Total defect density <= 0.15 defects/cm^2 for particles/pits >= 0.18 um; zero line-type micro-scratches exceeding 1.0 um in length across the active die area.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, powder-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields, Antistatic ESD-safe cleanroom coat and footwear, Cleanroom face mask
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Immediately flush eyes with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Wash affected area thoroughly with mild soap and DI water; remove contaminated gloves. Inhalation of particulate: Move victim to fresh ambient air immediately. Seek prompt medical evaluation if irritation persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Operation conducted inside cleanroom bay with mini-environment laminar flow HEPA/ULPA filtration (0.35-0.45 m/s downflow face velocity) and dedicated tool-level exhaust for IPA solvent vapor abatement.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wafers are solid-state dry media. Contaminated IPA stage wipes must be disposed of in designated sealed solvent-waste containers. No direct chemical drain discharge during metrology.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Colloidal Silica (residual slurry dried particulate)** | `7631-86-9` | Semiconductor Grade | `< 0.05% w/w residual surface trace` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW rinse film)** | `7732-18-5` | UPW Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `> 99.999%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (carrier/wipe solvent for stage sanitation)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `70% v/v in DIW` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic post-megasonic-scrubbed, spin-rinse-dried ILD SiO2 surface, free of chemical rinse residue and moisture droplets.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Characterized, defect-mapped, dry dielectric oxide surface ready for subsequent lithography primer coating or post-CMP furnace densification.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption and moisture-induced silica agglomeration nucleation, leading to false defect alarms and permanent particulate bonding that ruins subsequent lithography DoF.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full metrological qualification of post-ILD CMP wafers establishing quantitative baseline for Material Removal Rate (MRR), Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU), and defectivity to confirm Prestonian process stability and tapeout compliance for 180nm DRAM integration.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ild_cmp_mrr_wiwnu_49pt_report.csv`
- [ ] `surface_defect_density_map.tiff`
- [ ] `cmp_metrology_qualification_dof_summary.pdf`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean ILD Oxide Removal Rate (MRR) conforms to targeted Prestonian polish window** | `250 nm/min` | ± 25 nm/min | Automated 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry pre/post polish differential calculation |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) 1-sigma metric across active wafer area** | `3.5%` | <= 4.5% | Statistical standard deviation over mean calculation from 49-point ellipsometry map excluding 3mm edge zone |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Critical post-CMP surface defect density for sizes >= 0.18 um** | `0.08 defects/cm^2` | <= 0.15 defects/cm^2 | Full-wafer darkfield laser scattering surface particle inspection |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All tested wafers demonstrate MRR within 225-275 nm/min, WIWNU <= 4.5%, defect density <= 0.15 defects/cm^2 with zero fatal micro-scratches, and automated verification files deposited in MES artifact storage.

critics.domain_expert: Spectroscopic ellipsometry modeling on polished ILD oxide requires a dual-layer Cauchy or Sellmeier formulation to decouple refractive index shifts caused by mechanical sub-surface damage from actual physical film thickness variation, while 49-point polar mapping is required to accurately capture edge roll-off effects.
critics.supply_chain: Metrology throughput is bounded by automated stage stepping and cassette-to-cassette wafer handling; secondary calibration standards (NIST-traceable thermal oxide calibration wafers) and cleanroom nitrogen purges must have redundant stocking to prevent idle down-time.
critics.laya_pm: Ensure inspection recipes and automated wafer maps are locked into the MES with automated go/no-go interlocks prior to running production-grade split lots, preventing uninspected oxide wafers from advancing into tungsten plug contact etch.
critical_failure_modes: Slurry drying and irreversible colloidal silica agglomeration forming micro-scratches during post-CMP queue delay before metrology inspection
Optical dispersion model mismatch due to CMP-induced mechanical stress/damage layer, yielding systematic thickness measurement offsets > 5 nm
Severe edge roll-off / edge exclusion failure (> 5mm zone) skewing WIWNU calculations and masking center-to-edge polish non-uniformity

testcases.instrumentation: Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (polarizer-sample-analyzer configuration, spectral range 240-800 nm, 3mm edge exclusion) and NIST-traceable 100nm SiO2/Si calibration standard

testcases.procedure: 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck of automated spectroscopic ellipsometer. 2. Align wafer notch to 0 degrees and verify auto-focus reflectivity. 3. # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-CMP-038`
**Title:** Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Multi-Point Pre/Post Oxide Thickness Mapping & Preston MRR Extraction  
**Hierarchy Context:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > CMP of ILD & W-Plugs > ILD Oxide CMP Recipe Optimization and Polish > ILD Oxide CMP Downforce, Platen Speed, and Slurry Flow Recipe Optimization > Prestonian DoE Matrix Execution > Post-CMP Removal Rate (MRR) Extraction, WIWNU Analysis & Surface Defectivity Inspection > Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Multi-Point Pre/Post Oxide Thickness Mapping & Preston MRR Extraction  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

### 1. Process Overview & Objective
This procedure defines the non-destructive multi-point optical metrology sequence for characterizing Inter-Layer Dielectric (ILD) silicon oxide films before and after Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP). Using automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (SE), the procedure measures polarization angle shifts $(\Psi, \Delta)$, fits dispersion models to extract film thickness across radial wafer patterns, and quantifies the Material Removal Rate (MRR) as a function of the Prestonian mechanical-chemical parameters (downforce pressure $P$, platen relative velocity $V$).

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   1. Recipe Setup & Dispersion Modeling     |
       |  Cauchy Model: n(λ) = A + B/λ^2, k(λ) = 0   |
       +---------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   2. Pre-CMP Automated Wafer Mapping        |
       |  49-point polar/concentric grid measurement |
       +---------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   3. CMP Polishing Execution                |
       |  Prestonian DoE parameter run: (P, V, Flow) |
       +---------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   4. Post-CMP Ellipsometry Mapping          |
       |  Identical 49-point grid coordinate measure |
       +---------------------------------------------+
                              |
                              v
       +---------------------------------------------+
       |   5. MRR Extraction & WIWNU Calculation     |
       |  MRR = ΔT / t_polish ; Prestonian k_p fit   |
       +---------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Optical Model Parameterization & Tool Recipe Setup
1. Initialize the spectroscopic ellipsometer light source and spectrometer covering the standard broadband spectral range.
2. Load the transparent dielectric optical model for ILD oxide using the **Cauchy dispersion model**:
   $$\rho = \frac{r_p}{r_s} = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$$
   where $r_p$ and $r_s$ are the complex Fresnel reflection coefficients, parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$ (with $k \approx 0$ across the transparent optical regime).
3. Set the angle of incidence (AOI) to $70.0^\circ$ (near the Brewster angle for $\text{SiO}_2/\text{Si}$).
4. Select the automated **49-point wafer mapping** routine with a 5 mm edge exclusion to capture radial film non-uniformities.

#### Step 2: Pre-CMP Thickness Mapping ($T_{\text{pre}}$)
1. Load the production/DoE wafer onto the vacuum chuck and engage automatic pattern recognition / center alignment.
2. Execute the pre-CMP 49-point measurement scan across the wafer surface.
3. Record the individual point thickness values $T_{\text{pre}}(i)$ (where $i = 1, \dots, 49$), along with the mean thickness $\overline{T}_{\text{pre}}$ and standard deviation $\sigma_{\text{pre}}$. Ensure measurement goodness of fit ($\text{GoF} > 0.98$).

#### Step 3: CMP Polish Process
1. Transfer wafer to the ILD CMP tool.
2. Execute the programmed polishing run according to the designated Prestonian DoE matrix (specifying downforce pressure $P$, relative platen velocity $V$, and slurry flow rate) for a controlled polish time $t_{\text{polish}}$ (measured in minutes).
3. Complete post-CMP megasonic clean, brush scrub, and spin-rinse-dry (SRD) to present a clean, residue-free surface.

#### Step 4: Post-CMP Thickness Mapping ($T_{\text{post}}$)
1. Re-mount the dry wafer onto the spectroscopic ellipsometer chuck with notch-aligned orientation.
2. Run the identical 49-point polar coordinate recipe used in Step 2.
3. Record the post-polish point thicknesses $T_{\text{post}}(i)$, the mean thickness $\overline{T}_{\text{post}}$, and post-polish standard deviation $\sigma_{\text{post}}$.

#### Step 5: Prestonian MRR Extraction and WIWNU Computation
1. Calculate the point-by-point oxide removal $\Delta T(i) = T_{\text{pre}}(i) - T_{\text{post}}(i)$.
2. Calculate the Material Removal Rate (MRR) at each site:
   $$\text{MRR}(i) = \frac{\Delta T(i)}{t_{\text{polish}}} \quad [\text{nm/min}]$$
3. Compute the mean MRR:
   $$\overline{\text{MRR}} = \frac{1}{49} \sum_{i=1}^{49} \text{MRR}(i)$$
4. Compute the Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity ($\text{WIWNU}$):
   $$\text{WIWNU (\%)} = \frac{\sigma_{\Delta T}}{\overline{\Delta T}} \times 100 = \frac{\sqrt{\frac{1}{48}\sum_{i=1}^{49} (\Delta T(i) - \overline{\Delta T})^2}}{\overline{\Delta T}} \times 100$$
5. Extract the Preston coefficient $k_p$ using the Preston equation:
   $$\text{MRR} = k_p \cdot P \cdot V$$
   by plotting $\overline{\text{MRR}}$ against the mechanical product $(P \cdot V)$ across DoE splits.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria

| Metric ID | Parameter Description | Target / Threshold | Unit | Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-MET-01** | Measurement Precision / Gauge Repeatability ($1\sigma$) | $\le \pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry 10-cycle repeat at center site |
| **AC-MET-02** | Ellipsometric Goodness of Fit ($\text{GoF}$) / Model Convergence | $\ge 0.98$ | dimensionless | Cauchy model fitting across polarization angles $(\Psi, \Delta)$ |
| **AC-MET-03** | Wafer Map Sampling Density | $49$ | points/wafer | Automated polar/radial coordinate stage sweep |
| **AC-MET-04** | Post-CMP Within-Wafer Removal Non-Uniformity ($\text{WIWNU}$) | $\le 5.0$ | $\%$ | 49-point delta thickness calculation: $(\sigma / \text{mean}) \times 100$ |

---

### 4. Verified Context & Literature References
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**
  - *Governing Equation:* $\rho = r_p / r_s = \tan(\Psi) \cdot \exp(i\Delta)$ using Fresnel reflection coefficients.
  - *Dispersion Modeling:* Cauchy dispersion model parameterizing refractive index $n(\lambda)$ and extinction coefficient $k(\lambda)$.
  - *Precision Benchmark:* Dry gate oxide / thin films measured with sub-Angstrom precision ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$).
  - *Mapping Routine:* Automated 49-point wafer mapping to track radial film non-uniformity across process runs.
- **Source: SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**
  - Physical placement grid resolution: $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$). Minimum contact hole dimension: $0.17\ \mu\text{m} \times 0.17\ \mu\text{m}$.
- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Integration context: W-plug contacts and stacked capacitor dielectric layers for 180nm cell architecture.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated 49-point polar/radial spectroscopic ellipsometry mapping requires seamless MES telemetry and recipe correlation with the CMP polisher's multi-zone downforce carrier (zones 1 to 5). Optical models must account for backside reflection and edge-exclusion zones (<= 3 mm) to avoid skewed Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) and Preston material removal rate (MRR) extraction drift.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: For 180nm ILD TEOS/PECVD SiO2 films, fitting Psi and Delta across 240-800 nm wavelengths using a parameterized Cauchy dispersion model (An ~ 1.457, Bn ~ 0.0035 um^2) demands constant tracking of surface roughness and post-CMP moisture/slurry micro-residue absorption layers, which artificially inflate extracted oxide thickness and perturb the fitted Mean Squared Error (MSE > 2.0).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Spectroscopic ellipsometer broadband Xe/D2 arc lamps exhibit finite calibrated lifespans (~1000-1500 hours) with spectral drift below 300 nm; secondary source calibration standards (NIST-traceable 100nm thermal SiO2 reference wafers) and automated wafer chuck vacuum seals must have dedicated spares in the local cleanroom inventory to avoid metrology downtime.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Prestonian matrix extraction (MRR = Kp * P * V) dictates pre- and post-measurement turnaround times under 15 minutes per wafer to avoid holding up the chemical mechanical planarization split-lot DoE and causing bottleneck delays in downstream post-CMP brush scrubber cleaning and defect inspection.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry/chemical residue cross-contamination causing multi-wavelength optical model divergence (MSE > 3.5) and false thickness anomalies
1. Wafer edge-roll-off distortion leading to severe mathematical divergence in Preston coefficient (Kp) calculations at r > 97mm
1. Post-CMP queue time violation resulting in atmospheric airborne molecular contamination (AMC) organic deposition and native oxide re-growth

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-1-01` | **49-Point Pre/Post Spectroscopic Ellipsometry Film Thickness Mapping and WIWNU Verification** | Automated Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (240-800 nm Xe source, 70-degree angle of incidence, 3 mm edge exclusion, NIST-calibrated reference stage) | 1. Load wafer onto vacuum chuck and align notch to 0 degrees. 2. Measure pre-CMP oxide thickness across standard concentric 49-point polar coordinate map with 3 mm edge exclusion. 3. Transfer wafer to ILD CMP tool and execute prescribed Preston polishing recipe. 4. Complete post-CMP clean and spin dry. 5. Reload onto ellipsometer and re-map the identical 49 points. 6. Compute site-by-site delta thickness (removal amount) and 1-sigma WIWNU percentage. | `Spectroscopic fit Mean Squared Error (MSE) <= 2.0 across all 49 sites; Post-CMP WIWNU (1-sigma / mean removal) <= 4.5%; Thickness removal within 200 nm ± 15 nm of target.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-1-02` | **Preston Material Removal Rate (MRR) Linear Regression and Kp Extraction** | Calibrated Variable-Angle Spectroscopic Ellipsometer linked to Run-to-Run (R2R) Data Engine; Multi-zone CMP polisher with calibrated pressure transducers and platen tachometer | 1. Extract area-averaged material removal rate (MRR in nm/min) for each wafer split from post-CMP ellipsometry maps. 2. Tabulate product of applied downforce P (psi) and relative platen velocity V (m/s). 3. Perform linear least-squares regression of MRR versus (P * V). 4. Extract slope as Preston constant Kp and calculate coefficient of determination (R^2). | `Preston coefficient of determination R^2 >= 0.985 demonstrating linear Prestonian oxide removal behavior; Preston constant Kp extracted between 4.5e-14 and 7.0e-14 Pa^-1.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloving recommended), UV-absorbing cleanroom safety glasses (optical safety rating EN 166 / ANSI Z87.1 for Xe/UV lamps), Full cleanroom ESD gowning suite with antistatic footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Flush with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes and remove contaminated garments. Eye contact: Flush with saline or sterile eye-wash for 15 minutes. Inhalation: Move subject to clean ambient air immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Class 100 cleanroom lamina flow hood with localized VOC solvent exhaust extraction (> 100 FPM face velocity) for manual IPA chuck wipe-down; enclosed optical casing interlocked for xenon lamp ozone and thermal venting.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes segregated into dedicated sealed, grounded flammable waste receptacles; zero direct aqueous drain disposal of concentrated solvent.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Electronic Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 4 (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water (DIW)** | `7732-18-5` | ASTM Type 1 (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, clean, DIW spin-dried post-CMP oxide surface free of slurry abrasive streaks, micro-scratches, and water marks.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Optically mapped, contamination-free, dry ILD oxide surface, verified ready for post-CMP megasonic clean and defect scanning.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to ambient cleanroom air causes airborne organic molecular contamination and moisture uptake into porous post-CMP TEOS oxide, skewing ellipsometric refractive index fits (n) and producing thickness extraction errors > 3.0 nm.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full wafer spectroscopic ellipsometry 49-point pre/post oxide thickness mapping, WIWNU non-uniformity calculation, and linear Preston MRR extraction across the CMP parameter matrix, establishing baseline process kinetics for 180nm DRAM ILD planarization.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ild_cmp_49pt_thickness_contour_maps.pdf`
- [ ] `preston_mrr_extraction_doe_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `ellipsometry_dispersion_model_fit_residuals.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Spectroscopic ellipsometry optical model goodness-of-fit (Mean Squared Error)** | `1.50` | <= 2.00 | Automated regression fit residual calculation using Levenberg-Marquardt algorithm against Cauchy dispersion model over 240-800 nm spectrum. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Post-CMP Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU 1-sigma)** | `3.8%` | <= 4.5% | Statistical standard deviation over mean removal amount across 49 polar coordinate metrology sites (3 mm edge exclusion). |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Preston model linearity of oxide removal rate vs pressure-velocity product (R^2)** | `0.992` | >= 0.985 | Least-squares linear regression analysis of extracted MRR (nm/min) versus P*V operating points across the DoE wafer set. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 49 wafer sites demonstrate MSE <= 2.0 with zero unmodeled boundary reflections, post-CMP WIWNU confirmed <= 4.5%, and linear Prestonian removal response verified with R^2 >= 0.985 signed off by Metrology and CMP Module leads.

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: Pre-CMP Initial Oxide Film Metrology
1. Mount the 180nm DRAM test vehicle wafer (bearing post-deposition ILD SiO₂ deposited over $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ minimum gate length poly structures) onto the automated vacuum chuck of a broadband spectroscopic ellipsometer (wavelength range $240\,\text{nm} - 800\,\text{nm}$).
2. Execute a standard 49-point polar coordinate map with a boundary edge exclusion of $3.0\,\text{mm}$.
3. Record the initial film thickness matrix $T_{\text{pre}}(r_i, \theta_j)$ (nominal $8500\,\text{\AA} \pm 200\,\text{\AA}$). Verify standard deviation does not exceed baseline deposition limits ($1\sigma \le 1.5\%$).

### Step 2: Prestonian Full-Factorial Polishing Matrix Run
1. Place pad conditioner in in-situ conditioning mode using a diamond grit conditioning disk with $6.0\,\text{lbf}$ downforce.
2. Deliver colloidal silica slurry (acidic/neutral, abrasive size $70-90\,\text{nm}$) at a constant volumetric rate of $150\,\text{mL/min}$ centered onto the IC1000/Suba-IV stacked polyurethane pad.
3. Process test wafers according to the randomized $3 \times 3$ Prestonian DoE parameter space:
   - **Applied Downforce Pressure ($P$):** Set carrier multi-zone membrane heads to $2.0\,\text{psi}$, $3.5\,\text{psi}$, and $5.0\,\text{psi}$.
   - **Relative Linear Velocity ($V$):** Sweep platen/head angular velocity pairs ($40/42\,\text{rpm}$, $75/78\,\text{rpm}$, $110/114\,\text{rpm}$) corresponding to mean relative linear velocities of $0.65\,\text{m/s}$, $1.20\,\text{m/s}$, and $1.85\,\text{m/s}$.
   - **Polish Duration ($\Delta t$):** Polish each wafer for precisely $60.0 \pm 0.1\,\text{seconds}$.
4. Rinse immediately in the integrated cleaner module using deionized water (DIW) and megasonic scrubbing to quench chemical activity, followed by isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor drying.

### Step 3: Post-CMP Metrology & Radial Removal Rate Calculation
1. Reload post-polish wafer onto the spectroscopic ellipsometer using the identical 49-point site index coordinate map.
2. Acquire the residual film thickness distribution matrix $T_{\text{post}}(r_i, \theta_j)$.
3. Compute the site-specific Material Removal Rate ($MRR_{ij}$):
   $$MRR(r_i, \theta_j) = \frac{T_{\text{pre}}(r_i, \theta_j) - T_{\text{post}}(r_i, \theta_j)}{\Delta t} \quad [\text{\AA/min}]$$
4. Aggregate $MRR$ into discrete concentric annular zones: Center ($0 \le r < 35\,\text{mm}$), Mid-Radius ($35 \le r < 70\,\text{mm}$), and Edge ($70 \le r \le 97\,\text{mm}$).

### Step 4: Prestonian Constant Fitting & Non-Uniformity Extraction
1. Plot mean removal rate $MRR$ versus the $P \cdot V$ product ($\text{psi} \cdot \text{m/s}$).
2. Perform ordinary linear regression fitting to extract the empirical Prestonian coefficient $K_p$ and intercept $C_0$:
   $$MRR = K_p \cdot (P \cdot V) + C_0$$
   - Extract slope $K_p$ ($\text{\AA} \cdot \text{min}^{-1} \cdot \text{psi}^{-1} \cdot (\text{m/s})^{-1}$).
   - Verify correlation coefficient $R^2 \ge 0.985$.
3. Compute Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity percent ($WIWNU\%$):
   $$WIWNU\% = \left( \frac{\sigma_{MRR}}{\mu_{MRR}} \right) \times 100\%$$
   Where $\sigma_{MRR}$ is the standard deviation and $\mu_{MRR}$ is the 49-point arithmetic mean of the removal rate.

### Step 5: Recipe Offset Calibration & Profile Correction
1. If $WIWNU\% > 5.0\%$, inspect the radial contour for roll-off edge-fast or center-slow behaviors.
2. Adjust pneumatic multi-zone carrier backpressures:
   - For edge roll-off (edge fast): Decrease zone-3 (outer edge retaining ring zone) backpressure by $-0.2\,\text{psi}$ to $-0.5\,\text{psi}$.
   - For center-slow profile: Increase zone-1 (center diaphragm) backpressure by $+0.3\,\text{psi}$.
3. Repeat validation on monitor wafer until spatial contour deviation stays below threshold limits.

## 4. Context Citations & Technical Alignment

1. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid:**
   - Governs underlying topography constraints for 180nm tapeouts: minimum poly gate length is $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ ($150\,\text{nm}$), minimum poly spacing is $0.21\,\mu\text{m}$, contact hole dimension is $0.17\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.17\,\mu\text{m}$, and manufacturing placement grid is $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$).
   - Maximum allowable overlay error between gate poly and active diffusion is $\le 35\,\text{nm}$. Minimizing CMP oxide thickness variance (WIWNU $\le 5.0\%$) preserves DUV lithography Depth of Focus ($\text{DoF} = k_2 \frac{\lambda}{\text{NA}^2}$) during subsequent contact hole patterning.

2. **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity:**
   - Underpins the electrical criticality of accurate ILD oxide clearing: total contact resistance $R_T = 2 R_c + (R_s/W)d$ and specific contact resistivity $\rho_c = R_c W L_T = R_s L_T^2$. Uniform planarization ensures uniform contact hole etch depth down to the active diffusion pads ($W = 100\,\mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\,\mu\text{m}$), preventing over-etch or unetched residue across pad spacing variations ($d = 5\,\mu\text{m}$ to $80\,\mu\text{m}$).

3. **Three-Zone Quartz Tube Thermal Dynamics and PID Temperature Regulation:**
   - Provides boundary thermal stability conditions ($\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ across central boat region) for pre-CMP densification/anneal of deposited dielectrics prior to mechanical polish, stabilizing baseline chemical removal resistance across the wafer diameter.

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-ILD CMP thickness variations directly eat into the i-line/deep-UV depth-of-focus (DOF >= 0.5 um) budget across the full 200mm wafer. If Prestonian calibration ignores multi-zone carrier pressure distribution or localized pad temperature gradients, modeled non-uniformity fails to capture edge roll-off (ERO) beyond 97mm radius, which downstream leads to critical dimension (CD) variations in dense 180nm DRAM contact/via lithography.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Calibrating the Prestonian constant kp = MRR / (P * V) across 49-point spectroscopic reflectometry maps requires explicit accounting for non-Newtonian shear thinning of colloidal silica slurry and localized thermal flash temperatures. Assuming a purely linear Prestonian response underpredicts removal rate at low pressure (<2.0 psi) and high velocity due to hydroplaning regime transitions, skewing 2D contour fits.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Metrology throughput and consumable pad wear directly gate lot cycle times. Excessive 49-point pre/post measurement iterations on production wafers choke the ellipsometry queue; furthermore, pad glazing drift across consecutive wafer runs invalidates the calibrated kp unless in-situ pad conditioning (diamond disk sweep) profile is tracked as a secondary variable.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Delivery of this work package is a critical gating item for locking ILD1/ILD2 oxide planarization recipes before MPW pilot lot dispatch. The empirical modeling artifact must yield actionable carrier pressure recipe offsets within 48 hours to avoid schedule slippage on the 180nm DRAM metallization stack.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Edge-fast polishing regime caused by improper carrier retaining ring pressure ratio, yielding localized oxide thinning (>40 nm over-polish) that punches through underlying gate topography at edge dies.
1. Prestonian non-linearity due to pad glazing or slurry starvation, causing contour model divergence (>12% residual error) and premature failure of downstream dielectric breakdown (TDDB) tests.
1. Optical dispersion model mismatch in spectroscopic reflectometry (inaccurate Cauchy parameterization of TEOS vs. thermal oxide), producing false thickness delta measurements and bogus WIWNU calculations.

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, minimum 6 mil thickness), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles with side shields, Chemical-resistant neoprene apron during manual slurry handling or bath maintenance, Cleanroom face shield and chemical-resistant sleeve covers during slurry line connection
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin contact: Immediately flush skin with copious volumes of deionized water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE; seek medical evaluation if alkaline irritation persists. In case of eye contact: Forcefully hold eyelids open and irrigate with eyewash station DI water for 20 minutes; transport to emergency ophthalmologist immediately. Inhalation: Move subject to fresh laminar air cleanroom chase or outdoors; administer CPR if breathing ceases.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on CMP polaten enclosures and slurry drum dispense manifolds maintaining negative pressure of >= 0.05 inches water gauge and face velocity >= 100 FPM (0.51 m/s) to vent alkaline aerosol mist.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: CMP effluent contains suspended colloidal silica and alkaline buffer; route all spent rinse and slurry waste directly to dedicated fluoride-free CMP Industrial Waste Neutralization (IWN) station. Coagulate suspended silica using polyaluminum chloride, neutralize pH to 6.5-8.5 using dilute sulfuric acid (H2SO4, CAS 7664-93-9), filter flocculated sludge through filter press before municipal sewer release.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, particulate-free as-deposited PECVD TEOS oxide with pre-CMP defectivity < 0.05 defects/cm^2 (>0.18 um size threshold).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Chemically scrubbed, cleanroom-dry, planarized hydrophilic oxide surface passivated with DI rinse residue < 1 ppb total cations and zero dry slurry agglomerations.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time prior to post-polish brush scrub leads to irreversible slurry drying and chemical crystallization of colloidal silica on the wafer surface, creating catastrophic micro-scratches and permanent killer defects that short subsequent 180nm metal line spaces.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Brightfield Optical & Laser Darkfield Automated Surface Micro-Scratch / Slurry Residue Defectivity Inspection

**Module**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip — Inter-Layer Dielectric (ILD) Oxide CMP Metrology  
**Process Tier**: Gen 3 (nm) / SkyWater SKY130 Commercial MPW Alignment  
**Document Link**: [`docs/sop_post_cmp_defectivity_inspection.md`](./docs/sop_post_cmp_defectivity_inspection.md)

---

### 1. Process Workflow Architecture

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Post-CMP DI Water   │
│   Rinse & Megasonic   │
│         Clean         │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Wafer Alignment &   │
│  5nm Grid Coordinate  │
│     Registration      │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│    Laser Darkfield    │
│   High-Speed Defect   │
│       Scanning        │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Brightfield Optical  │
│    Defect Review &    │
│    Classification     │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      Acceptance       │
│  Verification & Lot   │
│      Disposition      │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre-Inspection Surface Preparation**:
   - Verify post-CMP scrubber cycle completion followed by a thorough deionized (DI) water rinse.
   - Transfer wafer via automated robotic arm onto the vacuum stage in a Class 1/10 mini-environment.

2. **Coordinate Registration on Manufacturing Grid**:
   - Perform optical notch/flat registration followed by die corner fiducial alignment.
   - Lock coordinates to the physical placement manufacturing grid resolution of **$0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$)**.
   - Verify stage positioning error stays within the overlay budget limit ($\le 35\,\text{nm}$).

3. **High-Speed Laser Darkfield Surface Scanning**:
   - Engage darkfield laser illumination (DUV/visible laser) at grazing incidence.
   - Execute spiral/raster scan across the full wafer surface covering automated **49-point wafer mapping** tracks to detect Rayleigh light scatter from slurry aggregates and abrasions.
   - Generate defect polar/Cartesian coordinate maps and scatter intensity histograms.

4. **Automated High-Resolution Brightfield Defect Review**:
   - Direct the automated microscope turret ($NA = 0.65$ or $NA = 0.25$ review optics) with $248\,\text{nm}$ DUV / $365\,\text{nm}$ i-line illumination to coordinate hotspots identified in Step 3.
   - Perform automated pattern subtraction against adjacent reference dies.
   - Classify defects into **Micro-Scratches** (linear abrasions) vs. **Slurry Residues** (particulate binder aggregates).

5. **Defect Sizing & Critical Dimension Filtering**:
   - Measure physical defect widths against Metal 1 minimum width ($0.14\,\mu\text{m}$) and contact hole dimension ($0.17\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.17\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Flag bridging defects exceeding poly gate spacing ($0.21\,\mu\text{m}$).

---

### 3. Critical Metrology Dimensions

```text
Defectivity & Metrology Critical Dimensions (nm)
                    ┌──────────────────────────────────┐
                    │░░░░░░░░                          │
Overlay Registration┤░░░░░░░░                          │
                    │▒▒                                │
 Stage Repeatability┤▒▒                                │
 Micro-Scratch Width┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
                    │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓      │
 Slurry Residue Size┤██████████████████████████████████│
                    │██████████████████████████████████│
                    └┬───────┬────────┬───────┬───────┬┘
                    0.0    42.5     85.0    127.5 170.0 
```

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

1. **Slurry Residue Critical Diameter**:  
   $$\text{Residue Particle Diameter} < 0.17\,\mu\text{m}\ (170\,\text{nm})$$  
   *(Strictly below minimum contact hole dimension $0.17\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.17\,\mu\text{m}$)*.
2. **Micro-Scratch Width & Critical Dimension**:  
   $$\text{Scratch Width} < 0.14\,\mu\text{m}\ (140\,\text{nm}),\quad \text{Scratch Length} < 5.0\,\mu\text{m}$$  
   *(Strictly below Metal 1 minimum width $0.14\,\mu\text{m}$ to prevent interconnect open/bridge defects)*.
3. **Stage Placement & Coordinate Registration Error**:  
   $$\text{Stage Repeatability} \le 0.005\,\mu\text{m}\ (5\,\text{nm}),\quad \text{Defect Overlay Error} \le 35\,\text{nm}$$  
   *(Directly aligned with physical placement grid resolution $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ and overlay error budget $\le 35\,\text{nm}$)*.
4. **Surface Defect Density**:  
   $$\text{Defect Density} < 0.05\,\text{defects/cm}^2$$  
   *(Measured across automated 49-point wafer map)*.

---

### 5. Context Citations
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**: Physical placement grid resolution $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$); minimum poly gate spacing $0.21\,\mu\text{m}$; minimum contact hole dimension $0.17\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.17\,\mu\text{m}$; Metal 1 minimum width $0.14\,\mu\text{m}$; overlay error budget $\le 35\,\text{nm}$; DUV $248\,\text{nm}$ KrF ($NA = 0.65$) & i-line $365\,\text{nm}$.
- **Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology**: Automated 49-point wafer mapping for radial uniformity and defect distribution tracking.
- **Sam Zeloof Z1 Garage Semiconductor Journal (2018)**: Post-process DI water rinse protocol and optical review mechanics.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Automated surface inspection tools using combined brightfield and laser darkfield metrology must interface directly with cleanroom fab automation via SECS/GEM (SEMI E5/E30) protocols. The primary system challenge at the 180nm node is throughput vs. sensitivity: darkfield detection must capture sub-90nm colloidal silica residue and chatter scratches without overwhelming the defect classification pipeline with false positives from underlying grain topography or multi-layer thin-film optical interference.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Post-oxide CMP inspection requires decoupling slurry nanoparticle residue (silica/ceria precipitate, 30-150nm) from mechanical surface defects such as micro-scratches and chatter marks. While laser darkfield metrology (e.g., 488nm or 355nm scanning laser) provides high-speed wafer-scale scatterometry to map point defects and line scratches, polarized UV brightfield confocal imaging must review coordinates to distinguish benign pad debris from catastrophic dielectric gouges that breach the 180nm ILD breakdown voltage ceiling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring production-grade unpatterned and patterned defect inspection tools (e.g., KLA-Tencor Surfscan or Candela series, or refurbished SP1/SP2 platforms) entails lead times exceeding 9 to 12 months with high capital overhead. For the DRAM Foundation open-source 180nm initiative, sourcing refurbished brightfield/darkfield inspection platforms or establishing an equipment co-op lease with local pilot lines is critical to control capex while ensuring optical replacement parts (argon-ion/DPSS lasers, PMT detectors) remain supported.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Defectivity inspection gating directly dictates whether CMP recipe parameters can be qualified for subsequent tungsten plug lithography and etch. Inspection cycle time must stay below 4 minutes per 200mm wafer to prevent lot hold-ups and maintain strict Q-time windows between post-CMP megasonic rinse/dry and subsequent furnace/deposition steps.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry precipitation crystallization: Incomplete megasonic clean allows fumed silica particles (<100nm) to dry onto the ILD oxide, irreversibly binding via siloxane bridges and forming killer bridges for subsequent metal lines.
1. Micro-scratch propagation: Pad debris or conditioning diamond grit creates sub-surface micro-fractures in the PETEOS/BPSG dielectric layer, causing inter-metal leakage and gate oxide short circuits during high-voltage DRAM cell operation.
1. Interference pattern false triggering: Optical phase variance across underlying polysilicon or metal-1 topologies causes darkfield background haze fluctuations, blinding the threshold algorithm to killer residue defects.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-3-01` | **Full-Wafer Laser Darkfield Micro-Scratch and Particle Defectivity Mapping** | Laser Darkfield Surface Inspection System (355nm DPSS UV Laser, multi-channel PMT collectors, automated R-theta scanning stage) | 1. Load wafer onto electrostatic chuck with automated robotic end-effector. 2. Calibrate baseline optics using 100nm NIST-traceable PSL (Polystyrene Latex) sphere reference wafer. 3. Execute full-surface spiral laser scan at 0.15 um sensitivity threshold with 3mm edge exclusion. 4. Run automated defect sorting algorithm to classify defects into point anomalies (particles/slurry) and high-aspect-ratio line clusters (micro-scratches). 5. Generate KLARF map and extract total defect count, defect density (defects/cm²), and scratch count. | `Total defect density must be <= 0.08 defects/cm² at >= 0.15 um size threshold; total micro-scratch count must be <= 2 per 200mm wafer; zero chatter/skid marks > 1 um length permitted across the active area.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-2-3-3-02` | **Automated High-Resolution Brightfield Review and Slurry Residue Classification** | Automated Defect Review Station (High-NA UV/Visible Brightfield Objective 100x/0.90 NA, motorized piezo Z-focus stage, high-resolution CCD/CMOS TDI camera) | 1. Align wafer notch and primary fiducials for automated coordinate transformation. 2. Drive stage sequentially to top 50 defect coordinates identified by laser darkfield scan. 3. Perform automated autofocus and capture high-contrast brightfield images in both normal and differential interference contrast (DIC) modes. 4. Execute image-processing segmentation to measure defect core diameter, depth morphology profile, and optical contrast signature. 5. Classify each defect as colloidal slurry residue, pad polyurethane flake, embedded grit, or dielectric micro-scratch. | `100% of the sampled 50 defect sites reviewed without stage positioning error; slurry residue cluster size must not exceed 0.20 um; zero verified abrasive diamond/pad embedded contaminants detected.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 1 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (double-gloving protocol), Laser Safety Eyewear (OD 6+ rated for 355nm and 488nm wavelengths), Polypropylene cleanroom smock and hood, ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with side shields
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately at emergency eyewash station with deionized water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin with copious amounts of water. Inhalation of organic/cleaning vapors: Move victim to fresh air immediately; seek medical evaluation if respiratory irritation or dizziness persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure maintained under negative static pressure with dedicated cleanroom solvent mini-exhaust (minimum 50 CFM face exhaust velocity); Class 1 laminar flow hood positioned above loader stage.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes and IPA effluent segregated into closed, grounded flammable solvent waste cans; dilute aqueous cleanroom effluent routed to fab acid/base industrial neutralization system (pH target 6.5 - 8.5).

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, semiconductor grade rinse)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier C / VLSI Grade (>99.9%) | `100%` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (residual brush clean trace)** | `1336-21-6` | Electronic Grade (EG) | `<0.5%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, dried PETEOS/BPSG oxide surface directly out of post-CMP PVA brush scrubber and megasonic spin-rinse-dry module, zero visible watermarks.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected, defect-classified, room-temperature dry oxide wafer with zero laser-induced damage, ready for immediate transfer to post-CMP dielectric cap PECVD or contact lithography.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding ambient air queue time causes airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption and ambient particulate electrostatic adhesion that cannot be distinguished from CMP process defectivity, leading to false lot rejection and permanent chemisorption of airborne hydrocarbons.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full-wafer automated brightfield review and laser darkfield defectivity inspection protocol qualifying 180nm ILD oxide post-CMP surface quality, confirming micro-scratch count and residual slurry density meet yield-sustaining standards.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `ILD_CMP_Defectivity_Inspection_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `ILD_CMP_FullWafer_DefectMap_Run01.klarf`
- [ ] `ILD_CMP_HighRes_Defect_Gallery.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-CMP surface killer defect density (size >= 0.15 um) across 200mm wafer active area (3mm edge exclusion)** | `0.06` | +0.02 defects/cm² | Automated UV Laser Darkfield Scatterometry scan with NIST PSL calibrated response |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total detected post-CMP linear micro-scratches per 200mm wafer** | `1` | +1 scratch/wafer | High-NA UV Brightfield automated defect review and optical classification (50-site sampling) |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full wafer scanned with KLARF file successfully logged in fab database, total defect density <= 0.08 defects/cm² at >= 0.15 um, micro-scratch count <= 2, zero embedded pad/diamond particles detected, and formal sign-off by Metrology Lead and Planarization Module Engineer.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and AFM Surface Planarity Characterization

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Post-CMP oxide film non-uniformity directly impacts lithographic focus margin and contact etch stop timing in 180nm DRAM backend integration. Correlation between 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) polar coordinate mapping and AFM micro-roughness must be decoupled from underlying topography variations across dense array vs. sparse periphery cells to avoid erroneous feed-forward recipe compensation to the polisher.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: SE modeling for post-CMP SiO2 on silicon requires fitting with a Sellmeier or Cauchy dispersion relation accounting for a 1-2 nm surface transition/roughness layer modeled via Bruggeman Effective Medium Approximation (BEMA, 50% void + 50% SiO2). Neglecting this overestimates film thickness and distorts refractive index n at 632.8 nm. Concurrently, AFM tapping-mode scans over 20x20 um2 and 5x5 um2 areas must resolve both high-frequency microroughness (Rq < 0.3 nm) and slurry-induced micro-scratch depth without tip-convolution artifacts.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: AFM cantilever probe tips (silicon, tip radius < 10 nm, resonant frequency ~300 kHz) suffer high tip degradation rates on hard dielectric surfaces, necessitating strict lifecycle tracking (<50 scans/tip) and dual-sourcing (e.g., BudgetSensors, Bruker, or Olympus). SE deuterium and halogen source lamps require calibrated operating hour tracking to prevent spectral drift in UV ranges (193-248 nm) which invalidates automated 49-point thickness runs.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Metrology throughput is a major bottleneck: 49-point SE mapping takes ~3 minutes per wafer, but AFM micro-roughness and step-height extraction on 5 target dies takes >35 minutes per wafer. AFM must be throttled to 1 monitor wafer per lot run (or 3-site sampling) to prevent violating downstream dry clean/lithography queue times.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Over-polishing or dishing/erosion undetected by optical SE due to measurement spot averaging (>50 um beam diameter over dense array lines), leading to contact punch-through during plug etch.
1. Organic slurry surfactant residue or drying watermarks creating fictitious optical film thickness offsets (delta shift > 1.5 deg) and AFM tip contamination.
1. AFM tip breakage or wear leading to blunt tip geometry, severely underestimating micro-scratch depth and post-CMP RMS surface roughness (Rq).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-3-01` | **49-Point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry ILD Oxide Thickness and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) Characterization** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 193 nm - 800 nm, micro-spot optics <= 50 um diameter, automated 200mm wafer stage) | 1. Load wafer onto automated ellipsometer stage and align notch to 0 degrees. 2. Acquire polar angle spectra (Psi and Delta) across a standardized 49-point polar coordinate map (5 mm edge exclusion, 7 concentric radii). 3. Fit spectral data using Cauchy dispersion model (An=1.457, Bn=0.0035 um2) layered with a BEMA surface roughness layer over a Si substrate. 4. Extract mean remaining thickness, standard deviation (sigma), and calculate WIWNU% = (Thickness_max - Thickness_min) / (2 * Thickness_mean) * 100. 5. Export thickness contour map and raw parameter files. | `Mean post-CMP ILD oxide thickness = 600.0 nm ± 20.0 nm; Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) <= 3.0%; Optical fit goodness-of-fit parameter (MSE) <= 2.5 across all 49 points.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-1-2-3-02` | **Tapping-Mode AFM Surface Roughness and Micro-Scratch Depth Profilometry** | Atomic Force Microscope (Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, acoustic enclosure, vibration isolation platform, n-type Silicon probe tip radius <= 10 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m, resonant frequency ~300 kHz) | 1. Position stage at 5 specified die locations: Center, North, South, East, West (10 mm from wafer edge). 2. Engage tip on wide-field unpatterned ILD test pad (100x100 um2 minimum area). 3. Acquire 10x10 um2 scan at 0.5 Hz scan rate and 512x512 pixel resolution. 4. Apply 1st order plane fit and flatten to remove sample tilt. 5. Calculate Root Mean Square roughness (Rq) and surface average roughness (Ra). 6. Acquire high-resolution cross-sectional profiles across any observed micro-scratches to measure peak-to-valley depth. | `Root Mean Square roughness (Rq) <= 0.30 nm across all 5 test sites; Ra <= 0.22 nm; Maximum micro-scratch trench depth <= 5.0 nm; Zero micro-scratches with depth > 8.0 nm in a 10x10 um2 window.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom clean-suit (bunny suit), Nitrile gloves (double-gloved, accelerator-free), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV-filtering safety glasses, ESD-safe dissipative footwear
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with residual cleaning solvent/slurry: Flush affected area immediately with cleanroom emergency eyewash/drench shower for a minimum of 15 minutes while removing contaminated PPE. In case of inhalation of solvent vapors, move individual immediately to fresh air outside cleanroom. Seek occupational health triage if irritation persists.

critics.systems_engineer: Post-CMP oxide film non-uniformity directly impacts lithographic focus margin and contact etch stop timing in 180nm DRAM backend integration. Correlation between 49-point spectroscopic ellipsometry (SE) polar coordinate mapping and AFM micro-roughness must be decoupled from underlying topography variations across dense array vs. sparse periphery cells to avoid erroneous feed-forward recipe compensation to the polisher.
critics.domain_expert: SE modeling for post-CMP SiO2 on silicon requires fitting with a Sellmeier or Cauchy dispersion relation accounting for a 1-2 nm surface transition/roughness layer modeled via Bruggeman Effective Medium Approximation (BEMA, 50% void + 50% SiO2). Neglecting this overestimates film thickness and distorts refractive index n at 632.8 nm. Concurrently, AFM tapping-mode scans over 20x20 um2 and 5x5 um2 areas must resolve both high-frequency microroughness (Rq < 0.3 nm) and slurry-induced micro-scratch depth without tip-convolution artifacts.
critics.supply_chain: AFM cantilever probe tips (silicon, tip radius < 10 nm, resonant frequency ~300 kHz) suffer high tip degradation rates on hard dielectric surfaces, necessitating strict lifecycle tracking (<50 scans/tip) and dual-sourcing (e.g., BudgetSensors, Bruker, or Olympus). SE deuterium and halogen source lamps require calibrated operating hour tracking to prevent spectral drift in UV ranges (193-248 nm) which invalidates automated 49-point thickness runs.
critics.laya_pm: Metrology throughput is a major bottleneck: 49-point SE mapping takes ~3 minutes per wafer, but AFM micro-roughness and step-height extraction on 5 target dies takes >35 minutes per wafer. AFM must be throttled to 1 monitor wafer per lot run (or 3-site sampling) to prevent violating downstream dry clean/lithography queue times.
critical_failure_modes: Over-polishing or dishing/erosion undetected by optical SE due to measurement spot averaging (>50 um beam diameter over dense array lines), leading to contact punch-through during plug etch.
Organic slurry surfactant residue or drying watermarks creating fictitious optical film thickness offsets (delta shift > 1.5 deg) and AFM tip contamination.
AFM tip breakage or wear leading to blunt tip geometry, severely underestimating micro-scratch depth and post-CMP RMS surface roughness (Rq).

testcases.title: 49-Point Spectroscopic Ellipsometry ILD Oxide Thickness and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) Characterization
testcases.instrumentation: Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (wavelength range 193 nm - 800 nm, micro-spot optics <= 50 um diameter, automated 200mm wafer stage)
testcases.pre_conditions: 200mm post-ILD CMP monitor wafer cleaned via Megasonic DIW rinse and spin-dried; Q-time from clean < 30 minutes; Stage vacuum > 80 kPa; Ellipsometer baseline calibrated on standard reference Si/SiO2 wafer (NIST traceable 100 nm ± 0.2 nm).
testcases.procedure:
1. Load wafer onto automated ellipsometer stage and align notch to 0 degrees.
2. Acquire polar angle spectra (Psi and Delta) across a standardized 49-point polar coordinate map (5 mm edge exclusion, 7 concentric radii).
3. Fit spectral data using Cauchy dispersion model (An=1.457, Bn=0.0035 um2) layered with a BEMA surface roughness layer over a Si substrate.
4. Extract mean remaining thickness, standard deviation (sigma), and calculate WIWNU% = (Thickness_max - Thickness_min) / (2 * Thickness_mean) * 100.
5. Export thickness contour map and raw parameter files.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Mean post-CMP ILD oxide thickness = 600.0 nm ± 20.0 nm; Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) <= 3.0%; Optical fit goodness-of-fit parameter (MSE) <= 2.5 across all 49 points.

testcases.title: Tapping-Mode AFM Surface Roughness and Micro-Scratch Depth Profilometry
testcases.instrumentation: Atomic Force Microscope (Tapping/Non-Contact Mode, acoustic enclosure, vibration isolation platform, n-type Silicon probe tip radius <= 10 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m, resonant frequency ~300 kHz)
testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer inspected for zero macro-particle contamination; cantilever tuned to free resonance with drive amplitude set to 2.0 V and target amplitude setpoint at 75-80% of free amplitude; AFM tip qualification scan on calibration grating shows tip radius < 12 nm.
testcases.procedure:
1. Position stage at 5 specified die locations: Center, North, South, East, West (10 mm from wafer edge).
2. Engage tip on wide-field unpatterned ILD test pad (100x100 um2 minimum area).
3. Acquire 10x10 um2 scan at 0.5 Hz scan rate and 512x512 pixel resolution.
4. Apply 1st order plane fit and flatten to remove sample tilt.
5. Calculate Root Mean Square roughness (Rq) and surface average roughness (Ra).
6. Acquire high-resolution cross-sectional profiles across any observed micro-scratches to measure peak-to-valley depth.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Root Mean Square roughness (Rq) <= 0.30 nm across all 5 test sites; Ra <= 0.22 nm; Maximum micro-scratch trench depth <= 5.0 nm; Zero micro-scratches with depth > 8.0 nm in a 10x10 um2 window.
