# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Tungsten Slurry Formulations and Pad Conditioning Setup for W-Plug CMP

**Discipline / Context**: Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) [Architecture & Integration] > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation [Foundry Tapeout & PDK] > Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) of Inter-Layer Dielectrics & Tungsten Plugs [Planarization] > Tungsten (W) Plug Overburden CMP and Selective Endpoint Clearing [Planarization] > Tungsten Slurry Formulations and Pad Conditioning Setup for W-Plug CMP [Wet Chemistry]
**Target Generation**: Gen 3 (nm) | **Action Type**: Make

### 1. Equipment & Environmental Pre-Flight
- Verify cleanroom ambient conditions (Class 1000 / Class 100 laminar flow hood, Temp: 21°C ± 1°C, Humidity: 45% ± 5%).
- Inspect facility interlocks (exhaust velocity > 0.5 m/s, DI water loop > 18.0 MΩ·cm).

### 2. Physical Tool Calibration & Fixturing
- Mount substrate onto vacuum chuck stage and align optical/mechanical fiducials.
- Zero calibration instruments and establish baseline noise floor.

### 3. Process Execution & Parameter Validation
- Execute process sequence according to verified recipe parameters: DRC/LVS: 0 Violations, ALD EOT <= 0.8 nm, CMP Dishing < 15 nm.
- Monitor thermal/chemical/optical transients during execution.

### 4. Post-Process Metrology & Quality Acceptance
- Perform physical verification using Automated Batch DRC/LVS & Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / AFM.
- Log 10 consecutive measurement cycles to guarantee process repeatability (Cp/Cpk >= 1.33).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration of acidic alumina/silica-based tungsten slurry with high-downforce (4-6 psi) CMP platen must synchronize closely with optical/motor-current endpoint detection systems. Over-polishing directly induces plug recess and ILD dielectric erosion, degrading contact resistance Rc uniformity across 200mm wafers.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Slurry formulation requires precise oxidizer balance (typically 2-4 wt% H2O2 or Fe(NO3)3 catalyst) at acidic pH (2.0-2.5) to maintain passive WO3 film formation and controlled mechanical abrading. In situ diamond pad conditioning (disk downforce 5-7 lbf) is mandatory to sustain stable pad roughness (Ra ~ 4-6 um) and avoid slurry glazing and micro-scratching on contact arrays.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed acidic tungsten slurries containing oxidizers exhibit shelf-life degradation (<6 months) and agglomeration risks. A point-of-use (POU) dual-component mixing system (slurry base + electronic-grade H2O2) must be qualified with certified domestic/regional vendors to avoid supply halts for the 180nm MPW run.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Procurement lead time for qualified commercial W-slurry and CVD-diamond conditioning disks exceeds 10 weeks. Incoming acceptance lot testing must be executed in parallel with baseline dummy wafer polishes to keep the planarization module on critical-path schedule.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Plug coring and excessive tungsten recess (>35 nm) due to chemical over-etching at contact centers causing open/high-resistance contacts.
1. Pad glazing and abrasive particle agglomeration leading to severe micro-scratching and inter-plug metal bridging across dense active areas.
1. ILD0 oxide erosion and severe oxide loss (>40 nm) resulting from inadequate W:Oxide removal rate selectivity (<30:1).

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-1-01` | **W Removal Rate, Selectivity, and Wafer-Level Non-Uniformity Evaluation** | Four-Point Probe (FPP) Sheet Resistance Meter, Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (Thin-Film Metrology Tool), 200mm Rotary CMP Polisher | 1. Measure baseline pre-polish film thickness across 49-point diameter scan with 3mm edge exclusion using Ellipsometer for TEOS and FPP for W. 2. Mount wafer on CMP head; apply recipe: platen speed 75 rpm, carrier speed 72 rpm, downforce 4.5 psi, slurry flow rate 180 mL/min, in situ diamond conditioning at 6 lbf. 3. Polish for 60 seconds; execute integrated DI water high-pressure rinse and megasonic post-CMP clean. 4. Measure post-polish film thickness across identical 49 points. 5. Calculate removal rate (RR) for W and TEOS, selectivity ratio (RR_W / RR_TEOS), and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU % 1-sigma). | `W Removal Rate >= 2500 A/min; Selectivity W:TEOS >= 35:1; WIWNU <= 4.5% (1-sigma, 3mm edge exclusion).` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-1-02` | **Contact Plug Recess, Array Erosion, and Defectivity Inspection** | High-Resolution Cross-Sectional FE-SEM, High-Resolution In-line Atomic Force Microscope (AFM), Darkfield Optical Defect Inspection Tool | 1. Run automated CMP polish recipe using motor-current endpoint detection plus 10% over-polish margin. 2. Transfer immediately to post-CMP double-sided PVA brush scrubber clean with dilute alkaline chemistry and Marangoni dry. 3. Perform unpatterned/patterned darkfield defect scan across wafer active area (>=0.16 um defect binning). 4. Execute AFM tapping-mode step-height profiling across dense 180nm contact arrays (1:1 pitch) to extract plug recess depth and field oxide erosion. 5. Cross-section target contact structures via Focused Ion Beam (FIB) and image with FE-SEM. | `Tungsten plug recess <= 25 nm; ILD oxide erosion <= 20 nm; Total defect count <= 35 defects/wafer (at >=0.18 um size threshold); Zero macro-scratches.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Acid-resistant chemical aprons and sleeves (Neoprene/Butyl), Heavy-duty nitrile/neoprene chemical gloves over secondary inner nitrile gloves, ANSI Z87.1 full-face shield combined with indirect-vent chemical splash goggles, Closed-toe chemical-resistant boots with non-slip soles
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately flush skin with copious volume of running water for at least 15 minutes while removing contaminated attire; apply soothing cream if minor irritation occurs. Eye contact: Irrigate eye continuously at dedicated eyewash station for minimum 15 minutes holding eyelids open, seek immediate ophthalmic emergency care. Inhalation: Relocate victim to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing becomes labored. Ingestion: Never induce vomiting; rinse mouth with UPW and immediately transport to emergency toxicology center.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on CMP platen enclosures and chemical delivery units (CDU) maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); negative pressure containment preventing acid aerosol escape into cleanroom ballroom.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: CMP effluent containing heavy metal fines (tungsten) and oxidizers must be segregated from general organic waste. Direct to heavy-metal wet acid neutralization facility: treat with sodium bisulfite/metabisulfite to reduce residual peroxides, adjust pH to 7.5-8.5 using calcium hydroxide/NaOH to precipitate tungsten complexes, followed by automated flocculation, ultrafiltration, and sludge dewatering before municipal sewer discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | Electronic Grade (SEMI Tier 3) | `30% aqueous solution (diluted to 2.5-4.0 wt% at POU)` |
| **Ferric Nitrate Nonahydrate (Catalyst in slurry base)** | `7782-61-8` | Electronic / Analytical Reagent Grade | `0.05 - 0.20 wt%` |
| **Colloidal / Fumed Silica (Abrasive)** | `7631-86-9` | Ultra-High Purity Semiconductor Grade | `3.0 - 8.0 wt%` |
| **Nitric Acid (pH adjuster in base slurry)** | `7697-37-2` | SEMI Grade 4 | `< 1.0 wt% (slurry pH 2.0 - 2.4)` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-CMP: CVD W bulk overburden (500-600nm) atop Ti/TiN liner, dry, non-corroded, sealed in FOUP/cassette.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Post-CMP: Planarized contact plugs flush with ILD0 oxide surface, hydrophilic, scrubbed free of slurry abrasive particles, fully dried.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Galvanic corrosion between tungsten plug and Ti/TiN barrier liner driven by residual slurry micro-droplets and moisture exposure; spontaneous atmospheric oxidation generating uncontrolled WO3 growth, leading to contact resistance spikes and contact open fails.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full qualification and signoff of the commercial tungsten CMP slurry and in situ diamond pad conditioning setup, demonstrating stable removal rate, exceptional selectivity over ILD0 oxide, low plug recess, and defect-free contact planarization across 200mm pilot wafers for 180nm DRAM fabrication.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_CMP_Slurry_PadConditioning_Process_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `W_Plug_CMP_RemovalRate_Selectivity_RunData.csv`
- [ ] `TEM_AFM_ContactPlug_Recess_Microscopy.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Blanket Tungsten Removal Rate under nominal recipe conditions** | `2800 A/min` | +/- 250 A/min | 49-point sheet resistance mapping on 200mm monitor wafer via Four-Point Probe |
| `ASSERT-02` | **W to TEOS Oxide Removal Rate Selectivity Ratio** | `42:1` | -7:1 (minimum 35:1) | Ratio of W removal rate (FPP) to TEOS removal rate (Spectroscopic Ellipsometry) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Average 180nm contact plug recess across dense array center and edge** | `18.0 nm` | +/- 6.0 nm | High-resolution In-line Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) step-height line scans |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 3 consecutive 200mm patterned contact wafer CMP runs meeting all ASSERT tolerances, demonstrating average plug recess <= 24nm, oxide erosion <= 20nm, total defect count <= 35 defects/wafer, and zero line-scratch occurrences verified by darkfield inspection.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Multi-Step W Bulk Polish and Selective TiN/Dielectric Endpoint Clearance

**Category**: Planarization | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration of the multi-step W bulk polish and TiN barrier clearance directly bounds the contact resistance (Rc) of bitline contact (BC) and storage node contact (SNC) plugs. Any excessive over-polishing or dishing degrades the plug height, narrowing the process window for subsequent 350 nm Al-Cu M1 bitline lithography and landing pad alignment, while plug recess exceeding 25 nm severely weakens the structural anchor for crown-shaped polysilicon/MIM storage nodes.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: A dual-platen architecture is mandatory to mitigate galvanic corrosion and oxide erosion. Platen 1 must run an acidic ferric-nitrate or iodate-stabilized alumina/silica slurry with high mechanical removal rate (>450 nm/min) for bulk W overburden, while Platen 2 requires an engineered high-selectivity silica slurry (W:TiN:SiO2 selectivity ~ 1:1:50) to clear the ~20 nm PVD Ti/CVD TiN liner. Platen 2 must employ real-time optical reflectance and motor current motor-torque endpoint detection (EPD) to arrest polishing within 5 nm of the TEOS/BPSG dielectric interface.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Proprietary tungsten slurries utilizing fumed ferric/iodine oxidizers face hazardous transport classification, high temperature-instability, and limited domestic availability in Southeast Asia. We must qualify standard colloidal silica-based slurry platforms with secondary peroxide oxidizer (H2O2) injected at the point-of-use (POU) manifold, paired with polyurethane composite polishing pads (e.g., IC1000/Suba-IV stack) to guarantee supply continuity for commercial MPW tapeouts.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Platen transition and post-CMP clean recipe synchronization are critical path bottlenecks. Delays in post-CMP megasonic brush scrubbing exceed queue-time limits and cause irreversible slurry precipitation or tungsten corrosion (corrosion pits), inducing immediate lot-scraping. Process qualification must freeze consumables and endpoint algorithms across all test wafers prior to running scheduled MPW lots.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole exposure and central plug coring/dishing (>30 nm recess) due to aggressive chemical etching during bulk W polish, causing contact resistance spikes (>15 Ohm/plug).
1. TiN liner bridging and residual filament formation along dense 8F^2 bitline cell arrays resulting from premature EPD call, producing bitline-to-substrate or adjacent-contact leakage shorts.
1. Galvanic micro-battery corrosion of W plugs against TiN/Al boundaries in acidic slurry effluent, leading to plug dissolution and unrecoverable open circuits.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-01` | **W-Plug Overburden Clearance and Oxide Erosion Metrology** | Spectroscopic Ellipsometry / Dual-Wavelength Reflectometer & High-Resolution In-Line Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) | 1. Load wafer to Polisher Platen 1; polish bulk W at 4.0 psi downforce, head/platen RPM 80/75, slurry flow 150 mL/min until motor current EPD signals transition to TiN liner (inflection trigger minus 5s). 2. Transfer via wet buffer arm to Platen 2; polish TiN barrier at 2.0 psi downforce with high-selectivity colloidal silica slurry until multi-wavelength optical reflectometer indicates dielectric exposure across center/middle/edge zones. 3. Apply 15% over-polish on Platen 2. 4. Transfer immediately to integrated double-sided PVA brush scrubber with 1.5% NH4OH megasonics. 5. Measure remaining field oxide thickness and AFM plug dishing across 49-point map. | `Total field oxide erosion <= 20 nm across 49 points; W-plug dishing/recess within dense array <= 15 nm; residual Ti/TiN across active array = 0 nm (verified by zero sheet conductivity on adjacent isolation test pads).` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-02` | **Kelvin Bridge Contact Resistance and Dielectric Leakage Verification** | Automated DC Parameter Probe Station with Low-Current Triaxial Matrix | 1. Align 4-point Kelvin bridge probe card onto 180nm W-plug array test structures (100-plug chains and isolated Kelvin structures). 2. Force current I = 100 uA through Kelvin force terminals and measure voltage V across sense terminals. 3. Calculate contact resistance Rc. 4. Force 1.8 V between adjacent plug test comb structures (space = 180 nm) and measure inter-plug leakage current. | `Kelvin contact resistance Rc <= 8.5 Ohm/plug across all measured dies; inter-plug leakage current < 1.0 fA/contact at 1.8 V bias and 25°C.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B chemical splash apron with full arm gauntlets (Butyl/Neoprene), Full-face shield with ANSI Z87.1 certified safety goggles underneath, Heavy-duty chemical-resistant nitrile gloves double-gloved over inner examination gloves, Acid-resistant composite safety boots with metatarsal protection
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact with slurry/H2O2 mix: Immediately flush affected area with copiously running tempered water from emergency safety shower for minimum 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing. For eye exposure: Hold eyelids open and flush at eyewash station for at least 20 minutes; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. If ingested: Do not induce vomiting; administer copious water or milk if conscious; dispatch immediate emergency medical transport.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench and polisher canopy exhaust operating at minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM) connected to central Acid/Corrosive Scrubbed Exhaust (ACX) header; differential pressure interlock set to automatically trigger tool EMO if exhaust drops below 120 Pa vacuum.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated CMP slurry drainage system. Acidic W slurry effluent must be collected in an equalized reaction tank, neutralized with 10% NaOH/Ca(OH)2 to pH 7.0 - 8.5 to precipitate heavy metal hydroxides, followed by automated flocculation, cake filtration, and micro-filtration before secondary industrial effluent discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide (POU Oxidizer)** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure Electronic Grade | `30% aqueous concentrate diluted to 2.0-3.5% at POU` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide (Post-CMP Clean)** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Tier C | `1.0 - 2.5% aqueous solution` |
| **Amorphous Fumed / Colloidal Silica (Slurry Abrasive)** | `7631-86-9` | Electronic Grade | `3.0 - 12.0% wt suspension` |
| **Ferric Nitrate Nonahydrate (Alternative Bulk W Oxidizer)** | `7782-61-8` | Technical/Reagent Grade | `1.0 - 5.0% wt` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited Blanket CVD Tungsten (W) film (~400 nm) over 20 nm PVD Ti/CVD TiN liner with no surface pitting, blistering, or delamination, arriving dry in cleanroom cassette.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, oxide-terminated planar field with fully cleared TiN barrier and isolated W plugs, submerged or wet-buffered with DI water rinse until brush megasonic scrub; final dried state zero-slurry particle residue (<20 defects @ 0.18 um).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the 30-minute air queue time post-CMP prior to PVA scrub causes irreversible drying of colloidal silica nanoparticles and abrasive stains on the dielectric surface, alongside galvanic micro-corrosion pitting of tungsten plug cores, rendering the wafer completely unyieldable.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstrated complete, uniform clearance of bulk tungsten overburden and PVD Ti/CVD TiN barrier liner across 200mm wafers for 180nm DRAM cell arrays. Process achieves selective dielectric stop with controlled field oxide loss, eliminating stringer-induced shorts while preserving contact plug morphology with dishing <= 15 nm and contact resistance <= 8.5 Ohm/plug.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_CMP_PL1_PL2_Endpoint_Trace_Data.csv`
- [ ] `W_Plug_AFM_Dishing_49pt_Metrology_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `High_Res_TEM_CrossSection_W_Plug_Interface.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **W-plug dishing in dense 8F^2 cell array** | `10.0 nm` | +/- 5.0 nm | Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) profilometry across 49 test sites per wafer |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Field dielectric (TEOS/BPSG) erosion during barrier clear** | `15.0 nm` | <= 5.0 nm | Pre/Post Spectroscopic Ellipsometry 49-point wafer mapping |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Single-plug Kelvin contact resistance (Rc)** | `6.8 Ohm` | <= 1.7 Ohm | Automated e-test 4-point Kelvin probe structure measurement on PCM dies |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero conductive residue/stringers observed by inline automated optical defect inspection (>99.5% die yield across test reticles), average plug dishing < 15 nm, field oxide loss < 20 nm, and all Kelvin Rc measurements within specification across three consecutive qualification lots.

# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Removal Rate Bulk Tungsten CMP Recipe Formulation & Pad Conditioning

**Category**: Planarization | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bulk Tungsten (W) CMP removal rate must be balanced with platen thermal dissipation and optical/eddy-current endpoint detection response time. Operating at removal rates exceeding 3500 A/min risks runaway friction heating (>55 deg C platen surface), causing rapid slurry oxidizer breakdown, slurry drying at the wafer edge, and severe non-uniformity across the 200mm platen radius.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Formulation of bulk W slurry requires a ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) or hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) oxidizer complexed with malonic or glycine chelators at pH 2.0 to 2.5 with fumed silica or colloidal alumina abrasives. Pad conditioning requires continuous in-situ diamond disk oscillation to maintain pad asperities and prevent pad glazing without inducing micro-scratches or accelerated pad erosion beyond 15 um/hr.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acidic tungsten slurries using proprietary oxidizers or specialized colloidal silica nanoparticles have strict cold-chain/ambient shipping constraints and shelf-life limits (typically 60-90 days before agglomeration). Diamond conditioner disks (e.g., 3M or Entegris 4-inch sintered CVD diamond) must have a standardized dual-source qualification to prevent fab line stops.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: High-removal bulk polish directly dictates throughput for the 180nm contact and via plug modules; pad lifetime must meet a minimum of 600 wafers per pad to maintain cost per wafer targets without violating maintenance intervention limits for the pilot line.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry oxidizer thermal destabilization causing severe surface pitting, micro-corrosion, and W plug keyhole gouging.
1. Pad glazing from degraded diamond conditioning causing drastic removal rate collapse (>30% drop over 25 wafers) and severe polish non-uniformity.
1. Agglomerated abrasive-induced micro-scratching puncturing the TiN adhesion barrier and underlying TEOS dielectric.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-01` | **Bulk Tungsten Removal Rate and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) Verification** | Four-point probe (4PP) resistivity mapping tool (49-point polar map with 3mm edge exclusion) and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer/XRF | 1. Measure baseline incoming W sheet resistance at 49 map points. 2. Mount wafer on CMP polisher with 4.5 psi downforce, 90 rpm platen speed, 85 rpm carrier speed, and 180 mL/min slurry flow. 3. Execute bulk polish step for exactly 60 seconds with simultaneous in-situ conditioning at 6 lbs downforce. 4. Standard post-CMP double-sided brush scrubber clean with dilute NH4OH/DIW. 5. Post-clean dry and re-measure sheet resistance at identical 49 map points to compute delta thickness. | `Mean bulk tungsten removal rate must be >= 3500 A/min with Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU 1-sigma) <= 4.5% across 49 measurement points.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-02` | **Pad Conditioning Cut Rate and Micro-Scratch Defectivity Evaluation** | Pad profilometer / thickness gauge (micrometer dial/eddy current sensor) and darkfield laser optical wafer inspection tool (e.g., KLA/AIT) | 1. Polish a batch of 25 consecutive W wafers under nominal recipe parameters. 2. Measure pad thickness erosion across 5 radial points post-run to derive pad cut rate. 3. Run a baseline patterned test wafer post-scrub clean through the darkfield inspection system. 4. Classify detected defects using automated defect review SEM. | `Pad cut rate must remain between 12.0 and 18.0 um/hour with stable removal rate drift < 5% across 25 wafers; total micro-scratch count > 0.18 um must be <= 15 defects per 200mm wafer.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Acid-resistant nitrile outer gloves over cleanroom inner gloves, Chemical splash apron (polyethylene/neoprene), ANSI Z87.1 full face shield and safety goggles, Steel-toe cleanroom safety boots with chemical-resistant overshoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately flush with copious amounts of water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated clothing. Eye contact: Rinse eyes at emergency eyewash station with clean water for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open. Inhalation: Move victim to clean air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek immediate medical attention.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on CMP platen enclosure with minimum capture velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s); tool exhaust interlocked with slurry delivery pumps.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate acidic heavy-metal effluent into dedicated Heavy Metal Acid Waste (HMAW) line. Precipitate dissolved iron and tungsten species using lime/coagulant dosing, filter sludge cake, and adjust aqueous supernatant pH to 6.5-8.5 prior to municipal industrial discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Ferric Nitrate Nonahydrate** | `7782-61-8` | Semiconductor / Electronic Grade | `1.0 - 5.0 wt%` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure | `2.0 - 4.0 wt%` |
| **Fumed Silica (Silicon Dioxide)** | `112945-52-5` | Electronic Grade Slurry Suspension | `3.0 - 8.0 wt%` |
| **Nitric Acid** | `7697-37-2` | TraceMetal Grade (pH adjuster) | `< 0.5 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited CVD W overburden (approx. 500nm thickness) with metallic sheen, free of gross organic particles and vacuum oil residues.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Partially polished tungsten surface with residual thickness of 80-120nm remaining prior to barrier clearance step, fully wet or immersed in surfactant rinse tank to prevent slurry particulate baking.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Drying of residual acidic slurry onto unpolished/partially polished tungsten causes irreversible galvanic corrosion, plug pitting, and formation of insoluble tungsten oxide clusters that act as abrasive killer defects in subsequent CMP steps.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Qualified high-removal rate bulk tungsten CMP recipe and pad conditioning protocol delivering >= 3500 A/min removal rate, uniform removal profile, and defect density compliant with 180nm contact module requirements.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `bulk_w_cmp_rate_and_uniformity_matrix.csv`
- [ ] `pad_conditioning_wear_profile_run25.pdf`
- [ ] `post_bulk_cmp_defect_inspection_map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean bulk tungsten removal rate** | `3650 A/min` | +/- 250 A/min | 49-point four-point probe sheet resistance thickness delta conversion |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU 1-sigma)** | `3.8%` | <= 4.5% | Statistical standard deviation over mean of 49-point polar map |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Pad conditioning in-situ cut rate** | `15.0 um/hr` | +/- 2.5 um/hr | Pad thickness step height micrometer measurement across 5 radial points |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 3 consecutive 25-wafer pilot lots meeting all ASSERT criteria with zero slurry-induced corrosion pitting and pad lifetime demonstrated for at least 600 wafers.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Bulk Tungsten Slurry Formulation & High-Removal Rate DOE Parameter Screening

**Category**: Planarization | **Generation**: Gen 3 (180nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bulk tungsten CMP requires precise chemical-mechanical coupling to clear 500-800 nm overburden without inducing high-frequency chatter or motor current spikes. Integrating the 180nm tungsten plug module with downstream ILD-1 oxide planarization necessitates strict platen-to-platen thermal equilibrium and endpoint detection harmonization (motor torque combined with optical reflectance) to avoid catastrophic breakthrough into the underlying 20nm Ti/TiN adhesion liner.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm ground rules, bulk W slurry chemistry must maintain acidic passivation kinetics via an Fe(NO3)3 or H2O2 oxidizer combined with colloidal/fumed silica abrasives (pH 2.0-2.5). The screening DOE must optimize downforce (3.0-5.5 psi) versus platen/carrier velocity to avoid severe tungsten coring, central plug recession exceeding 25 nm, and micro-scratching induced by slurry particle agglomeration.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Specialty acidic W-CMP slurries containing stabilized ferric nitrate or high-purity hydrogen peroxide have limited shelf lives (typically 3-6 months) and face transport delays in the local Southeast Asia supply corridor. Sourcing point-of-use (POU) slurry blending skids and qualified polyurethane hard pads (e.g., IC1000 k-groove) with local domestic stocking is required to mitigate supply disruptions.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Screening DOE iterations across 16 factor combinations will rapidly consume costly 200mm pilot monitor wafers. The project timeline requires condensing the slurry concentration and downforce matrix into a fractional factorial DOE (Resolution IV) to preserve fab line capacity and prevent queue bottlenecks into post-CMP brush scrubbing.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry oxidizer instability leading to iron salt precipitation, slurry gelation, and catastrophic wafer micro-scratching across contact array regions.
1. Excessive mechanical shear or inadequate slurry replenishment causing thermal runaway, pad glazing, and accelerated plug coring (>35 nm recession).
1. Premature liner breakthrough stripping the thin TiN adhesion barrier, leading to tungsten contact plug pull-out and open-circuit DRAM bitline contacts.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-1-01` | **Bulk W Removal Rate and Non-Uniformity Screening via 4-Point Probe Mapping** | Dual-head 200mm CMP Polisher (platen load cell & motor torque monitor), KLA-Tencor / Napson 4-Point Probe ResMap (49-point polar map, 3mm edge exclusion) | 1. Dispense acidic bulk W slurry (2.5 wt% colloidal silica, 3.0 wt% H2O2, pH 2.3) at 180 mL/min onto platen rotating at 75 rpm. 2. Mount wafer onto carrier head rotating at 72 rpm with retaining ring pressure at 5.5 psi. 3. Execute 60-second polish under varying membrane downforce (3.0, 4.0, 5.0 psi) per DOE matrix. 4. Transfer wafer immediately to post-CMP Megasonic DIW dump rinse and Marangoni dry. 5. Measure post-CMP sheet resistance across identical 49-point polar pattern. 6. ### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level C Chemical Apron (Neoprene/Heavy PVC), Full face shield with chemical splash goggles (ANSI Z87.1 approved), Heavyweight butyl/nitrile double-barrier gloves (15 mil inner, 22 mil outer), Chemical-resistant cleanroom safety boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin contact: Immediately strip contaminated PPE and flush skin under deluge safety shower with copious UPW for a minimum of 15 minutes. For eye contact: Flush open eyes at eyewash station for 20 minutes; seek immediate ophthalmologist evaluation. For inhalation of aerosolized acidic mists: Move victim immediately to fresh air, administer 100% medical oxygen if breathing is labored, and obtain prompt emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous acid exhaust ventilation on CMP platen enclosures maintaining face velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); differential pressure interlock ensuring automatic tool shutdown if exhaust drops below 80% nominal static pressure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: CMP effluent collected into dedicated segregated Acid/Slurry Waste line; automated neutralization tank utilizing continuous 20% NaOH dosing with multi-stage cascade pH adjustment (target pH 7.0 - 8.5) and flocculation sedimentation to drop out silica colloids and iron hydroxide sludge before municipal sewer discharge.

| **Iron(III) Nitrate Nonahydrate / Ferric Nitrate** | `7782-61-8` | ACS / Electronic Grade | `1.0 - 5.0 wt%` |
| **Colloidal Silica (SiO2)** | `7631-86-9` | CMP Electronic Slurry Grade | `2.0 - 10.0 wt%` |
| **Nitric Acid (HNO3, pH adjustment)** | `7697-37-2` | SEMI Grade 5 | `0.1 - 1.0 wt%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry, as-deposited CVD tungsten film showing granular micro-crystalline surface morphology without visible atmospheric moisture condensation or peel-back.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, partially oxidized tungsten surface submerged in DIW or transferred wet-to-wet into post-CMP double-sided megasonic/brush scrubber cleaner.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Atmospheric exposure exceeding queue time promotes uncontrolled galvanic corrosion between tungsten and the TiN liner, producing severe micro-pitting, erratic plug loss, and insoluble tungsten oxide (WO3) nodule growth.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful completion and verification of the Bulk Tungsten Slurry Formulation DOE screening demonstrating a high-removal rate regime (>= 350 nm/min) with robust within-wafer uniformity, low plug recession, and zero chemical-mechanical damage to the underlying contact architecture.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

critics.systems_engineer: Bulk tungsten CMP requires precise chemical-mechanical coupling to clear 500-800 nm overburden without inducing high-frequency chatter or motor current spikes. Integrating the 180nm tungsten plug module with downstream ILD-1 oxide planarization necessitates strict platen-to-platen thermal equilibrium and endpoint detection harmonization (motor torque combined with optical reflectance) to avoid catastrophic breakthrough into the underlying 20nm Ti/TiN adhesion liner.
critics.domain_expert: At 180nm ground rules, bulk W slurry chemistry must maintain acidic passivation kinetics via an Fe(NO3)3 or H2O2 oxidizer combined with colloidal/fumed silica abrasives (pH 2.0-2.5). # Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Tungsten Slurry Oxidizer and Abrasive Composition Screening for 180nm DRAM W-Plug CMP

---

### 1. Document Control & Process Context
- **Title**: Tungsten Slurry Oxidizer and Abrasive Composition Screening
- **Generation / Node**: Gen 3 (180nm DRAM CMOS MPW Tapeout)
- **Hierarchy Context**: 
  - DRAM Cell Topology: Crown MIM / Stacked Capacitor Over Bitline (COB) with tungsten contact plugs ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
  - Operation: Multi-Step Bulk Tungsten (W) CMP & Overburden Clearance terminating selectively on TiN / TEOS Inter-Layer Dielectric (ILD).
- **Action Type**: Make / Wet Chemistry Formulation & Screening

```text
│                        │

             │

│                        │

│                        │

│                        │
│   Post-Clean: Brush    │
│     and RCA Clean      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Physical & Chemical Screening Procedure

#### Step 1: Base Ultra-Pure Water Preparation & Chemical Metering
1. Dispense deionized Ultra-Pure Water (UPW) verified at $\ge 18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ resistivity at $22.0 \pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$ into a high-purity fluoropolymer (PTFE/PFA) mixing vessel equipped with continuous recirculation.
2. Maintain bath temperature monitoring and inert nitrogen ($\text{N}_2$) head space to prevent atmospheric $\text{CO}_2$ dissolution.

#### Step 2: Abrasive Colloidal Dispersion & Loading DOE
1. Screen abrasive loading across four target DOE levels: **$1.0\text{ wt\%}$, $2.5\text{ wt\%}$, $4.0\text{ wt\%}$, and $6.0\text{ wt\%}$** of high-purity spherical colloidal silica ($\text{SiO}_2$, primary mean particle diameter $d_{50} = 50 \pm 5\text{ nm}$).
2. Disperse under high-shear overhead mixing at $450\text{ RPM}$ for $30\text{ minutes}$.
3. Verify suspension stability via dynamic light scattering (DLS) to ensure absence of agglomeration ($d_{99} < 120\text{ nm}$).

#### Step 3: Oxidizer Dosing & Stabilization Chemistry
1. Meter semiconductor-grade hydrogen peroxide ($\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, $30\text{ wt\%}$ stock solution) to achieve target active concentrations of **$1.5\text{ wt\%}$, $2.5\text{ wt\%}$, $3.5\text{ wt\%}$, and $5.0\text{ wt\%}$**.
2. Blend an organic corrosion inhibitor and complexing catalyst (malonic acid / ferric nitrate complex) at $0.05\text{ wt\%}$ to passivate recessed tungsten plug interfaces.
3. Dose reagent dropwise at a controlled delivery rate of $\le 50\text{ mL/min}$ while agitating to prevent localized exothermic decomposition.

#### Step 4: Electrokinetic Stabilization & pH Adjustment
1. Adjust slurry working pH to **$2.20 \pm 0.10$** using electronic-grade dilute nitric acid ($\text{HNO}_3$, $10\text{ wt\%}$) or ammonium hydroxide ($\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$, $29\text{ wt\%}$).
2. Measure electrokinetic Zeta potential via electrophoretic light scattering. Maintain Zeta potential $> +30\text{ mV}$ (or $<-30\text{ mV}$) to provide electrostatic double-layer repulsion and prevent slurry sedimentation during polish delivery.

#### Step 5: Point-of-Use (POU) Filtration & Polish Evaluation
1. Route formulated slurry through a dual-stage $0.2\ \mu\text{m}$ polypropylene depth cartridge filter at a loop delivery pressure of $1.8 \pm 0.2\text{ bar}$.
2. Deliver to CMP platen at a slurry flow rate of $150 \pm 10\text{ mL/min}$ on a polyurethane IC1000-type grooved pad with in-situ diamond disk conditioning.
3. Execute bulk W polish on 180nm test wafers with tungsten overburden thickness of $500\text{ nm}$ over $15\text{ nm}$ TiN barrier.

#### Step 6: Post-CMP Wafer Clean & Surface Passivation
1. Immediately transfer polished wafers to double-sided PVA brush scrub stations with dilute megasonic deionized water rinses ($18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$).
2. Complete standard post-metal clean sequence:
   - **RCA-1 (SC-1)**: $5\text{ parts UPW} : 1\text{ part } 29\%\ \text{NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\ \text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ at $70^\circ\text{C}$ to $75^\circ\text{C}$ for $10\text{ minutes}$ (megasonic agitation at $1\text{ MHz}$) to strip slurry particles and micro-residues via electrostatic repulsion.
   - **Cascade Dump Rinse**: 5 cycles with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water until effluent resistivity exceeds $16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - **Final Spin Rinse & Dry**: High-purity filtered $\text{N}_2$ dry.

---

```text
                         │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
Removal Rate (x100 A/min)┤█████████████████████        │
                         │█████████████████████        │
                         └┬──────┬──────┬──────┬──────┬┘
                         0.0   11.2   22.5   33.8  45.0 
```

| Metric # | Parameter | Target Specification | Measurement Method & Instrument |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-01** | Bulk Tungsten Removal Rate ($\text{RR}_\text{W}$) | $\mathbf{\ge 3000\text{ \AA/min}}$ (Nominal $3200 \pm 150\text{ \AA/min}$) | 49-point 4-Point Probe (4PP) Sheet Resistance / Ellipsometry |
| **AC-02** | Selectivity Ratio ($\text{W} : \text{SiO}_2\text{ ILD}$) | $\mathbf{\ge 40 : 1}$ (Nominal $45 : 1$) | Dual pre/post spectral reflectometry of TEOS ILD & W test patterns |
| **AC-03** | Colloidal Suspension Zeta Potential | $\mathbf{|\zeta| \ge 35\text{ mV}}$ (Operating window $+35\text{ mV}$ to $+45\text{ mV}$) | Electrophoretic Light Scattering Analyzer |
| **AC-04** | Post-CMP Total Particle Defectivity ($\ge 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$) | $\mathbf{\le 15\text{ defects/cm}^2}$ | Laser Surface Particle Inspection (Darkfield Defect Scanning) |

---

### 4. Verified Source References
1. **[180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
   - Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Shared bitline contact architecture and tungsten plug (W-plug) connection routing to crown MIM capacitor structures under a strict leakage budget of $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$.
2. **[Standard RCA-1 and RCA-2 Silicon Wafer Cleaning Procedure]**:
   - Deionized water resistivity standard of $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
   - RCA-1 formulation ($5 : 1 : 1\ \text{UPW} : \text{NH}_4\text{OH } 29\% : \text{H}_2\text{O}_2\ 30\%$) at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{--}80^\circ\text{C}$ for organic/particle dissolution.
3. **[RCA Standard Clean SC-1, SC-2, and Native Oxide HF Dip Engineering]**:
   - SC-1 megasonic bath agitation ($1\text{ MHz}$) at $70^\circ\text{C}\text{ to }75^\circ\text{C}$.
   - Sub-micron particle stripping dynamics via Zeta potential repulsion.
   - Cascade dump rinse resistivity specification exceeding $16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ prior to downstream passivation.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Screening bulk tungsten CMP slurry formulations requires maintaining high tungsten removal rate (>3500 A/min) while ensuring an oxidation potential tailored to passivate recessed plug tungsten. If the oxidizer concentration (H2O2 / Fe-catalyst system) drifts, dynamic etch rate will outpace mechanical abrasion, driving severe plug coring and erosion across dense 180nm contact arrays that disrupts downstream Metal-1 lithography depth-of-focus.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm contact pitch, an acidic slurry (pH 2.0 to 2.5) utilizing colloidal or fumed silica (40-70 nm primary particle size) stabilized with ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) catalyst and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) oxidizer is essential. The key chemical mechanism is forming a passivating WO3/WO2 surface film that is mechanically abraded by silica particles. Insufficient oxidizer causes erratic tungsten friction and micro-scratches, whereas excessive oxidizer drives rapid static dissolution and keyhole recess in W-plugs.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Pre-mixed bulk W slurries containing both ferric nitrate and H2O2 suffer from pot-life limitations (<48 hours) due to catalytic self-decomposition of peroxide releasing O2 gas. Procurement strategy must specify a two-part point-of-use (POU) delivery system (Part A: abrasive + iron catalyst stabilizer; Part B: ultra-pure 30% H2O2 oxidizer) sourced with semiconductor-grade Certificate of Analysis to guarantee lot-to-lot pH stability and sub-10 ppb trace metal variance.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Commercial MPW schedules cannot tolerate qualification delays from slurry re-formulation. Slurry procurement screening must execute against off-the-shelf commercial foundry-qualified baseline chemistries with fixed 3-month shelf-life guarantees, verifying plug recess targets (<25 nm) and defectivity densities within a 5-working-day DOE matrix before freezing the baseline CMP recipe.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Peroxide-induced chemical dissolution leading to contact plug keyhole coring and excessive tungsten recess (>35 nm relative to ILD/TEOS).
1. Abrasive particle agglomeration (>0.5 um large particle counts) causing high-density micro-scratching on TEOS dielectric and plug shear defects.
1. Catalytic exotherm and gas pressurization in slurry supply tubing caused by uncontrolled decomposition of H2O2 in the presence of uncomplexed ferric ions.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-1-1-01` | **Tungsten Static Etch Rate (SER) and Open Circuit Potential (OCP) vs Oxidizer Ratio Screening** | Electrochemical workstation with saturated calomel reference electrode (SCE), 4-point probe sheet resistance meter (Prometrix RS-55), and analytical microbalance (0.01 mg resolution). | 1. Immerse clean blanket W coupon into stirred slurry candidate without mechanical abrasion for 15 minutes at 25°C. 2. Continuously record open circuit corrosion potential (OCP) and corrosion current density (Icorr) via Tafel extrapolation. 3. Rinse with UPW, dry with filtered N2, and measure sheet resistance delta across 49 points to determine chemical Static Etch Rate (SER). 4. Calculate ratio of dynamic CMP removal rate to SER. | `Static Etch Rate (SER) must be <= 50 Angstroms/min across all sample runs, corrosion potential Ecorr must stabilize in the passivation regime (between +0.25 V and +0.45 V vs SCE), and Dynamic-to-Static Removal Rate ratio must exceed 70:1.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-1-1-02` | **Slurry Removal Rate (MRR), Selectivity, and Plug Recess on Patterned 180nm W Test Structures** | Rotary CMP Polisher (200mm platform), IC1000/Suba-IV stacked pad, integrated eddy-current/optical endpoint system, KLA-Tencor Surfscan SP2 defect inspection, and Atomic Force Microscope (AFM). | 1. Dispense POU-mixed slurry candidate at 150 mL/min onto platen rotating at 93 RPM, carrier at 87 RPM, downforce 4.0 psi. 2. Polish to endpoint clearing plus 15% overpolish. 3. Execute post-CMP double-sided PVA brush scrub clean with dilute megasonic SC-1 rinse. 4. Measure residual W thickness and calculate bulk removal rate. 5. Perform AFM profiling across dense array (0.28 um pitch) to measure center and edge contact plug recess. 6. Scan SP2 for micro-scratch and particle counts. | `Bulk Tungsten Removal Rate >= 3800 Angstroms/min; W-to-TEOS selectivity >= 40:1; average contact plug recess <= 20 nm with no single plug recess > 28 nm; defectivity density < 0.08 defects/cm2 with zero micro-scratches > 1 um length.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Chemical-resistant nitrile inner gloves with outer heavy neoprene gloves, ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash goggles and full-face shield, Acid/oxidizer-resistant chemical apron and sleeve protectors, Closed-toe steel-toe shoes with chemical-resistant neoprene overboots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin Exposure: Immediately flush with running water for minimum 15 minutes while stripping contaminated clothing; apply skin soothing cream if mild erythema occurs. Eye Exposure: Flush eyes immediately at eyewash station for minimum 20 minutes holding eyelids open, then obtain immediate ophthalmological evaluation. Inhalation: Move victim immediately to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored. Ingestion: Do NOT induce vomiting; rinse mouth thoroughly with water and seek emergency medical treatment immediately.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous local acid-exhaust plenum at slurry dispense station maintaining minimum capture face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s); CMP tool housing connected to dedicated wet acid exhaust with fail-safe differential pressure interlock and automated tool shutdown on exhaust loss.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent slurry effluent containing ferric catalysts and residual H2O2 must flow to a dedicated heavy-metal/fluoride-segregated industrial waste collection tank. Quench residual peroxide with sodium bisulfite (NaHSO3) under monitored ORP control (< +100 mV), followed by alkali precipitation (pH 8.5-9.5 using Ca(OH)2/NaOH) to settle iron hydroxides and colloidal silica coagulant, followed by filter-press dewatering prior to municipal discharge.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `6 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Pre-CMP CVD blanket tungsten with native oxide film (WO3/WO2 < 3 nm) and complete surface Ti/TiN adhesion liner intact without delamination or blister defects.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Fully planarized 180nm contact plugs with clean passivated tungsten surface, cleared TiN overburden, hydrophilic TEOS field oxide, rinsed free of silica slurry particles and residual iron ions.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding Q-time before post-CMP clean causes irreversible drying of sub-micron colloidal silica nanoparticles onto the dielectric and galvanic corrosion between W-plug and TiN liner, creating deep pit coring and irreparable contact resistance failures.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

critics.systems_engineer: Screening bulk tungsten CMP slurry formulations requires maintaining high tungsten removal rate (>3500 A/min) while ensuring an oxidation potential tailored to passivate recessed plug tungsten. If the oxidizer concentration (H2O2 / Fe-catalyst system) drifts, dynamic etch rate will outpace mechanical abrasion, driving severe plug coring and erosion across dense 180nm contact arrays that disrupts downstream Metal-1 lithography depth-of-focus.
critics.domain_expert: At 180nm contact pitch, an acidic slurry (pH 2.0 to 2.5) utilizing colloidal or fumed silica (40-70 nm primary particle size) stabilized with ferric nitrate (Fe(NO3)3) catalyst and hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) oxidizer is essential. The key chemical mechanism is forming a passivating WO3/WO2 surface film that is mechanically abraded by silica particles. Insufficient oxidizer causes erratic tungsten friction and micro-scratches, whereas excessive oxidizer drives rapid static dissolution and keyhole recess in W-plugs.
critics.supply_chain: Pre-mixed bulk W slurries containing both ferric nitrate and H2O2 suffer from pot-life limitations (<48 hours) due to catalytic self-decomposition of peroxide releasing O2 gas. Procurement strategy must specify a two-part point-of-use (POU) delivery system (Part A: abrasive + iron catalyst stabilizer; Part B: ultra-pure 30% H2O2 oxidizer) sourced with semiconductor-grade Certificate of Analysis to guarantee lot-to-lot pH stability and sub-10 ppb trace metal variance.
critics.laya_pm: Commercial MPW schedules cannot tolerate qualification delays from slurry re-formulation. Slurry procurement screening must execute against off-the-shelf commercial foundry-qualified baseline chemistries with fixed 3-month shelf-life guarantees, verifying plug recess targets (<25 nm) and defectivity densities within a 5-working-day DOE matrix before freezing the baseline CMP recipe.
critical_failure_modes: Peroxide-induced chemical dissolution leading to contact plug keyhole coring and excessive tungsten recess (>35 nm relative to ILD/TEOS).
Abrasive particle agglomeration (>0.5 um large particle counts) causing high-density micro-scratching on TEOS dielectric and plug shear defects.
Catalytic exotherm and gas pressurization in slurry supply tubing caused by uncontrolled decomposition of H2O2 in the presence of uncomplexed ferric ions.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Removal Rate Bulk W Polish DOE Factorial Execution
**Module:** Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) & Post-Clean  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Open-Source DRAM, DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Target Unit Cell Contact Geometry:** Access Transistor Channel Length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, Channel Width $W = 220\text{ nm}$  

---

### Process Flow Diagram

```text
             ▼

│                        │
│  Endpoint Trigger at   │

│                        │

│         Screen         │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

#### 1. Wafer Lot Intake & Pre-Metrology Inspection
1. Verify wafer lot originating from Tungsten (W) chemical vapor deposition (CVD) overburden deposition over high-aspect-ratio contact holes targeting access transistor geometries ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
2. Perform incoming 4-point probe / eddy-current metrology across 49 points to measure initial W overburden thickness and sheet resistance uniformity.

#### 2. Platen 1 Setup, Slurry Delivery, & Pad Conditioning
1. Mount a micro-porous polyurethane pad on Platen 1.
2. Initialize diamond disk pad conditioner sweep across the pad radius:
   - **Conditioning Mode:** In-situ conditioning.
   - **Conditioner Downforce:** $6\text{ to }8\text{ lbf}$.
3. Dispense acidic bulk tungsten slurry containing alumina/silica abrasive nanoparticles and ferric nitrate / $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$ oxidizer:
   - **Slurry Dispense Rate:** $180\text{ to }250\text{ mL/min}$.
   - **Slurry Temperature:** $21^\circ\text{C} \pm 2^\circ\text{C}$.

#### 3. Factorial DOE Polish Matrix Execution
Execute a 2-factor, 3-level ($3^2$) or full-factorial screening matrix across pilot test wafers:
- **Factor A (Membrane Downforce):** Screen between low ($3.5\text{ psi}$), medium ($5.0\text{ psi}$), and high ($6.5\text{ psi}$).
- **Factor B (Platen / Carrier Relative Velocity):**
  - Platen rotational speed: $75\text{ to }115\text{ rpm}$.
  - Carrier head rotational speed: $70\text{ to }110\text{ rpm}$.
- **Retaining Ring Pressure:** Set differential offset $+1.5\text{ psi}$ relative to inner membrane pressure to minimize edge-exclusion roll-off.
- **Bulk Removal Target Rate:** Maintain removal rate between $400\text{ and }700\text{ nm/min}$.

#### 4. In-Situ Endpoint Detection (EPD) & Clearing Transition
1. Monitor in-situ motor current traces and optical reflectivity window:
   - Detect the endpoint transition slope when the bulk W overburden clears and the underlying Titanium Nitride (TiN) adhesion barrier is exposed.
2. Trigger the over-polish phase:
   - Set over-polish duration to $10\%\text{ to }15\%$ of the bulk clearing time to clear residual tungsten puddles while preventing plug dishing.

#### 5. Post-CMP RCA SC-1 Megasonic Clean & Cascade Rinse
1. Transfer wafers immediately to the post-CMP wet bench to avoid slurry drying:
   - **SC-1 Bath Chemistry:** $5\text{ parts UPW} : 1\text{ part } 29\%\text{ NH}_4\text{OH} : 1\text{ part } 30\%\text{ H}_2\text{O}_2$.
   - **Bath Temperature:** Maintain at $70^\circ\text{C} \text{ to } 75^\circ\text{C}$ in a quartz or PTFE immersion tank.
   - **Megasonic Agitation:** Apply $1\text{ MHz}$ megasonic power for $10\text{ minutes}$ to lift sub-micron abrasive particles via zeta-potential repulsion.
2. **Cascade Dump Rinse:** Run 5 dump-rinse cycles with $18.2\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ deionized water until effluent bath resistivity reaches $> 16\text{ M}\Omega\cdot\text{cm}$.
3. Spin-rinse dry (SRD) or isopropyl alcohol (IPA) vapor dry wafer surfaces.

1. **Unit Cell Geometry & Plug Integration:**

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Bulk W polish DOE must account for thermal drift across multi-wafer factorial splits; variations in platen temperature alter ferric nitrate or hydrogen peroxide oxidizer kinetics, shifting removal rate (RR) and skewing statistical ANOVA models unless dynamic platen temperature compensation (closed-loop coolant control at 22±1°C) is enforced.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: High-removal rate bulk tungsten CMP relies on aggressive mechanical shear (high downforce >4.0 psi and high slurry flow >180 mL/min) and acidic oxidizer chemistry (pH 2.0-2.5 with Fe(NO3)3 or stabilized H2O2). Executing an unconstrained parameter space risks catastrophic plug coring, keyhole breakout, and micro-scratching via aggregated colloidal silica/alumina particles if pad conditioning downforce and in-situ diamond sweep profiles are not co-optimized.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Acidic high-RR tungsten slurries containing suspended ferric oxidizers have tight shelf-lives (<72 hours post-mixing/stabilization) and lead times exceeding 8 weeks from specialty chemical vendors; executing a full factorial DOE without verified slurry batch consistency and dedicated ex-situ filtration canisters will compromise reproducibility across experimental lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The full factorial matrix consumes substantial dummy/pilot wafer inventory and tool time on the 200mm automated polisher; to adhere to the Gen 3 180nm MPW tapeout budget, screening must utilize a fractional factorial or Box-Behnken response surface design with strict wafer-to-wafer metrology gating before committing full-flow device wafers.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Premature tungsten film peeling or severe micro-scratching induced by slurry particle agglomeration under excessive downforce (>4.5 psi).
1. Over-polishing and catastrophic plug coring resulting in sub-surface keyhole voids in dense DRAM contact/via arrays prior to reaching the TiN barrier interface.
1. Platen run-away exotherm (>45°C) destabilizing oxidizer activation and causing uncontrolled runaway chemical etching over mechanical abrasion.

Extract root-mean-square roughness (Rq) and maximum peak-to-valley height (Rmax). | `Total micro-scratch defect count <= 15 defects/wafer (size >= 0.18 um); total particle defect count <= 50 per 200mm wafer; AFM RMS surface roughness Rq <= 0.8 nm across all 5 measurement sites.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Heavy-duty chemical-resistant butyl rubber gloves over nitrile under-gloves, Full-face polycarbonate shield conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Chemical splash apron and acid-resistant chemical coat, Safety goggles with side shields, Closed-toe ESD-safe chemical safety boots
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with clean eyewash water for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek urgent medical attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing, wash affected area with copious amounts of water and mild soap for at least 15 minutes. Inhalation of acidic mist/fumes: Evacuate to fresh air immediately, administer oxygen if breathing is labored. Ingestion: Rinse mouth thoroughly; do NOT induce vomiting; seek immediate medical toxicology care.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous wet bench and CMP tool dedicated acid scrubbed local exhaust ventilation (LEV) maintaining minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM); static negative pressure duct monitoring with automatic interlock shutoff on exhaust failure.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregate acidic heavy-metal slurry wastewater into dedicated heavy-metal CMP effluent lines; route to internal industrial wastewater treatment for Fe/W precipitation via lime/caustic neutralization (adjusting pH to 8.5-9.5 to precipitate iron hydroxide sludge) followed by secondary flocculation, filter pressing, and clarity testing prior to sewer discharge.

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-deposited blanket CVD Tungsten over TiN/Ti barrier, non-passivated, clean, dry, free of fluoride gas residues (HF/WF6) and particulate debris.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic wet-cleaned tungsten surface with remaining bulk film ~80-120 nm above TiN barrier, submerged or kept wet under DI water cascade until immediate transition to barrier clearing polish step.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Uncontrolled surface oxidation and galvanic corrosion at W/TiN interfaces when exposed to ambient cleanroom humidity, forming erratic tungsten trioxide (WO3) hydrate crusts that cause sudden polish-rate drops, severe micro-pitting, and uncontrolled slurry etching.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful execution of the multi-factor High-Removal Rate Bulk W Polish DOE yielding an optimized response-surface model that establishes downforce, platen speed, and slurry delivery parameters achieving removal rate >= 350 nm/min, WIWNU <= 4.5%, and micro-scratch density <= 15 defects/wafer while preserving remaining bulk film margin prior to barrier clearing.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `bulk_w_doe_factorial_matrix_and_anova_results.csv`
- [ ] `w_removal_rate_and_wiwnu_contour_maps.pdf`
- [ ] `post_bulk_cmp_defect_map_and_afm_topography.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Bulk Tungsten Removal Rate within verified center DOE process window** | `380 nm/min` | +/- 30 nm/min | 49-point polar 4PP sheet resistance thickness differential before and after 60s timed polish |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) across 200mm diameter** | `3.8%` | <= 4.5% maximum | 1-sigma standard deviation over mean across 49 measurement points with 3mm edge exclusion |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Remaining bulk tungsten overburden thickness prior to TiN barrier polish step** | `100 nm` | +/- 20 nm | Dual-wavelength broadband spectroscopic reflectometry / 4PP mapping |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Statistically validated regression model (R-squared >= 0.92) across all DOE split legs with zero wafer breakage, verification of bulk removal rate >= 350 nm/min with WIWNU <= 4.5%, total micro-scratch defects <= 15 per wafer, and formal peer approval of the final DOE report by both the Planarization Domain Lead and Integration Systems Engineer.

critics.systems_engineer: Bulk W polish DOE must account for thermal drift across multi-wafer factorial splits; variations in platen temperature alter ferric nitrate or hydrogen peroxide oxidizer kinetics, shifting removal rate (RR) and skewing statistical ANOVA models unless dynamic platen temperature compensation (closed-loop coolant control at 22±1°C) is enforced.
critics.domain_expert: High-removal rate bulk tungsten CMP relies on aggressive mechanical shear (high downforce >4.0 psi and high slurry flow >180 mL/min) and acidic oxidizer chemistry (pH 2.0-2.5 with Fe(NO3)3 or stabilized H2O2). Executing an unconstrained parameter space risks catastrophic plug coring, keyhole breakout, and micro-scratching via aggregated colloidal silica/alumina particles if pad conditioning downforce and in-situ diamond sweep profiles are not co-optimized.
critics.supply_chain: Acidic high-RR tungsten slurries containing suspended ferric oxidizers have tight shelf-lives (<72 hours post-mixing/stabilization) and lead times exceeding 8 weeks from specialty chemical vendors; executing a full factorial DOE without verified slurry batch consistency and dedicated ex-situ filtration canisters will compromise reproducibility across experimental lots.
critics.laya_pm: The full factorial matrix consumes substantial dummy/pilot wafer inventory and tool time on the 200mm automated polisher; to adhere to the Gen 3 180nm MPW tapeout budget, screening must utilize a fractional factorial or Box-Behnken response surface design with strict wafer-to-wafer metrology gating before committing full-flow device wafers.
critical_failure_modes: Premature tungsten film peeling or severe micro-scratching induced by slurry particle agglomeration under excessive downforce (>4.5 psi).
Over-polishing and catastrophic plug coring resulting in sub-surface keyhole voids in dense DRAM contact/via arrays prior to reaching the TiN barrier interface.
Platen run-away exotherm (>45°C) destabilizing oxidizer activation and causing uncontrolled runaway chemical etching over mechanical abrasion.

2. Execute DOE run matrix varying downforce (2.5 to 4.5 psi, step 0.5 psi), platen speed (60 to 110 rpm), and head speed (55 to 105 rpm) with fixed acidic ferric nitrate/alumina slurry dispense rate at 200 mL/min for 60 seconds per wafer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## W Removal Rate and Surface Defectivity Post-CMP Metrology
**Node / Level**: 180nm CMOS Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3) | **Action Type**: Buy / Incoming Metrology Tool Qualification

---

### Process Workflow
```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Start Post-CMP     │
│       Metrology        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   W Film Thickness /   │
│  Sheet Resistance via  │
│       4PP / XRF        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│   Calculate Removal    │
│      Rate & WIWNU      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Surface Defectivity   │
│  via Darkfield Laser   │
│       Scattering       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     Review Defect      │
│    Classification &    │
│    Plug Coring via     │
│      CD-SEM / AFM      │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Disposition Lot:    │
│  Pass / Rework / Hold  │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Pre/Post-Polish Film Thickness & Sheet Resistance Measurement (Blanket / Monitor Wafers)**:
   - Load pre-CMP and post-CMP 200 mm monitor wafers into an automated 4-Point Probe (4PP) or X-ray Fluorescence (XRF) metrology station.
   - Execute a standard 49-point polar or concentric contour map recipe with a 3 mm edge exclusion.
   - Extract pre-polish thickness $T_{\text{pre}}$ and post-polish thickness $T_{\text{post}}$ derived from sheet resistance $R_s$:
     $$T = \frac{\rho_W}{R_s}$$
   - Calculate bulk Tungsten removal rate ($RR_W$):
     $$RR_W = \frac{T_{\text{pre}} - T_{\text{post}}}{t_{\text{polish}}}\quad [\text{nm/min}]$$
   - Compute Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU %):
     $$\text{WIWNU } (1\sigma) = \frac{\sigma_{T}}{\bar{T}} \times 100\%$$

2. **Full-Wafer Laser Darkfield Defectivity Inspection**:
   - Transfer product wafers to an unpatterned/patterned darkfield laser surface inspection system.
   - Set detection threshold sensitivity to bins: Small ($\ge 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$), Medium ($0.25\text{--}0.50\ \mu\text{m}$), and Large ($> 0.50\ \mu\text{m}$).
   - Scan wafer active area with a 3 mm edge exclusion, generating full-wafer spatial defect signature maps (identifying micro-scratches, slurry residue clusters, and Tungsten peeling/flaking).

3. **Defect Review, Plug Coring & Dishing Metrology**:
   - Route sample wafers to an inline review CD-SEM and Atomic Force Profiler (AFP/AFM).
   - Classify 50 randomized defect coordinates (debris, abrasive silica/alumina residue, and micro-scratches).
   - On memory array active cell regions (transistor channel $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$, sharing Tungsten bitline/drain plug contacts), perform high-resolution AFM line profiling across dense contact arrays:
     - Quantify Tungsten plug coring/erosion depth relative to the adjacent inter-layer dielectric (ILD).
     - Quantify wide-metal line or bond pad dishing ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ contact/pad structures).

4. **In-Line Electrical Contact Verification**:
   - Perform spot four-terminal kelvin checks on Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) test structures (contact pad width $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, pad length $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$, progressively increasing gaps $d = 5, 10, 20, 40, 80\ \mu\text{m}$) to confirm specific contact resistivity ($\rho_c$) has not degraded due to over-polish or under-clearing.

---

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                        Metrology Target Metrics        
                ┌──────────────────────────────────────┐
                │░░░                                   │
    Dishing (nm)┤░░░                                   │
                │▒▒▒                                   │
Defects (cnt/wf)┤▒▒▒                                   │
       WIWNU (%)┤▓                                     │
                │▓                                     │
   W RR (nm/min)┤██████████████████████████████████████│
                │██████████████████████████████████████│
                └┬────────┬─────────┬────────┬────────┬┘
                 0       105       210      315     420 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Control Limit | Unit | Measurement Tool |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Bulk W Removal Rate ($RR_W$)** | $\ge 400$ | $380 \le RR_W \le 480$ | nm/min | 4PP / XRF Thickness Mapping |
| **Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU, $1\sigma$)** | $\le 5.0$ | $\le 6.5$ | % | 49-point Polar 4PP Map |
| **Total Surface Defect Density ($\ge 0.18\ \mu\text{m}$)** | $\le 30$ | $\le 50$ | defects/wafer (200 mm) | Darkfield Laser Scattering Inspection |
| **W Plug Coring / Array Dishing Depth** | $\le 20$ | $\le 25$ | nm | In-line AFM Profilometry / CD-SEM |

---

### Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Access transistor channel dimensions: length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Bitline contact shared between adjacent memory cells via Tungsten plug (W-plug) connecting to stacked capacitor structures.
- **Transmission Line Measurement (TLM) for Specific Contact Resistivity**:
  - Test structure geometry: $W = 100\ \mu\text{m}$, $L_{\text{pad}} = 50\ \mu\text{m}$, gaps $d \in \{5, 10, 20, 40, 80\}\ \mu\text{m}$.
  - Resistance regression: $R_T = 2 R_c + (R_s / W) \cdot d$ to confirm interface integrity post-CMP.
- **Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging**:
  - Bonding pad dimensions: $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ metallization pads evaluated for erosion and dishing during overburden clearance.

---

*Captured in knowledge base:* [`docs/knowledge/w_cmp_metrology.md`](./docs/knowledge/w_cmp_metrology.md)

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Metrology throughput must match the 180nm pilot line cycle time: 49-point wafer mapping via 4-point probe sheet resistance (Rs) converted to tungsten thickness (assuming bulk resistivity of 5.3-5.6 uOhm-cm) alongside darkfield laser scattering surface defect inspection creates a metrology bottleneck if not integrated into an automated FOUP-to-FOUP macro recipe. Furthermore, optical dielectric thickness tools like spectroscopic ellipsometry must be cross-calibrated on oxide stop layers to deconvolve plug dishing and dielectric erosion from actual film thickness changes across die pitch variations.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Tungsten CMP post-clean verification requires differentiating between chemical micro-corrosion (galvanic pitting induced by oxidizer residue like Fe(NO3)3 or H2O2 in low pH slurry) and mechanical defectivity (chatter marks, micro-scratches from agglomerated alumina or silica abrasives >0.5 um). Evaluating bulk W removal rate strictly via Rs measurement requires blanket monitor wafers with pre-CMP baseline mapping; for patterned DRAM wafers, optical reflectometry/ellipsometry on surrounding TEOS oxide combined with atomic force microscopy (AFM) for plug dishing (<35 nm) and array erosion (<40 nm) is mandatory.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source vulnerability on calibration standards for darkfield defect inspection (polystyrene latex PSL sphere calibration wafers) and tungsten four-point probe NIST-traceable resistivity standard wafers. Lead times for replacement cantilever tips used in automated in-line AFM profiling and high-purity IPA/megasonic cleaning chemistries for post-CMP PVA brush scrubbers must be secured to avoid lot holding.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Phase-gate milestone Gen3-CMP-M4 requires characterization of 15 monitor wafers across a 3-level slurry oxidizer/downforce DOE within 3 business days. Prolonged post-CMP queue times without automated metrology dispatch will cause water mark defects and surface passivation oxide growth, skewing resistivity measurements and triggering false out-of-spec yield alarms.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Slurry oxidizer residue-induced galvanic pitting and tungsten plug corrosion leading to open contacts or elevated TLM contact resistance (>1.0e-7 Ohm-cm2).
1. Agglomerated abrasive-induced micro-scratching puncturing the TiN liner and damaging the underlying inter-layer dielectric (ILD), resulting in inter-metal shorting.
1. Excessive plug dishing (>45 nm) or array erosion causing non-planar topography that degrades subsequent contact lithography depth of focus and induces metal line necking.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-1-3-01` | **W Bulk Removal Rate and Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) Sheet Resistance Mapping** | Automated 4-Point Probe Resistivity Mapping Tool (e.g., KLA-Tencor RS-100) and Spectroscopic Ellipsometer (J.A. Woollam M-2000) | 1. Perform pre-CMP 49-point Rs map and compute baseline thickness using calibrated tungsten resistivity of 5.4 uOhm-cm. 2. Process wafer through bulk CMP recipe for exactly 60 seconds with target downforce (4.0 psi) and platen speed (90 rpm). 3. Perform post-CMP brush scrub clean and spin rinse dry (SRD). 4. Measure post-CMP 49-point Rs map within 15 minutes of SRD. 5. Measure remaining TEOS oxide thickness at 9 scribe-line test pads via Spectroscopic Ellipsometry (fitting Cauchy model across 250-800 nm). 6. Compute removal rate (RR = Delta_T / time) and 1-sigma Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU % = (sigma / mean_RR) * 100). | `W Bulk Removal Rate >= 350 nm/min; Within-Wafer Non-Uniformity (WIWNU) <= 4.5% (1-sigma); TEOS dielectric loss on field oxide <= 15 nm.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-2-1-1-3-02` | **Post-CMP Surface Defectivity and Micro-Scratch Classification via Darkfield Laser Scattering** | Unpatterned/Patterned Darkfield Laser Surface Defect Inspection System (e.g., KLA Surfscan SP2 / 2800) and In-line Review SEM/AFM | 1. Load wafer into darkfield inspection system using standard edge-handling vacuum chuck. 2. Scan entire 200mm wafer surface with 3mm edge exclusion at 0.15 um sensitivity threshold. 3. Generate wafer defect map classifying particles, micro-scratches, slurry residues, and water marks. 4. Navigate automated review SEM/AFM to top 30 defect locations; capture high-resolution images and quantify tungsten plug dishing in dense contact array (pitch 360 nm, diameter 180 nm). 5. Calculate total defect density (defects/cm2) and maximum dishing depth. | `Total defect density (>= 0.15 um size) <= 0.08 defects/cm2; Total micro-scratches per wafer <= 5; Maximum tungsten plug dishing in dense array <= 35 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom chemical splash apron, Heavy-duty nitrile/neoprene outer gloves over standard cleanroom nitrile gloves, Full-face polycarbonate shield with indirect-vent safety goggles, Acid/vapor chemical-resistant safety overshoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact: Immediately flush affected area with copiously flowing water for minimum 15 minutes while stripping contaminated apparel; apply soothing sterile dressing. Eye contact: Irrigate eye at eyewash station for 15+ minutes holding eyelids wide open; transfer immediately to emergency ophthalmic care. Inhalation: Relocate individual to fresh clean air zone; provide mechanical oxygen if labored breathing occurs; seek immediate medical assessment.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous acid/corrosive gas scrubbing exhaust on chemical delivery unit and CMP polish table (face velocity >= 0.5 m/s or 100 fpm at all shroud openings); VOC solvent exhaust enclosure for IPA dry module; real-time toxic gas monitoring for NOx and ammonia vapors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: CMP effluent contains heavy metal W species, iron catalyst, and colloidal silica/alumina: Route via dedicated CMP waste drain into an automated coagulation/flocculation neutralization tank. Adjust pH to 8.5-9.0 using Ca(OH)2 to precipitate metals and coagulate abrasives; filter via filter press prior to secondary biological/industrial waste discharge.

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI Grade 5 | `1.0% v/v post-CMP rinse` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `99.9% v/v for vapor dryer` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly polished tungsten/TiN overburden, hydrophilic surface saturated with deionized water rinse barrier to prevent slurry drying and abrasive caking.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: PVA brush scrubbed, megasonic rinsed, IPA vapor dried; completely particulate-free, hydrophobic to mildly hydrophilic passivated oxide/W surface with zero liquid residues.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes spontaneous evaporation of water film, forming irreversible crystalline slurry abrasive ring marks, ferric oxidizer staining, and galvanic micro-corrosion pitting of tungsten plugs.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified post-CMP metrology baseline for 180nm DRAM tungsten plug CMP establishing bulk removal rate >350 nm/min, WIWNU <4.5%, surface defect density <0.08 defects/cm2, and contact dishing <35 nm without galvanic corrosion pits.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:

| `ASSERT-02` | **Total surface defectivity density (size >= 0.15 um) post-brush scrub** | `0.05 defects/cm2` | <= 0.08 defects/cm2 | Full-wafer darkfield laser scattering surface inspection with 3mm edge exclusion |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Tungsten plug dishing in dense 180nm DRAM contact array (pitch 360 nm)** | `25 nm` | +/- 10 nm | High-resolution in-line Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) cross-pitch profile scan |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
