# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Deconvoluted Step-Height Extraction and ILD Dishing Profilometry Analysis
**Module:** Metrology / Post-CMP Planarization Characterization  
**Node Generation:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3)  
**Process Step:** Post-W CMP Overburden Clearing & ILD Polish Analysis  

---

### Metrology Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   AFM Calibration &    │
│     Cantilever Tip     │
│       Profiling        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   High-Density Grid    │
│  Scanning over W-Plug  │
│         & ILD          │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│       Tip-Shape        │
│  Morphological Blind   │
│    Reconstruction &    │
│     Deconvolution      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Quantitative      │
│      Step-Height       │
│    Extraction: Plug    │
│     Recess vs ILD      │
│        Dishing         │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Statistical Process   │
│  Control & Metrology   │
│     Pass/Fail Gate     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step SOP Procedure

1. **AFM Tip & Metrology Station Qualification:**
   - Mount a high-aspect-ratio (HAR) diamond-like carbon (DLC) silicon cantilever tip (tip apex nominal radius $R \le 5\text{ nm}$, cone half-angle $< 10^\circ$).
   - Run piezo-stage Z-height and XY linearization calibration using certified silicon pitch standards aligned to the 180nm cell dimensions (bitline/wordline pitch = $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$; access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Verify instrument Z-height baseline noise floor achieves sub-Angstrom precision ($< \pm 0.05\text{ nm}$).

2. **Automated Wafer Alignment & Multi-Point Inspection:**
   - Load post-CMP 180nm DRAM wafer with cleared tungsten overburden.
   - Execute an automated 49-point wafer mapping routine to track radial within-wafer non-uniformity (WIWNU) across center, mid-radius, and edge die sites.
   - Align the probe head to dense DRAM memory array test blocks containing contact vias/W-plugs shared between adjacent memory cells and adjacent isolated field oxide/ILD regions.

3. **High-Resolution Tapping-Mode Topography Scanning:**
   - Set scan field size to $5\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 5\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ across the dense array cell matrix and $20\text{ }\mu\text{m} \times 20\text{ }\mu\text{m}$ across array-to-periphery boundary regions.
   - Configure raster resolution to $1024 \times 1024$ lines with scan speed $\le 0.5\text{ Hz}$ in non-destructive tapping/intermittent contact mode to eliminate tip shearing and lateral force deformation.

4. **Tip-Convolution Correction & Morphological Erosion:**
   - Image a certified characterization tip-check spike sample to execute Blind Tip Reconstruction (Villarrubia morphological deconvolution).
   - Apply morphological dilation/erosion filtering on acquired raw AFM profiles to remove tip-sidewall artifacts at the steep vertical transitions of contact plug openings ($L = 180\text{ nm}$).

5. **Step-Height & Dishing Extraction:**
   - Establish planar reference planes from adjacent undeformed ILD field oxide regions.
   - Extract **W-Plug Recess** ($\Delta Z_{\text{plug}}$) by calculating the height delta between the nominal ILD surface plane and the bottom nadir of the tungsten contact plug.
   - Extract **ILD Dishing** ($\Delta Z_{\text{dishing}}$) across wide dielectric spaces and dense array pitches ($360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$) relative to periphery stopping layers.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
                   ┌───────────────────────────────────┐
                   │░░░░░░░░                           │
   Dry Ox Ref (EOT)┤░░░░░░░░                           │
                   │▒                                  │
    AFM Z Precision┤▒                                  │
ILD Dishing (Array)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
                   │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
      W-Plug Recess┤█████████████████████████████      │
                   │█████████████████████████████      │
                   └┬────────┬───────┬────────┬───────┬┘
                   0.0      4.5     9.0     13.5   18.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Nominal Target | Upper / Lower Control Limit (UCL / LCL) | Exact Physical Units | Metrology Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **W-Plug Recess ($\Delta Z_{\text{plug}}$)** | $15.0$ | $\le 25.0$ (Max allowable recess before contact open) | $\text{nm}$ | Deconvoluted AFM step-height extraction |
| **Dense Array ILD Dishing ($\Delta Z_{\text{dishing}}$)** | $12.0$ | $\le 18.0$ (Total oxide loss / dishing limit) | $\text{nm}$ | Cross-sectional AFM step-height profilometry |
| **Metrology Z-Height Precision** | $\pm 0.05$ | $\le \pm 0.05$ | $\text{nm}$ | AFM standard noise qualification |
| **Wafer Sampling Inspection Density** | $49$ | $49$ (Full radial pattern) | points/wafer | Automated optical/AFM wafer-mapping stage |

---

### 3. Context & Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, defining the physical aperture dimensions for bitline and drain contact W-plugs erected below the crown/MIM capacitor.
- **Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology:**
  - Standard baseline metrology precision targets of sub-Angstrom level ($\pm 0.05\text{ nm}$) and automated 49-point wafer mapping protocol tracking radial film uniformity across fabrication runs.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - Array pitch constraints of $360\text{ nm}$ to $400\text{ nm}$ bitline and wordline pitch, governing the critical scan window and spatial frequency for deconvolving plug recess vs ILD dishing.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: AFM cantilever tip-shape convolution induces non-negligible dilation artifacts along high-aspect 180nm contact hole sidewalls, artificially broadening perceived recess width and distorting the trench bottom topography. The step-height algorithm must incorporate blind tip estimation (Villarrubia model) using characterizer gratings before applying profile deconvolution, otherwise ILD dishing depth and plug recess values will diverge from in-line optical ellipsometry cross-checks and TEM cross-sections.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm lithography ground rules, contact plug diameter ranges from 220nm to 260nm. Measuring a 15-35nm tungsten recess requires high-aspect-ratio (HAR) diamond-like carbon or tilt-compensated silicon cantilevers with tip radius < 5nm and half-cone angle < 10°. Standard tapping mode risks tip apex chipping on dense array edges; peak-force tapping or non-contact true non-contact AFM mode with cantilever amplitude feedback calibration is strictly required to prevent scratching planarized SiO2 ILD.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-crystal silicon HAR AFM probes with sub-5nm tip radii have high lead times (>8 weeks) and fragile lifespans (<30 scans in contact/tapping regime before tip blunting exceeds calibration threshold). A robust secondary source of high-frequency diamond-coated or rotated etched silicon probes must be qualified, and tip wear monitors must run automated tip qualification protocols every 10 site measurements.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: AFM is inherently throughput-limited (3-5 minutes per site). Scanning 49 wafer mapping points per wafer post-W-CMP will create a severe fab queue bottleneck. Metrology sampling must be restricted to a standardized 9-point radial map coupled with spectroscopic reflectometry/ellipsometry screening, reserving full 3D AFM dishing deconvolution for pilot lots, qualifying wafers, and out-of-spec excursions.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. AFM tip apex fracturing/blunting during scanning across dense W-plug arrays causing severe underestimation of plug recess depth by up to 60%.
1. Piezo scanner Z-axis non-linearity and thermal drift during long raster scans yielding false concave tilt misinterpreted as ILD field oxide dishing.
1. Organic residue or slurry nanoparticle contamination trapped in plug recesses creating false step-height peaks and masking genuine contact over-polishing.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-1-3-3-01` | **Quantitative Deconvoluted Step-Height Extraction of 180nm Dense Contact W-Plug Recess** | Atomic Force Microscope (Bruker Dimension Icon or equivalent) equipped with High-Aspect-Ratio Silicon AFM Cantilever (tip radius < 5 nm, spring constant ~40 N/m, resonant frequency ~300 kHz), acoustic isolation enclosure, and integrated blind tip deconvolution software. | 1. Load wafer and navigate automated stage to dense memory array test structure (240nm contact diameter, 500nm pitch) across standard 9-point radial layout. 2. Engage cantilever in PeakForce Tapping mode with setpoint force < 1.0 nN and scan rate 0.5 Hz over a 2.0 um x 2.0 um scan window (512x512 pixels). 3. Acquire raw Z-sensor height topography and peak force error channels. 4. Execute automated 1st-order flattening on surrounding planar ILD baseline to correct scan tilt. 5. Apply blind tip deconvolution algorithm using the daily tip characterization kernel. 6. Extract average step height from planarized ILD plateau to bottom of 20 representative tungsten plugs within the frame using ISO 5436-1 step-height calculation protocol. | `Average W-plug recess step-height must be 20.0 nm <= h_recess <= 35.0 nm across all 9 measurement sites. Within-die recess 1-sigma standard deviation must be <= 3.0 nm. Any tip-convolution artifact reporting unresolvable plug bottom (>10% bottom curvature distortion) constitutes a re-scan failure.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-1-3-3-02` | **Wide-Field ILD Oxide Dishing and Array Erosion Profilometry Analysis** | Atomic Force Microscope with large-area automated XY closed-loop stage and calibrated 100um piezo scanner, coupled with calibrated spectroscopic reflectometer for field oxide reference thickness. | 1. Align wafer coordinates to dedicated CMP dishing and erosion macrostructures (100 um x 100 um dense array adjacent to 100 um open oxide field). 2. Set scan area to 80 um x 10 um line profile perpendicular to the pattern boundary at 0.25 Hz. 3. Collect height profile across open ILD, pattern boundary transition, and dense array field. 4. Fit reference plane to the open field ILD baseline 20 um away from pattern edge. 5. Calculate maximum oxide dishing depth (Delta Z_max) in open spaces and cumulative array erosion (Delta Z_erosion) in dense contact fields. | `Maximum ILD field dishing must be <= 15.0 nm. Maximum dense array oxide erosion must be <= 25.0 nm across all measured test sites. Profile curvature goodness-of-fit R^2 relative to parabolic dishing model must be >= 0.95.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 nitrile gloves (double-gloving required), ANSI Z87.1 certified chemical splash safety goggles, Full cleanroom bunny suit with integrated hood and ESD boots, Class 1 laser safety protective eyewear when aligning AFM laser beam
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin exposure to IPA, flush immediately with copious clean water for at least 15 minutes and remove contaminated garments. In case of eye contact, flush eyes at emergency eye-wash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open. For accidental laser reflection into eye, seek immediate medical ophthalmology evaluation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: AFM acoustic/vibration chamber must maintain continuous clean dry air (CDA) or N2 purge at 2-5 SCFM with low-velocity laminar exhaust. Local solvent wipe stations must operate under certified chemical exhaust hood with minimum face velocity of 100 FPM (0.51 m/s).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: IPA contaminated cleanroom wipes and swabs must be segregated into dedicated sealed, grounded, fire-rated flammables bins for hazardous solvent waste disposal. Rinse effluents must drain directly to industrial solvent recovery or VOC stripping waste lines.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic / Semiconductor Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Deionized Water** | `7732-18-5` | Ultra-pure (18.2 MOhm-cm) | `100.0%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-W-CMP brush-scrubbed, megasonic rinsed, IPA vapor dried, free of slurry particulate and chemical watermarks.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Metrology complete, defect-free, surface verified dry and un-scratched, ready for pre-metal dielectric cap deposition (PE-CVD SiN/TEOS).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air queue time causes native oxide growth on exposed tungsten plug tips (>1.5nm WO3) and atmospheric organic hydrocarbon adsorption, shifting AFM tip contact mechanics, degrading subsequent contact resistance (Rc) by >20%, and causing adhesion failure of barrier/capping layers.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Quantitative multi-site AFM profilometry analysis yielding deconvoluted W-plug recess depth and ILD oxide dishing/erosion topography across 180nm DRAM test structures, fully validating W-CMP clearing selectivity and planarization compliance.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_Plug_Recess_Dishing_Profilometry_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Deconvoluted_AFM_Height_Maps_9Point.tiff`
- [ ] `Step_Height_Extraction_Raw_Dataset.csv`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Mean tungsten plug recess depth in 180nm dense contact arrays conforms to design specification.** | `25.0 nm` | ± 5.0 nm | Blind-tip deconvoluted AFM step-height analysis averaged across 9 radial wafer sites (20 plugs per site). |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Maximum ILD field oxide dishing across isolated test structures remains within acceptable planarity bounds.** | `12.0 nm` | + 3.0 nm / - 5.0 nm | Calibrated 80um long-range AFM cross-sectional profiling verified against spectroscopic ellipsometry field oxide remaining thickness. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **AFM tip radius stability throughout wafer measurement run maintains measurement fidelity.** | `4.5 nm` | <= 7.0 nm post-run maximum | Pre-run and post-run blind tip reconstruction using certified silicon tip characterization standard grid. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Complete delivery of signed metrology report and CSV data demonstrating W-plug recess (20-30nm), ILD dishing <= 15nm, tip radius qualification passing post-run threshold, and zero mechanical scratch damage verified on all inspected test dice.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Laser Scattering & Darkfield Optical Inspection for Tungsten Residue Detection

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-W-DF-180-01`  
**Process Level:** Context: 180nm Open-Source DRAM Chip (DRAM Foundation VN) > 180nm CMOS Commercial MPW Tapeout & PDK Implementation > Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) of Inter-Layer Dielectrics & Tungsten Plugs > Tungsten (W) Plug Overburden CMP and Selective Endpoint Clearing > Post-CMP Plug Recess Profilometry and Residual Metal Defect Metrology > Laser Scattering & Darkfield Optical Inspection for Tungsten Residue Detection  
**Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm Node)  
**Action Type:** Make  

---

## 1. Principle & Objectives
Following Chemical Mechanical Planarization (CMP) of the tungsten (W) overburden used for contact plugs (channel width $W = 220\text{ nm}$, gate length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, stacked capacitor over bitline / COB architecture), residual metallic tungsten can bridge adjacent plug contacts or cause bitline shorts. 

This procedure utilizes high-speed darkfield laser scattering to inspect the dielectric surface across the wafer. By suppressing specular reflection from planarized dielectric films and collecting non-specular Rayleigh and Mie scattered light, metallic tungsten flecks, micro-bridging lines, and CMP slurry/flake residuals are detected, mapped, and classified prior to dielectric cap deposition and capacitor formation.

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

```
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| [Step 1: Calibration & Recipe]  --> Calibrate darkfield laser & set optical map |
|                                                                                |
| [Step 2: Wafer Alignment]       --> Load wafer & align to notch / die grid     |
|                                                                                |
| [Step 3: Darkfield Scan]        --> Spiral/XY scan & collect laser scattering  |
|                                                                                |
| [Step 4: Mapping & Review]      --> Generate 49-point map & flag W defects     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

### Step 1: Tool Setup & Optical Channel Calibration
1. Initialize the automated darkfield laser inspection system. Select the narrow/wide-angle darkfield collector configuration.
2. Load calibration standards to verify signal sensitivity:
   - Verify detector baseline noise floor across clean oxide/nitride surfaces ($t_{\text{ox}} = 3.5\text{ nm}$ gate oxide equivalent or ILD oxide benchmark).
   - Set the polarization angle and optical filtering to reject regular orthogonal pattern scatter from the 180nm access transistor cell array (pitch based on $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$).

### Step 2: Wafer Handling and Precision Chucking
1. Transfer the post-CMP cleaned and dried 200mm wafer onto the vacuum inspection chuck.
2. Perform automated optical pre-alignment using the wafer notch and align array coordinates to the reticle layout.
3. Establish edge-exclusion zone ($3.0\text{ mm}$ edge bevel exclusion) to eliminate edge-bead and boundary edge-proximity artifacts.

### Step 3: Laser Scattering & Darkfield Scanning Execution
1. Scan the wafer using synchronized stage translation and laser illumination:
   - Ensure the grazing-incidence laser beam illuminates the surface while specular reflection enters the beam dump.
   - Channel scattered photons into darkfield photomultiplier tube (PMT) / CCD detector arrays.
2. Continuously subtract periodic background pattern scatter via die-to-die (cell-to-cell) digital thresholding tailored to the $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ folded bitline layout.
3. Record high-intensity scatter spikes corresponding to anomalous metallic tungsten residue, unpolished metal flakes, and scratches.

### Step 4: Wafer Mapping & Defect Binning
1. Aggregate detected scattering signals into an automated wafer map tracking radial non-uniformity across 49 inspection points (or full-die continuous scan).
2. Bin defects into:
   - **Tungsten Micro-Residue / Flakes** (high scattering cross-section, localized).
   - **CMP Scratches / Chattering** (linear scattering track).
   - **Slurry Residue** (low-intensity diffuse scatter).
3. Export coordinate defect file (KLARF/XML) for subsequent defect review.

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

| Metric | Target Value | Engineering Units | Metrology Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Minimum Residual Tungsten Defect Capture Size** | $\le 180$ | $\text{nm}$ (spatial critical dimension) | Darkfield Laser Scattering Metrology |
| **Post-CMP Tungsten Residue Defect Density** | $< 0.05$ | $\text{defects/cm}^2$ | Full-wafer darkfield optical scan |
| **Wafer Non-Uniformity Map Sampling Grid** | $\ge 49$ | $\text{points}$ | Automated radial wafer mapping |
| **Inspection Edge Bevel Exclusion** | $\le 3.0$ | $\text{mm}$ | Automated stage edge masking |

---

## 4. Source Citations

- **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**:
  - Cell layout parameters ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$ access transistor geometry, $8F^2$ / $6F^2$ folded bitline structure, and tungsten plug contact integration for stacked capacitor over bitline).
- **[Source: Spectroscopic Ellipsometry and Reflectometry for Dielectric Film Metrology]**:
  - Thin film dielectric baseline modeling, gate oxide calibration references ($3.5\text{ nm}$ precision metric), and automated 49-point wafer mapping methodology tracking radial non-uniformity.
- **[Source: Four-Point Collinear Probe Metrology for Semiconductor Sheet Resistance]**:
  - Edge proximity correction factor boundaries and geometric constraints governing wafer defect mapping and conductivity verification.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration of laser scattering and darkfield inspection post-W CMP requires seamless SECS/GEM interface handshakes with the fab automation host to prevent lot stalling. The primary systems challenge is separating optical pattern scatter noise generated by underlying dense DRAM cell arrays (wordline/bitline topography) from actual sub-micron residual tungsten flakes, requiring high dynamic range PMT/CCD sensor thresholding and die-to-die subtraction algorithms.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node DRAM contact/via plug pitch, tungsten stringers and micro-scratches filled with residual W slurry or redeposited metal present severe bridging risks between adjacent storage node contacts. Normal-incidence and oblique-angle darkfield laser scattering (typically 355nm or 488nm laser illumination) must be tuned with polarized spatial spatial filters (Fourier filtering) to suppress periodic diffraction patterns from the memory array while capturing anomalous rayleigh/mie scattering from non-periodic tungsten flakes down to 60nm size.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring a dedicated automated darkfield inspection tool (e.g., KLA-Tencor SP/AIT series or equivalent refurbished Gen 3 toolset) introduces long lead times (32-40 weeks) and substantial CAPEX. Sourcing calibration standards (NIST-traceable polystyrene latex PSL spheres on bare silicon and specialized tungsten CMP defect qualification wafer standards) must be locked in immediately to prevent commissioning delays for the DRAM Foundation VN tapeout.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Tool qualification and recipe synthesis must align strictly with the Gen 3 DRAM baseline sprint. Any prolonged recipe optimization (>3 weeks) for nuisance filtering in the dense array will stall the W-CMP clearing loop and downstream Inter-Metal Dielectric (IMD1) deposition, burning precious wafer budget and jeopardizing the MPW delivery milestone.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Severe pattern noise overload causing nuisance defect saturation (>50,000 counts/wafer), blinding the darkfield detector to genuine sub-100nm killer tungsten bridge defects.
1. Optical haze misinterpretation caused by residual post-CMP surfactant/slurry water marks (slurry burn) being erroneously flagged as residual tungsten film.
1. Laser-induced thermal damage or photolytic oxidation on polished plug surfaces during high-power ultraviolet laser dwell times.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-2-01` | **Darkfield Laser Scattering Sensitivity and Defect Detection Verification** | Automated Darkfield Optical/Laser Wafer Inspection System (355nm Solid-State UV Laser, Multi-channel PMT collectors), NIST-traceable 80nm PSL Calibration Wafer, Automated Review SEM | 1. Load calibration wafer with known 80nm PSL defects and execute 100% surface scan to verify optical scattering sensitivity and coordinate accuracy (<= 0.5 um). 2. Load post-W CMP production wafer with programmed contact plug arrays. 3. Engage die-to-die polarization filter (P-polarization illumination, S-polarization collection) and optical spatial Fourier filter to null periodic DRAM array scattering. 4. Run full-wafer scan with 0.18 um pixel resolution. 5. Export defect pareto, coordinate map, and classify residual tungsten anomalies. 6. Perform automated review SEM sampling on top 50 optical defect coordinates. | `Capture rate of >= 95% for tungsten residues >= 80nm; false alarm/nuisance defect rate <= 5% in dense array regions; zero detected unpolished W overburden patches > 1 um^2 across all active dies.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-2-02` | **Post-CMP Tungsten Residue Bridge Identification and Die-to-Die Repeatability** | Darkfield Laser Defect Inspection System, In-line Defect Review SEM with Energy Dispersive X-ray Spectroscopy (EDS) | 1. Perform consecutive dynamic scans (3 iterations) on the same post-CMP wafer with unload/reload cycles to measure defect coordinate repeatability. 2. Identify repeating defect coordinates located across active cell boundary regions. 3. Transfer defect map coordinates directly to in-line Review SEM/EDS. 4. Collect secondary electron images and acquire EDS spot spectra at 5 keV beam energy on 30 flagged scattering sites to confirm tungsten (M-alpha line at 1.77 keV) versus silica/alumina slurry particles or dielectric divots. | `Coordinate relocation repeatability >= 98% across 3 scans; SEM/EDS confirmation of tungsten residue bridges <= 0 defect/cm^2 on functional cell array; residual slurry nanoparticle count < 10 defects per 200mm wafer.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 4 Laser safety goggles rated for 355nm and 532nm (Optical Density OD >= 7+), Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), Electrostatic discharge (ESD) certified cleanroom coverall suit, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield (during calibration liquid handling)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye exposure to scattered laser beam: Immediately isolate beam, apply sterile eye patch, and transport victim to certified ophthalmologist immediately. Inhalation or skin contact with IPA: Flush skin with copius amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes; move individual to fresh cleanroom air; seek medical attention if irritation or respiratory distress persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Tool enclosure maintained under interlocked Class 1 laminar downward airflow with dedicated Class 4 laser safety enclosure interlocks; chemical load/unload area coupled to dedicated fab solvent exhaust duct pulling minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent IPA lint-free wipes and effluent collected in dedicated solvent carboys, labeled as flammable hazardous waste, and routed to an off-site certified hazardous incinerator; aqueous PSL rinse residue routed to local chemical industrial wastewater neutralization plant.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) Cleanroom Grade** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Tier C / Ultra-Pure Electronic Grade (VLSI) | `99.9%` |
| **Polystyrene Latex (PSL) Suspension Calibration Solution** | `9003-53-6` | Analytical Standard in Deionized Water | `0.1% w/v` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Hydrophilic, de-slurried, megasonic-cleaned, and IPA-vapor dried oxide/tungsten planarized surface free of moisture pools and slurry stains.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Particle-mapped, non-destructive laser-scanned, dry planar surface ready for immediate vacuum transfer into PVD/CVD Inter-Metal Dielectric (IMD1) chamber.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure Q-time causes ambient atmospheric moisture condensation and galvanic corrosion between the tungsten plug and surrounding titanium/titanium nitride liner, causing plug recess etching, severe tungsten oxide (WOx) bloom, and irreversible killer particle formation.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full optical darkfield qualification and automated defect classification recipe established for 180nm DRAM post-tungsten CMP clearing, reliably detecting residual tungsten bridges down to 80nm with robust periodic array pattern noise suppression and zero thermal laser damage.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `W_CMP_Darkfield_Defect_Pareto_Map.csv`
- [ ] `SEM_EDS_Tungsten_Residue_Review_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer_Haze_and_Scattering_Intensity_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Tungsten residue defect capture rate for particle/stringer sizes >= 80nm** | `95.0` | +5.0% / -2.0% | Automated Review SEM inspection of 100 blind seeded coordinates per test wafer |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Nuisance and false defect rate over high-density DRAM array blocks** | `3.0` | +2.0% / -1.5% | Die-to-die darkfield subtraction noise tally across 20 unpatterned and patterned fields |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Total residual tungsten stringer killer defect density across active die area** | `0.0` | +0.02 defects/cm^2 | In-line EDS composition confirmation at 5 keV beam energy across all flagged bridging coordinates |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful execution of 5 consecutive post-W CMP production qualification lots demonstrating < 0.02 defects/cm^2 residual tungsten bridges, zero tool hardware interlock trip events, and 100% data export compliance to fab yield management system.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Cross-Sectional In-Line CD-SEM & EDS Defect Review Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In-line cross-sectional CD-SEM and EDS review provides indispensable nanoscale grounding for the post-W CMP clearing module, bridging top-down defect inspection with physical root-cause analysis. However, beam-induced carbon contamination and local electrostatic charging on exposed inter-layer dielectric (ILD SiO2) surfaces can distort critical dimension (CD) measurements by up to 8 nm and attenuate low-energy characteristic X-ray lines (e.g., C-Kalpha, N-Kalpha). Beam deceleration mode (V_acc <= 1.0 keV) and low-probe current (< 30 pA) must be strictly integrated with dual-EDS silicon drift detector (SDD) geometry to ensure high spatial resolution without causing structural collapse or dielectric puncture into underlying access transistor gates.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm DRAM node, the cell contact plug aspect ratio exceeds 3.5:1 with nominal CD around 220 nm. The primary physical risk after overburden polishing is under-clearing of residual Ti/TiN barrier films or micro-bridging of tungsten ribbons across dense bitline contact arrays, leading to catastrophic inter-bitline short circuits. Cross-sectional EDS linescans must reliably differentiate between native surface oxidation (WOx) and conductive titanium-tungsten residue down to a 5 nm threshold. Furthermore, sample preparation via in-line dual-beam FIB must use low-energy Ga+ final polishing (2-5 kV) or Ar+ milling to prevent amorphous damage layers and Ga implantation artifacts that artificially elevate background EDS noise.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-source dependency on advanced field-emission CD-SEM and FIB-EDS platforms introduces acute throughput bottlenecks in open-source MPW tapeout runs, where automated defect review (ADR) sampling rates must be rationed (< 25 sites per wafer) to avoid stalling lot progression. Consumables including Ga liquid metal ion sources (LMIS), FEG electron emitter cartridges, and aperture strips have extended lead times exceeding 16 weeks. Establishing correlation models between high-throughput top-down dark-field optical scatterometry and cross-sectional SEM reviews is critical to reduce physical cross-section demand on production lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Defect review metrology directly governs the go/no-go gate for releasing post-CMP wafers to Stacked Capacitor (COB) or Bitline metallization modules. High defect false-alarm rates or delayed cross-sectional classification inflate cycle time by 18-36 hours per lot. Implementing automated recipe-driven fiducial alignment, rapid sub-surface defect re-detection, and standardized Defect Classification (ADC) code generation ensures that unmitigated CMP scratch or slurry agglomerate issues are flagged within a strict 2-hour feedback loop to CMP tool engineers.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron beam charging and Ga+ ion beam over-etching causing artificial erosion of the W-plug recess profile, generating false-positive recess out-of-spec readings.
1. Unresolved Ti/TiN residual barrier stringers along dielectric micro-scratches resulting in unmapped leakage paths between adjacent cell nodes (leakage > 1 fA/cell).
1. Slurry nanoparticle entrapment (fumed silica or colloidal alumina) at the plug-dielectric boundary obscured by beam-induced carbon deposition, preventing accurate EDS identification of foreign material.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-01` | **Cross-Sectional In-Line CD-SEM Measurement of Contact Plug Recess and Top-CD** | Dual-Beam In-line FIB-SEM (Focused Ion Beam / Cold-FEG In-line CD-SEM with sub-nanometer immersion lens) calibrated against NIST SRM 2800 nanometer magnification standard. | 1. Load wafer into vacuum chamber (P < 5e-5 Pa) and align using global die fiducials. 2. Navigate automatically to 15 pre-selected contact plug defect and reference coordinate sites across center, middle, and edge dies. 3. Deposit a 1.0 um protective carbon/Pt capping layer via in-situ gas injection system (GIS). 4. Mill cross-sectional trench using Ga+ FIB at 30 kV (beam current: 300 pA rough cut, 30 pA fine polish, finishing at 2 kV / 10 pA to suppress amorphization). 5. Acquire high-resolution secondary electron (SE) cross-section images at 800 V landing energy, 25 pA probe current, 150 kX magnification, working distance 3.0 mm. 6. Execute automated edge-detection algorithm to extract top CD, bottom CD, sidewall angle, and plug recess depth relative to adjacent ILD planar baseline. | `W-plug top CD must measure 220 nm +/- 15 nm; plug recess depth relative to ILD planar field must be between 10.0 nm and 30.0 nm across all 15 sites; sidewall taper angle must be >= 88.0 degrees; zero visible seam void opening > 10 nm.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-02` | **Nanoscale In-Line EDS Elemental Mapping and Line-Scan Profile of Inter-Plug Bridging Defects** | Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscope integrated with Windowless Silicon Drift Detector (SDD) Energy Dispersive X-Ray Spectrometer (energy resolution <= 126 eV for Mn-Kalpha). | 1. Set electron beam accelerating voltage to 5.0 kV (sufficient to excite W-Malpha at 1.774 keV, Ti-Kalpha at 4.510 keV, Si-Kalpha at 1.739 keV, and O-Kalpha at 0.525 keV, while minimizing interaction volume < 80 nm). 2. critics.systems_engineer: In-line cross-sectional CD-SEM and EDS review provides indispensable nanoscale grounding for the post-W CMP clearing module, bridging top-down defect inspection with physical root-cause analysis. However, beam-induced carbon contamination and local electrostatic charging on exposed inter-layer dielectric (ILD SiO2) surfaces can distort critical dimension (CD) measurements by up to 8 nm and attenuate low-energy characteristic X-ray lines (e.g., C-Kalpha, N-Kalpha). Beam deceleration mode (V_acc <= 1.0 keV) and low-probe current (< 30 pA) must be strictly integrated with dual-EDS silicon drift detector (SDD) geometry to ensure high spatial resolution without causing structural collapse or dielectric puncture into underlying access transistor gates.
critics.domain_expert: At the 180nm DRAM node, the cell contact plug aspect ratio exceeds 3.5:1 with nominal CD around 220 nm. The primary physical risk after overburden polishing is under-clearing of residual Ti/TiN barrier films or micro-bridging of tungsten ribbons across dense bitline contact arrays, leading to catastrophic inter-bitline short circuits. Cross-sectional EDS linescans must reliably differentiate between native surface oxidation (WOx) and conductive titanium-tungsten residue down to a 5 nm threshold. Furthermore, sample preparation via in-line dual-beam FIB must use low-energy Ga+ final polishing (2-5 kV) or Ar+ milling to prevent amorphous damage layers and Ga implantation artifacts that artificially elevate background EDS noise.
critics.supply_chain: Single-source dependency on advanced field-emission CD-SEM and FIB-EDS platforms introduces acute throughput bottlenecks in open-source MPW tapeout runs, where automated defect review (ADR) sampling rates must be rationed (< 25 sites per wafer) to avoid stalling lot progression. Consumables including Ga liquid metal ion sources (LMIS), FEG electron emitter cartridges, and aperture strips have extended lead times exceeding 16 weeks. Establishing correlation models between high-throughput top-down dark-field optical scatterometry and cross-sectional SEM reviews is critical to reduce physical cross-section demand on production lots.
critics.laya_pm: Defect review metrology directly governs the go/no-go gate for releasing post-CMP wafers to Stacked Capacitor (COB) or Bitline metallization modules. High defect false-alarm rates or delayed cross-sectional classification inflate cycle time by 18-36 hours per lot. Implementing automated recipe-driven fiducial alignment, rapid sub-surface defect re-detection, and standardized Defect Classification (ADC) code generation ensures that unmitigated CMP scratch or slurry agglomerate issues are flagged within a strict 2-hour feedback loop to CMP tool engineers.
critical_failure_modes: Electron beam charging and Ga+ ion beam over-etching causing artificial erosion of the W-plug recess profile, generating false-positive recess out-of-spec readings.
Unresolved Ti/TiN residual barrier stringers along dielectric micro-scratches resulting in unmapped leakage paths between adjacent cell nodes (leakage > 1 fA/cell).

Slurry nanoparticle entrapment (fumed silica or colloidal alumina) at the plug-dielectric boundary obscured by beam-induced carbon deposition, preventing accurate EDS identification of foreign material.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Dual-Beam FIB Site Preparation & Precision Cross-Section Milling

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-beam FIB (Focused Ion Beam) site preparation for 180nm tungsten (W) contact/via plug cross-sections introduces thermal and mechanical stress, ion implantation artifacts, and local charge accumulation on dielectric layers (SiO2/BPSG). The integration challenge is achieving mill-stop accuracy within ±10nm of the contact center without inducing curtaining artifacts across high-aspect-ratio (AR ~4:1) tungsten plugs embedded in relatively soft oxide matrices. A dual-cap protective layer strategy (electron-beam assisted Pt/C deposition followed by high-current Ga+ ion-beam Pt/C deposition) must be rigidly implemented to prevent top-surface erosion and preserve the original post-CMP recess profile.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm node dimensions, tungsten plugs typically have diameters between 200nm and 240nm. Milling with a high-current Ga+ FIB beam (e.g., 30kV, 300pA to 1nA) across dissimilar materials (W plug density 19.25 g/cm3 vs SiO2 density 2.2 g/cm3) causes severe differential sputter rates, producing vertical striations (curtaining). Final cross-sectional polishing must step down progressively from 30kV/50pA to 5kV/15pA, ending with a low-kV (2kV, 10-20pA) polish to remove the amorphous Ga-damaged layer (<5nm) and accurately reveal plug recess, Ti/TiN barrier adhesion, and voiding without smearing tungsten across the ILD interface.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Precursor sources for in-situ gas injection systems (GIS)—specifically Trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum [(CH3)3Pt(CpCH3)] for protective capping and Xenon Difluoride (XeF2) or Iodine (I2) for enhanced selective milling—face export controls and single-vendor vulnerabilities. Ga liquid metal ion sources (LMIS) require routine 1,500-2,000 hour emitter replacements with lead times exceeding 12 weeks. Cryo-pumps and ultra-high vacuum (UHV) roughing lines require dedicated preventive maintenance to mitigate hydrocarbon contamination.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Dual-beam FIB milling represents a severe throughput bottleneck in failure analysis and in-line defect metrology, typically requiring 45 to 75 minutes per cut and polish site. If in-line process feedback for CMP tungsten clearing fails to reach the metrology cell within the designated queue time, oxidation of recessed W plugs will skew profilometry and EDS stoichiometry, leading to false process scrap calls or unrepresentative barrier erosion metrics.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Curtaining effect caused by differential Ga+ ion sputter rates between dense W plugs and softer dielectric oxide, obscuring the true plug recess profile and sidewall barrier coverage.
1. Ion beam-induced gallium contamination and amorphization (>10nm depth) from high-voltage milling (30kV), degrading high-resolution in-lens SEM contrast and invalidating EDS chemical state analysis.
1. Mechanical and electrostatic beam damage or charging-induced drift during protective platinum deposition, resulting in premature plug top-surface ablation and loss of post-CMP reference datum.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-1-01` | **Dual-Beam Protective Cap Integrity and Curtaining Suppression Verification** | Dual-Beam FIB/FE-SEM system (Ga+ LMIS column paired with Schottky FEG electron column, GIS Pt precursor, in-lens SE/BSE detectors) | 1. Navigate to target post-CMP tungsten contact plug array using FE-SEM at 5 kV, 50 pA. 2. Deposit in-situ protective Electron-Beam Platinum (EB-Pt) cap: 2.0 kV, 1.6 nA, 200 nm nominal thickness over a 5 um x 2 um box. 3. Deposit Ion-Beam Platinum (IB-Pt) bulk strap: 30 kV, 80 pA, 1.2 um thickness directly atop the EB-Pt layer. 4. Execute bulk cross-section trench milling: 30 kV, 1.0 nA stair-step pattern terminating 250 nm before target plug center. 5. Intermediate clean-up mill: 30 kV, 100 pA pattern terminating 50 nm before target plug center. 6. Final low-damage cross-section polish: 5 kV, 20 pA angled polish (tilt ±1.5° rock) precisely bisecting the 220nm tungsten plug. 7. Image cross-section in-situ via In-Lens SE detector at 2.0 kV, 25 pA, WD 4.0 mm, capturing high-resolution digital micrograph. | `Curtaining striation depth across the SiO2/W interface must be < 4.0 nm as measured by profile grey-level variation; EB-Pt protective cap thickness must measure >= 180 nm across 100% of the plug opening with zero top-surface Ga sputtering penetration into the W plug.` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-1-02` | **Post-FIB Amorphous Damage Layer and Contact Plug Recess CD Metrology** | In-situ In-Lens BSE / High-Resolution FE-SEM, calibrated digital line-scan metrology module, low-kV Ga+ polishing column (2 kV capability) | 1. Tilt stage to 52° (orthogonal to electron beam optical axis) and adjust focus/astigmatism at 2.0 kV, 100kX magnification on cross-section plane. 2. Acquire calibrated 16-bit In-Lens secondary electron image (4096 x 3536 resolution, dwell time 10 us/pixel). 3. Establish baseline datum line across top planar oxide surface adjacent to contact plug opening. 4. Execute orthogonal line-scan profiler across center of the bisected W plug to determine vertical recess depth relative to adjacent oxide datum. 5. Measure remaining Ti/TiN barrier liner thickness at bottom corner and sidewall of contact via. 6. Inspect oxide lattice amorphization halo under high-contrast BSE mode at plug interface. | `Amorphous damaged halo thickness at the W/SiO2 boundary must be <= 5.0 nm; tungsten plug recess depth measurement must yield repeatability of <= ±2.0 nm (3-sigma) across 5 repeat measurements on the same site; void detection threshold resolution must resolve gaps >= 3.0 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, EN 374-3 certified), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and laser/radiation safety splash goggles, Class 100 cleanroom flame-retardant anti-static lab coat, Vapor respirator equipped with organic vapor / acid gas cartridges (during GIS precursor replenishment)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Eye contact: Flush immediately with sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately, wash affected skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and copious running water for 15 minutes. Inhalation of organometallic vapors: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek acute medical evaluation. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting without medical instruction; rinse mouth thoroughly with water.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dual-beam vacuum chamber turbomolecular and scroll roughing pumps must exhaust directly to a dedicated scrubber duct with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s. GIS precursor load-lock box must be operated inside a certified laminar flow hood with active chemical filtration (exhaust flow rate >= 150 CFM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent GIS organometallic ampoules and solid waste must be sealed in heavy-gauge polyethylene bags and handled as hazardous heavy-metal/flammable solid waste. Gallium-contaminated ion column parts must be cleaned in a dedicated ultrasonic tank using dilute nitric acid (5%), with effluent collected in labeled hazardous chemical waste drums for neutralization and certified off-site heavy metal reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum (GIS precursor)** | `94442-22-5` | Sublimed Electronic Grade (99.9%) | `> 99.0%` |
| **Gallium (LMIS source emitter)** | `7440-55-3` | Ultra-High Purity 7N | `99.99999%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA) for chamber wiper/degreasing** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Dry post-CMP cleaved coupon, DI water-rinsed and spin-dried, free of abrasive slurry particulate (silica/alumina), with native oxide growth on tungsten < 0.5 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Precision cross-sectioned via cavity with dual-layer Pt protective cap, low-kV Ga+ polished face (<5nm damage layer), kept under high vacuum (<1e-6 mbar) or backfilled with inert N2 purge.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Uncontrolled ambient exposure exceeding 30 minutes promotes galvanic micro-corrosion and atmospheric oxidation of the recessed W plug (forming porous WO3), altering cross-sectional dimensions, causing volume expansion artifacts, and degrading in-line EDS chemical profiling.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Dual-beam FIB precision cross-section site preparation successfully executed on 180nm node tungsten contact plugs. Dual Pt protective cap (e-beam and Ga+ beam) prevents surface recess ablation, followed by stepped coarse-to-fine milling and final 2-5 kV low-damage polishing. The cross-section face cleanly bisects the plug core with minimal curtaining and <5nm amorphization, providing sub-nanometer metrology baseline for CMP over-etch recess, barrier coverage, and core void analysis.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `FIB_W_PLUG_XSEC_INLENS_SEM_METROLOGY_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `POST_CMP_RECESS_AND_BARRIER_LINE_PROFILE_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `HIGH_RES_UNCROPPED_16BIT_XSECTION_MICROGRAPH.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Tungsten contact plug center bisect accuracy within longitudinal beam placement** | `0.0 nm (center plane)` | ± 10.0 nm | In-situ high-resolution FE-SEM top-down overlay comparison against contact via layout coordinates prior to and post cut. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Ga+ induced surface amorphization and thermal damage layer thickness at cross-section face** | `3.0 nm` | < 5.0 nm maximum | Cross-sectional In-Lens BSE backscatter contrast profile and edge-spread function across the polished W/SiO2 interface. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Protective EB-Pt strap thickness retention directly above tungsten plug recess center** | `220.0 nm` | >= 180.0 nm | Calibrated vertical SEM cross-section point-to-point measurement from top of W plug to EB-Pt/IB-Pt boundary. |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Cross-section SEM micrographs exhibit zero observable curtaining (striations < 4nm), undamaged post-CMP plug recess profile confirmed by intact EB-Pt cap (>180nm retained), damage zone <5nm, and quantitative CSV line-scan metrics successfully archived into the Fab Metrology database.

testcases.pre_conditions: Wafer coupon cleaved and mounted on a 45° pre-tilted stub using conductive carbon tape; chamber base vacuum < 5.0e-6 mbar; electron beam aligned and calibrated at 2.0 kV and 5.0 kV; Ga+ ion column aligned at 30 kV.
testcases.procedure:
1. Navigate to target post-CMP tungsten contact plug array using FE-SEM at 5 kV, 50 pA.
2. Deposit in-situ protective Electron-Beam Platinum (EB-Pt) cap: 2.0 kV, 1.6 nA, 200 nm nominal thickness over a 5 um x 2 um box.
3. Deposit Ion-Beam Platinum (IB-Pt) bulk strap: 30 kV, 80 pA, 1.2 um thickness directly atop the EB-Pt layer.
4. Execute bulk cross-section trench milling: 30 kV, 1.0 nA stair-step pattern terminating 250 nm before target plug center.
5. Intermediate clean-up mill: 30 kV, 100 pA pattern terminating 50 nm before target plug center.
6. Final low-damage cross-section polish: 5 kV, 20 pA angled polish (tilt ±1.5° rock) precisely bisecting the 220nm tungsten plug.
7. Image cross-section in-situ via In-Lens SE detector at 2.0 kV, 25 pA, WD 4.0 mm, capturing high-resolution digital micrograph.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Curtaining striation depth across the SiO2/W interface must be < 4.0 nm as measured by profile grey-level variation; EB-Pt protective cap thickness must measure >= 180 nm across 100% of the plug opening with zero top-surface Ga sputtering penetration into the W plug.

testcases.title: Post-FIB Amorphous Damage Layer and Contact Plug Recess CD Metrology
testcases.instrumentation: In-situ In-Lens BSE / High-Resolution FE-SEM, calibrated digital line-scan metrology module, low-kV Ga+ polishing column (2 kV capability)
testcases.pre_conditions: FIB milling of primary trench completed per TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-1-01; final 2 kV, 15 pA glancing angle polish applied for 90 seconds to eliminate Ga amorphization layer.
testcases.procedure:
1. Tilt stage to 52° (orthogonal to electron beam optical axis) and adjust focus/astigmatism at 2.0 kV, 100kX magnification on cross-section plane.
2. Acquire calibrated 16-bit In-Lens secondary electron image (4096 x 3536 resolution, dwell time 10 us/pixel).
3. Establish baseline datum line across top planar oxide surface adjacent to contact plug opening.
4. Execute orthogonal line-scan profiler across center of the bisected W plug to determine vertical recess depth relative to adjacent oxide datum.
5. Measure remaining Ti/TiN barrier liner thickness at bottom corner and sidewall of contact via.
6. Inspect oxide lattice amorphization halo under high-contrast BSE mode at plug interface.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Amorphous damaged halo thickness at the W/SiO2 boundary must be <= 5.0 nm; tungsten plug recess depth measurement must yield repeatability of <= ±2.0 nm (3-sigma) across 5 repeat measurements on the same site; void detection threshold resolution must resolve gaps >= 3.0 nm.

ppe_required: Cleanroom nitrile gloves (double-gloved, EN 374-3 certified)
ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and laser/radiation safety splash goggles
Class 100 cleanroom flame-retardant anti-static lab coat
Vapor respirator equipped with organic vapor / acid gas cartridges (during GIS precursor replenishment)
ehs_protocol.antidote_and_first_aid: Eye contact: Flush immediately with sterile eyewash solution for at least 15 minutes, holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. Skin contact: Remove contaminated clothing immediately, wash affected skin thoroughly with non-abrasive soap and copious running water for 15 minutes. Inhalation of organometallic vapors: Move victim to fresh air immediately; provide artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; seek acute medical evaluation. Ingestion: Do not induce vomiting without medical instruction; rinse mouth thoroughly with water.
ehs_protocol.exhaust_and_ventilation: Dual-beam vacuum chamber turbomolecular and scroll roughing pumps must exhaust directly to a dedicated scrubber duct with minimum face velocity of 0.5 m/s. GIS precursor load-lock box must be operated inside a certified laminar flow hood with active chemical filtration (exhaust flow rate >= 150 CFM).
ehs_protocol.waste_neutralization: Spent GIS organometallic ampoules and solid waste must be sealed in heavy-gauge polyethylene bags and handled as hazardous heavy-metal/flammable solid waste. Gallium-contaminated ion column parts must be cleaned in a dedicated ultrasonic tank using dilute nitric acid (5%), with effluent collected in labeled hazardous chemical waste drums for neutralization and certified off-site heavy metal reclamation.

q_time_constraints.incoming_surface_state: Dry post-CMP cleaved coupon, DI water-rinsed and spin-dried, free of abrasive slurry particulate (silica/alumina), with native oxide growth on tungsten < 0.5 nm.
q_time_constraints.outgoing_surface_state: Precision cross-sectioned via cavity with dual-layer Pt protective cap, low-kV Ga+ polished face (<5nm damage layer), kept under high vacuum (<1e-6 mbar) or backfilled with inert N2 purge.
q_time_constraints.critical_risk_on_expiry: Uncontrolled ambient exposure exceeding 30 minutes promotes galvanic micro-corrosion and atmospheric oxidation of the recessed W plug (forming porous WO3), altering cross-sectional dimensions, causing volume expansion artifacts, and degrading in-line EDS chemical profiling.

expected_result.summary: Dual-beam FIB precision cross-section site preparation successfully executed on 180nm node tungsten contact plugs. Dual Pt protective cap (e-beam and Ga+ beam) prevents surface recess ablation, followed by stepped coarse-to-fine milling and final 2-5 kV low-damage polishing. The cross-section face cleanly bisects the plug core with minimal curtaining and <5nm amorphization, providing sub-nanometer metrology baseline for CMP over-etch recess, barrier coverage, and core void analysis.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Tungsten contact plug center bisect accuracy within longitudinal beam placement
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: In-situ high-resolution FE-SEM top-down overlay comparison against contact via layout coordinates prior to and post cut.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Ga+ induced surface amorphization and thermal damage layer thickness at cross-section face
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Cross-sectional In-Lens BSE backscatter contrast profile and edge-spread function across the polished W/SiO2 interface.

quantitative_assertions.assertion: Protective EB-Pt strap thickness retention directly above tungsten plug recess center
quantitative_assertions.verification_method: Calibrated vertical SEM cross-section point-to-point measurement from top of W plug to EB-Pt/IB-Pt boundary.

expected_result.signoff_criteria: Cross-section SEM micrographs exhibit zero observable curtaining (striations < 4nm), undamaged post-CMP plug recess profile confirmed by intact EB-Pt cap (>180nm retained), damage zone <5nm, and quantitative CSV line-scan metrics successfully archived into the Fab Metrology database.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Title: Defect Relocation & Protective Electron/Ion Beam Pt Deposition
**Module**: In-Line Metrology & Failure Analysis (Dual-Beam FIB Site Preparation)  
**Generation Context**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — W-Plug Overburden CMP / Metrology

---

### 1. Process Overview & Visual Workflow

In 180nm DRAM fabrication (stacked capacitor over bitline / W-plug contact architectures), cross-sectional analysis of post-CMP residual tungsten or dielectric defects requires non-destructive site relocation and protective cap deposition. Direct focused ion beam (FIB) milling on raw topographies causes immediate sputtering damage, curtaining artifacts, and edge rounding. A dual-layer Platinum (Pt) strap consisting of non-damaging electron-beam deposition (`e-Pt`) followed by robust ion-beam deposition (`i-Pt`) encapsulates the defect site.

```text
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│  Defect Navigation &  │
│       Alignment       │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│       Dual-Beam       │
│   Coincidence Setup   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   Electron-Beam Pt    │
│   Deposition (e-Pt)   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│      Ion-Beam Pt      │
│   Deposition (i-Pt)   │
│                       │
└───────────┬───────────┘
            │
            │
            ▼
┌───────────────────────┐
│                       │
│   FIB Cross-Section   │
│     Milling Ready     │
│                       │
└───────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Defect Relocation & Coordinate Transformation**:
   - Import defect coordinates from the in-line optical/defect review map.
   - Perform a 3-point wafer/die global coordinate alignment using lithographic alignment marks.
   - Navigate the sample stage to the target W-plug defect site at coincidence height (working distance $WD = 5.0\text{ mm}$, stage tilt $= 0^\circ$).

2. **Dual-Beam Coincidence Verification**:
   - Align the SEM electron optical axis and Ga⁺ Focused Ion Beam (FIB) column at the dual-beam eucentric height ($52^\circ$ relative angle).
   - Verify defect position using low-dose SEM imaging ($E_{beam} = 2.0\text{ kV}$, beam current $I_e = 50\text{ pA}$) across the $360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$ bitline/wordline pitch array to prevent surface charging or beam damage.

3. **GIS Insertion & Gas Delivery Calibration**:
   - Insert the Methylcyclopentadienyl(trimethyl)platinum $[(CH_3)_3Pt(CpCH_3)]$ Gas Injection System (GIS) needle.
   - Position needle tip at $100\ \mu\text{m}$ clearance above the substrate and $150\ \mu\text{m}$ lateral offset from the defect center.
   - Heat GIS reservoir to $28^\circ\text{C}$ to establish uniform organometallic precursor flux across the localized defect area.

4. **Electron-Beam Protective Pt Deposition (e-Pt Pre-Cap)**:
   - Define deposition region: Strap dimensions $4.0\ \mu\text{m}\ (\text{width}) \times 15.0\ \mu\text{m}\ (\text{length})$, centered over the defect with $>1.5\ \mu\text{m}$ overlay margin.
   - Run SEM beam-induced deposition at $E_{beam} = 5.0\text{ kV}$, $I_e = 1.6\text{ nA}$, dwell time $= 1.0\ \mu\text{s}$, refresh time $= 100\ \mu\text{s}$.
   - Deposit non-destructive protective buffer layer to target thickness of $200\text{ nm} - 300\text{ nm}$ ($0.25\ \mu\text{m}$ nominal) to seal the post-CMP defect and underlying dielectric stack.

5. **Ion-Beam Structural Pt Deposition (i-Pt Hard Cap)**:
   - Tilt stage to $52^\circ$ (perpendicular to Ga⁺ ion column).
   - Engage Ga⁺ ion beam at $30\text{ kV}$ with a low beam current density of $I_{ion} = 80\text{ pA}$ to initiate interfacial deposition without sputtering the underlying e-Pt cap.
   - Ramp ion current to $I_{ion} = 300\text{ pA}$ for rapid structural build-up.
   - Deposit secondary hard Pt cap to target thickness of $1.5\ \mu\text{m} - 2.0\ \mu\text{m}$ ($1.75\ \mu\text{m}$ nominal) to provide curtain-free protection during rough and fine bulk milling.

6. **Retraction & Pre-Milling Quality Inspection**:
   - Retract GIS needle to home position.
   - Perform non-destructive SEM inspection ($2.0\text{ kV}$) to verify strap morphology, uniformity, and defect coverage prior to cross-section trench milling.

---

### 3. Dimensional Target Metrics

```text
                 Pt Deposition Target Dimensions (um)   
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                        │
Overlay Margin┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░                        │
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
   Strap Width┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒│
i-Pt Thickness┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                      │
e-Pt Thickness┤███                                     │
              │███                                     │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0         1         2        3         4 
```

---

### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter | Target Specification | Tolerance | Unit | Verification Tool / Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Protective e-Pt Buffer Thickness** | $250$ | $\pm 50$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-situ High-Resolution SEM ($52^\circ$ tilted view) |
| **Structural i-Pt Cap Thickness** | $1.75$ | $\pm 0.25$ | $\mu\text{m}$ | In-situ High-Resolution SEM ($52^\circ$ tilted view) |
| **Defect Relocation Overlay Accuracy** | $\le 100$ | Max | $\text{nm}$ | Dual-beam beam-shift / crosshair fiducial metrology |
| **Strap Sputter Loss on Substrate/Defect** | $0.0$ | $\le 5$ | $\text{nm}$ | Interface line profile & TEM/EDS verification |

---

### 5. Context Sources & Literature Citations

- **Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - Used for unit cell geometry and integration boundaries: Access transistor geometry ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$), tungsten plug (W-plug) drain contacts, stacked capacitor topology, and ONO/high-$\kappa$ dielectric stack considerations.
- **Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - Used for architectural pitches: Array bitline and wordline pitch ($\approx 360\text{ nm} - 400\text{ nm}$), gate oxide thickness ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$), ensuring that deposition patterns span multiple pitches ($4.0\ \mu\text{m}$ width $\ge 10\times$ pitch) to prevent edge effect artifacts during FIB cross-sectioning.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Dual-beam FIB/SEM defect relocation requires robust automated coordinate transformation from optical or CD-SEM defect maps (KLARF/CAD alignment). Thermal drift and piezo creep on the 5-axis stage must not exceed 2 nm/min during e-beam/i-beam GIS (Gas Injection System) deposition, or the protective strap will suffer misalignment, exposing the 180nm tungsten plug defect ROI to catastrophic ion beam curtailment.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Direct gallium focused ion beam deposition of Pt directly onto an unprotected tungsten plug or surrounding ILD causes severe Ga+ implantation damage, surface sputtering, and amorphization down to 20-30 nm depth. A multi-layer strategy is mandatory: first, electron-beam-induced Pt deposition (EBID) must deposit at least 250-500 nm of non-destructive platinum to act as a buffer, followed by high-current 30 kV ion-beam-induced deposition (IBID) to reach 1.5-2.0 um protective cap thickness before trench milling.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: The organometallic precursor (MeCpPtMe3 / Trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum(IV)) GIS crucibles are single-source, high-lead-time consumables with strict thermal budget controls. Running the GIS nozzle heater continuously leads to premature precursor degradation, clogged 500 um needles, and localized chamber vacuum degradation below acceptable UHV operating points (1e-6 mbar).
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Throughput bottleneck is acute: defect review on post-W-CMP wafers requires relocating, aligning, and depositing dual-layer Pt straps on 15 to 20 sites per wafer. Unassisted manual navigation and slow EBID rates risk violating the strict 30-minute queue-time window between post-CMP wash and ultra-high-vacuum preservation, threatening queue backlog across metrology shifts.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Gallium ion cascade damage and premature erosion of the tungsten plug defect core due to omitting or insufficiently sizing the initial e-beam Pt protective layer.
1. Curtain effect and non-uniform cross-sectional milling artifacts caused by porosity, carbon contamination (>30%), or pinholes in the organometallic Pt deposit.
1. Stage registration error exceeding 180 nm feature pitch, causing the protective strap to miss the defect epicenter and resulting in destructive milling of the wrong tungsten plug.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-1-1-01` | **Dual-Layer E-Beam and I-Beam Pt Protective Cap Thickness & Morphology Verification** | Dual-Beam FIB/SEM (30 kV Ga+ FIB, Field Emission SEM) with GIS Platinum Precursor | 1. Perform EBID Pt deposition over a 5 um x 2 um box centered on the tungsten defect at 2 kV, 1.4 nA for 180 seconds. 2. Retract/adjust beam parameters to 30 kV Ga+ at 40 pA (IBID) and deposit secondary Pt layer over a 4.5 um x 1.5 um box for 240 seconds. 3. Mill a non-destructive test fiducial cross-section at 30 kV 80 pA and tilt stage to 52 degrees. 4. Measure individual and total Pt cap thicknesses via calibrated secondary electron imaging at 100,000x magnification. | `E-beam Pt layer thickness must be >= 300 nm with 0 nm underlying substrate ion erosion; total composite Pt cap thickness must be >= 1.50 um with density uniformity > 95% (free of voiding > 20 nm diameter).` |
| `TC-CMP-PLANARIZATION-2-3-3-1-1-02` | **Defect Relocation Overlay Accuracy & Lateral Strap Enclosure Verification** | High-Resolution In-Line CD-SEM & Dual-Beam FIB Navigation Coordinate System (CAD/KLARF import) | 1. Drive stage to target W-plug defect coordinates. 2. Acquire 10 kV secondary electron image to identify visual centroid of residual metal defect. 3. Measure offset between programmed coordinate target and actual defect centroid. 4. Deposit 4 um x 2 um Pt protective patch. 5. Measure margin from defect perimeter to outer edge of the Pt strap in both X and Y directions. | `Coordinate relocation error must be <= 50 nm; lateral enclosure margin of Pt deposit around all defect edges must be >= 500 nm symmetrically.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving required during precursor exchange), Chemical splash goggles and full face shield for vacuum break procedures, Flame-retardant cleanroom lab coat / antistatic gown, Half-mask respirator with organic vapor/P100 particulate cartridge during GIS crucible replacement
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of organometallic precursor contact: immediately flush skin or eyes with copious amounts of DI water for at least 15 minutes. For inhalation, immediately remove victim to fresh air and seek urgent medical evaluation. Treat for platinum-group organometallic sensitivity and contact dermatitis.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: FIB system turbo-molecular and roughing pump exhaust must be continuously routed to dedicated fab toxic sub-atmospheric exhaust with scrubbed solvent ducting; precursor reload bench must have localized laminar capture velocity >= 0.5 m/s (100 FPM).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent GIS cartridges and Ga ion source assemblies must be sealed in argon-purged amber containers, labeled as hazardous platinum/heavy-metal organometallic waste, and sent to certified specialized metal-reclamation facilities.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Trimethyl(methylcyclopentadienyl)platinum(IV)** | `94442-22-5` | Sublimed Electronic Grade (>= 99.9% metal basis) | `100% solid precursor` |
| **Gallium (Liquid Metal Ion Source)** | `7440-55-3` | High Purity Electronic Grade (>= 99.99999%) | `100% metal` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly polished post-W-CMP planar surface with DI water spin-rinse-dried finish; zero slurry residues; native oxide growth on W plug < 1.0 nm.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: High-vacuum passivated defect site encapsulated under hermetic dual-layer e-beam/i-beam Pt protective strap; zero localized gallium staining outside target box.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure causes uncontrolled galvanic corrosion between tungsten plug and TiN barrier liner, accompanied by thick native WO3 oxidation that degrades defect contrast and promotes delamination of the EBID Pt strap.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful non-destructive coordinate relocation of tungsten plug residual defect and complete encapsulation under a dense, void-free dual-layer (EBID/IBID) platinum strap guaranteeing pristine structural integrity for subsequent cross-section milling.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `RELOC_PT_METROLOGY_REPORT_TC-CMP-2-3-3-1.pdf`
- [ ] `DEFECT_PT_OVERLAY_ALIGNMENT_COORDS.csv`
- [ ] `PRE_POST_PT_DEPOSITION_HIGHRES_SEM.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **E-beam deposited initial platinum buffer layer thickness** | `350 nm` | ±50 nm | Calibrated in-situ FIB cross-section SEM measurement at 52-degree tilt |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Total composite Pt protective strap thickness (EBID + IBID)** | `1.80 um` | ±0.20 um | Cross-sectional secondary electron profile metrology |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Defect site relocation coordinate deviation from KLARF map** | `25 nm` | ≤ 50 nm | In-line automated fiducial registration and high-magnification SEM imaging |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All target defects relocated within <= 50 nm deviation, encapsulated by >= 300 nm EBID Pt plus >= 1.2 um IBID Pt without substrate Ga ion amorphization, and validated by dual-tilt SEM imaging prior to rough FIB trench milling.
