# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document ID: `SOP-MET-180NM-TCK-001`
**Title:** Thermal & Cryogenic Chuck Calibration and High-Frequency Triaxial Probe Setup  
**Hierarchy Level:** Metrology & Characterization / 180nm Open-Source DRAM (Gen 3)  
**Target Structure:** 180nm 1T1C Stacked Crown MIM/High-$k$ Storage Capacitor & Access Transistor Arrays

---

### 1. Scope & Objective
This procedure establishes exact protocol instructions for thermal and cryogenic vacuum/ambient probe station chuck calibration, dry purge sealing, triaxial cable driven-guard integrity verification, and high-frequency RF/C-V calibration substrate alignment. The goal is to prepare the metrology bench for femtoampere-level dielectric leakage ($I\text{--}V$) and low-noise capacitance-voltage ($C\text{--}V$) dispersion extraction of 180nm cell capacitors across temperature ranges from 77 K (or $-55^\circ\text{C}$ cryogenic purge) up to elevated operating conditions ($85^\circ\text{C}$).

---

### 2. Relevant Literature & Architecture Context
* **Dielectric & Storage Capacitor Constraints:** Stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) utilizing $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ or ONO high-$k$ dielectric stacks ($\kappa > 15$, $\text{EOT} \approx 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$) requiring target capacitance budget $\ge 25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ (minimum $28\text{ fF}$) [Source: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*, *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*].
* **Leakage Floor Threshold:** Leakage current floor must resolve sub-threshold and dielectric leakage target $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain refresh retention intervals $> 64\text{ ms}$ [Source: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench*, *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering*].
* **Bonding Pad & Contact Geometry:** Characterization targets connect to on-chip probe pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$) matching aluminum top metallization [Source: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging*].

---

### 3. Equipment & Materials
1. **Triaxial/RF Probe Station:** Low-leakage shielded environmental probe chamber with vacuum chuck.
2. **Thermal Chuck Controller:** Closed-loop chiller/heater system capable of stable thermal dwells up to $85^\circ\text{C}$ and cryogenic cooling down to sub-zero/LN2 temperatures with $\pm 0.1^\circ\text{C}$ precision.
3. **Purge Gas System:** Dry high-purity $\text{N}_2$ purge ($> 99.999\%$ purity, dew point $\le -70^\circ\text{C}$).
4. **Cabling & Probing:** Low-noise triaxial cables (Center Force, Inner Guard, Outer Shield/Chassis Ground) with beryllium-copper or tungsten probe tips ($< 10\ \mu\text{m}$ tip radius for $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pads).
5. **Standards:** Impedance standard calibration substrate (ISS / Open-Short-Load standards) and calibrated thin-film RTD surface thermometer.

---

### 4. Step-by-Step Procedure

```text
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                       SETUP & CALIBRATION FLOW                           |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 1. Environmental Chamber Purge & Dew-Point Stabilization                 |
|    - Flow dry N2 at 15-20 L/min until chamber dew point <= -70 deg C     |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 2. Chuck Thermal Sensor Multi-Point Calibration                          |
|    - Validate surface RTD vs controller at 25 deg C and 85 deg C         |
|    - Maintain stability within +/- 0.1 deg C over a 15-minute soak       |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 3. Triaxial Guarding & Open-Circuit Residual Leakage Test                |
|    - Apply driven inner guard; measure open-air tip current at 85 deg C  |
|    - Verify background baseline leakage < 0.2 fA (limit < 1 fA floor)    |
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
                                    |
                                    v
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| 4. High-Frequency C-V / RF Impedance De-embedding                       |
|    - Probe Open/Short standards on ISS; execute zero-offset subtraction  |
|    - Verify residual stray capacitance offset < 1 fF (target budget 28 fF)|
+--------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```

#### Step 1: Environmental Purge & Hermetic Sealing
1. Load the reference calibration wafer or coupon onto the thermal vacuum chuck and engage vacuum hold-down ($\ge 80\text{ kPa}$ differential pressure).
2. Hermetically seal the environmental dark box chamber.
3. Initiate dry $\text{N}_2$ purge at a flow rate of $15\text{ to }20\text{ L/min}$ for at least 30 minutes to purge ambient humidity prior to temperature cycling, preventing condensation or ice frost formation during sub-ambient/cryogenic ramping.
4. Verify the chamber exhaust dew-point sensor reads $\le -70^\circ\text{C}$. Maintain continuous positive-pressure dry $\text{N}_2$ trickle flow ($2\text{ to }5\text{ L/min}$) throughout all operations.

#### Step 2: Thermal Chuck Temperature Calibration
1. Mount a calibrated secondary reference RTD surface sensor onto the chuck center and edge zones.
2. Step chuck temperature across setpoints: Room Temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) to Elevated Memory Qualification Temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$).
3. At $85^\circ\text{C}$, allow a 15-minute thermal soak. Calibrate controller offset so that surface temperature error remains within $\Delta T \le \pm 0.1^\circ\text{C}$ with cross-chuck thermal gradient $< 0.3^\circ\text{C}$.

#### Step 3: Triaxial Cable Guarding & Residual Noise Floor Verification
1. Connect triaxial feedthrough lines from the high-resolution Semiconductor Parameter Analyzer (SMU) to the micromanipulator probe arms.
2. Confirm the triaxial connection structure:
   - **Center Conductor:** Signal force/sense line to device pad.
   - **Inner Shield:** Active driven guard held at identical potential ($V_{\text{guard}} \approx V_{\text{force}}$) to eliminate cable dielectric leakage.
   - **Outer Shield:** High-integrity instrument chassis/earth ground.
3. Elevate the probe tips in open-air ($100\ \mu\text{m}$ above the wafer chuck) at $T = 85^\circ\text{C}$.
4. Apply a voltage sweep from $-1.0\text{ V}$ to $+1.5\text{ V}$ across the open probe tip.
5. Record residual system leakage. The open-circuit baseline current must not exceed $0.2\text{ fA}$ to guarantee reliable measurement of the $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ DRAM leakage floor.

#### Step 4: High-Frequency $C\text{--}V$ Dispersion & Cable De-embedding
1. Lower probe tips onto an impedance standard substrate (ISS).
2. Align probe needles to probe pads ($100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ pitch geometry).
3. Execute standard Open/Short compensation calibration across the operational frequency band ($10\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$/$10\text{ MHz}$):
   - **Open Calibration:** Measure probe tips lifted $\sim 50\ \mu\text{m}$ above the open standard; zero out parallel stray susceptance ($G_0, C_0$).
   - **Short Calibration:** Land probe tips on planar gold/aluminum shorting strip; zero out series residual resistance and cable inductance ($R_s, L_s$).
4. Verify corrected stray parasitic capacitance is de-embedded to $< 1.0\text{ fF}$, ensuring sufficient resolution to quantify individual and small-array $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ crown capacitors.

---

### 5. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Requirement | Units | Relevant Context Constraint |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **System Residual Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak, background}}$)** | $\le 0.20$ | Max $\le 0.50$ (at $85^\circ\text{C}$, $V_{\text{bias}} = 1.0\text{ V}$) | $\text{fA}$ | Resolves $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ retention requirement |
| **Thermal Chuck Temperature Stability & Accuracy** | $85.0$ | $\pm 0.1$ (dwell drift over 15 min) | $^\circ\text{C}$ | DRAM cell retention qualification baseline |
| **Residual Parasitic Capacitance Floor ($C_{\text{offset}}$)** | $< 1.0$ | De-embedded open residual $< 1.0$ | $\text{fF}$ | Cell capacitor budget $\ge 25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ (nom. $28\text{ fF}$) |
| **Chamber Purge Moisture Dew Point** | $\le -70.0$ | Max allowable $-65.0$ before thermal ramp | $^\circ\text{C}$ | Prevents condensation down to cryogenic range |

---

### 6. Referenced Literature
* **[Source: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench]**: Details 180nm cell layout geometry, stacked capacitor with $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ dielectric ($\kappa > 15$), capacitance budget minimum $28\text{ fF/cell}$, and refresh leakage threshold $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
* **[Source: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering]**: Establishes 1T1C target storage capacitance of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$ to ensure retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ with $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ EOT.
* **[Source: Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging]**: Specifies standard $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad dimensions and temperature constraints.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal chuck expansion and contraction cycles between 77 K (LN2 cryogenic) and 473 K (+200 °C) induce substantial mechanical drift (up to 15–25 µm lateral translation), risking catastrophic probe tip gouging or lift-off from 180nm crown capacitor test pads (typically 40 µm x 40 µm). Active triaxial guarding must maintain isolation resistance > 100 TΩ without introducing ground-loop capacitance (> 0.5 pF) into high-frequency C-V dispersion sweeps up to 10 MHz.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Accurate extraction of Fowler-Nordheim and Poole-Frenkel conduction across the ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 crown nanolaminate requires sub-femtoampere floor sensitivity (< 10 fA) and thermal chuck temperature stability within ±0.1 K. Triaxial cables and ceramic probe arm manipulators must eliminate triboelectric, piezoelectric, and thermoelectric Seebeck voltages during thermal ramping, otherwise artificial leakage artifacts will mask trap-assisted tunneling currents.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procurement of specialized low-noise triaxial micro-positioners, gold-plated beryllium-copper (BeCu) / tungsten probe needles, and automated closed-cycle liquid nitrogen (LN2)/purge gas thermal chuck controllers faces lead times exceeding 16–20 weeks; secondary sourcing for high-purity triaxial feedthroughs and vacuum/dry-purge environmental chambers must be locked down immediately to avoid project milestone slippage.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Budget and schedule risks are severe if thermal chuck integration requires bespoke vacuum chamber modifications. The qualification protocol must decouple baseline room-temperature automated matrix switching tests from cryogenic/high-temperature runs, ensuring initial 180nm MPW tapeout C-V parameter extractions proceed without blocking on complete cryogenic chamber commissioning.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Moisture condensation and frost formation on wafer chuck and crown dielectric test pads during sub-zero cooling due to inadequate dry N2 glovebox/chamber purge dew point (> -70 °C), inducing catastrophic surface shunting and dielectric breakdown misclassification.
1. Mechanical tip displacement exceeding contact pad boundaries (> 10 µm drift) caused by thermal expansion mismatch between the chuck platen and manipulator mounting bridge during 300 K to 473 K sweeps, resulting in scratch damage to ALD crown top electrodes.
1. Triaxial guard shield leakage or cable dielectric absorption saturation introducing parasitic shunt conductance > 10 pS, corrupting low-frequency dielectric dispersion and trap density (Dit) extraction.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-1-01` | **Thermal Chuck Temperature Uniformity and Triaxial Residual Leakage Calibration** | Automated Thermal-Cryogenic Wafer Prober (MPI/FormFactor/Signatone), Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Parameter Analyzer with B1517A High-Resolution SMU (HRSMU) and triaxial guarding, Class A PT100/K-type thin-film surface calibration wafer, Chilled N2/Liquid Nitrogen Dewar Purge Controller. | 1. Position thermal chuck at 298 K (25 °C), lower triaxial probe needles onto open ceramic isolation test artifact, and record leakage floor for 60 seconds at V_guard = V_force = 5.0 V. 2. Ramp chuck temperature from 77 K (-196 °C) to 473 K (+200 °C) in steps of 25 K at a ramp rate of 5 K/min under continuous dry N2 purge (flow rate > 30 slm). 3. At each temperature dwell (stabilization time = 10 minutes), log 9-point surface temperature across 150mm chuck platen. 4. Simultaneously execute a 100-sample DC leakage measurement at 1.0 V bias across triaxial open terminals to measure baseline noise floor and guard isolation. | `Chuck temperature uniformity <= ±0.5 °C across all 9 zones from 77 K to 473 K; triaxial probe open-circuit background leakage current <= 10 fA at ±3.3 V bias across the entire temperature envelope; no thermal drift induced tip movement > 3 µm measured via optical microscope.` |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-1-02` | **High-Frequency C-V Triaxial Probe Linearity and Residual Capacitance De-embedding** | Keysight E4980A Precision LCR Meter / B1520A Multi-Frequency C-V Module, 40 GHz GSG/Triaxial probe heads, Standard Impedance Substrate (ISS) calibration standard (Alumina substrate with open, short, 50-ohm load, and calibrated 1.0 pF capacitor structures). | 1. Perform complete Open/Short/Load calibration on standard impedance substrate at frequencies from 1 kHz to 10 MHz with 30 mV AC oscillation amplitude. 2. Lower triaxial probe tips onto calibrated 1.0 pF and 10.0 pF standard thin-film capacitor test structures. 3. Measure C-V characteristics across a DC bias sweep from -3.3 V to +3.3 V with zero integration delay and high-resolution mode. 4. Elevate chuck temperature to 398 K (125 °C) and repeat C-V extraction to quantify parasitic line phase shift and dielectric loss factor (tan delta). | `Measured residual open capacitance after de-embedding <= 15 fF; capacitance measurement error <= ±0.2% on standard 1.0 pF reference across 10 kHz to 2 MHz; dissipation factor (tan delta) <= 0.001 at 1 MHz; contact resistance drift <= 0.05 ohms over 50 consecutive touchdown cycles.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cryogenic safety gloves (EN 511 compliant) for liquid nitrogen handling, Full-face polycarbonate splash shield (ANSI Z87.1), High-temperature thermal insulating gloves rated to 250 °C, Cleanroom antistatic flame-retardant lab coat, Closed-toe ESD safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For cryogenic frostbite: Immediately immerse affected area in warm water bath (38–42 °C / 100–108 °F); do not rub or apply direct dry heat; seek emergency medical care immediately. For thermal burns: Flush with cool potable water for minimum 15 minutes; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing. In case of asphyxiation from LN2/N2 gas displacement: Immediately remove victim to fresh air; administer supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; initiate CPR if unconscious.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous probe chamber point-exhaust ventilation at >= 100 CFM to vent boiling N2 boil-off gas; cleanroom lab ambient oxygen depletion monitoring system (dual O2 sensors with audio-visual alarm triggering at < 19.5% O2); pressure relief valves on cryogenic transfer lines vented to building exterior.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Liquid nitrogen boil-off self-evaporates safely through dedicated dedicated exterior-ducted cryogenic vent line. Used cleanroom IPA wipes must be collected in sealed, grounded, dedicated solvent waste containers for hazardous waste disposal in compliance with EPA/RCRA regulations.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Liquid Nitrogen (Cryogenic)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity (UHP) Grade 5.0 | `99.999%` |
| **Nitrogen Gas (Purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Electronic Grade / Semiconductor UHP | `99.9999%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited and patterned ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 crown capacitor test wafers with TiN/polysilicon top electrodes, unpassivated or selectively opened contact pads, free of organic contamination and ambient moisture adsorption.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested and probe-marked wafer pads with scrub marks < 15% of total pad area, dry N2 desiccator stabilized, zero moisture condensation, pristine ALD dielectric stack with verified C-V/I-V operational limits.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding air exposure queue time leads to native oxide hydration and ambient moisture adsorption along ALD nanolaminate grain boundaries, creating parasitic surface conduction paths that falsely inflate low-field leakage current by > 2 orders of magnitude and induce misleading interfacial trap states (Dit).

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full calibration and qualification of the thermal-cryogenic wafer chuck (77 K to 473 K) and high-frequency triaxial probing assembly, establishing ultra-low electrical noise baseline (leakage < 10 fA, residual capacitance < 15 fF) necessary for uncorrupted dielectric C-V dispersion and I-V leakage profiling of 180nm crown capacitor modules.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `Thermal_Chuck_Temperature_Uniformity_Matrix_77K_473K.csv`
- [ ] `Triaxial_Probe_Residual_Impedance_DeEmbedding_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `High_Frequency_CV_Baseline_Dispersion_Verification.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Triaxial probe system background leakage floor under dark, dry-purged conditions across -3.3 V to +3.3 V force bias** | `5.0 fA` | <= 10.0 fA | Keysight B1517A HRSMU 100-sample integration test on lifted open probe needles inside closed purge chamber at 298 K. |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Thermal chuck surface temperature stability and spatial gradient across 150mm diameter platen across full operating range** | `0.1 K` | <= ±0.5 °C | Calibrated 9-point surface PT100 RTD wafer telemetry sweep logged during 30-minute steady-state dwell at 77 K, 298 K, and 473 K. |
| `ASSERT-03` | **High-frequency de-embedded residual open capacitance for C-V probe setup at 1 MHz test frequency** | `10.0 fF` | <= 15.0 fF | E4980A four-terminal-pair open-circuit de-embedding measurement calibrated against standard impedance alumina substrate (ISS). |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Successful completion and verification of ASSERT-01, ASSERT-02, and ASSERT-03 with probe drift <= 3 µm over full thermal cycle (77 K to 473 K), zero moisture condensation under continuous N2 purge (dew point <= -75 °C), and formal engineering sign-off from both the Lead Metrology Engineer and Cleanroom EHS Officer.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## Wideband Multi-Frequency C-V Dispersion Characterization Across Temperature (-50°C to 125°C)

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-CV-003`  
**Process Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) — Gen 3 (180 nm)  
**Classification:** Metrology & Characterization / Electrical Qualification  

---

### 1. Process Workflow Diagram

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Load Wafer on      │
│   Cryo/Thermal Chuck   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   N2 Purge & Dry Air   │
│       Evacuation       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Temperature Sweep:   │
│      -50C to 125C      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Multi-Frequency C-V:  │
│     1 kHz to 1 MHz     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Extract Cmin, Cmax,   │
│    Dispersion, Dit     │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **Tool Setup and Fixture Conditioning**:
   - Mount the 180nm DRAM test coupon/wafer (bearing Crown-shaped MIM storage capacitors with $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ high-$k$ stack or ONO triple dielectric, gate dielectric $\text{SiO}_2$ physical thickness ~3.5 nm) onto a closed-loop cryogenic/thermal chuck system.
   - Establish continuous dry $\text{N}_2$ chamber purge (dew point $\le -70^\circ\text{C}$, relative humidity $< 1\%$) to prevent moisture condensation and frost formation during cryogenic ramp-down below $0^\circ\text{C}$.

2. **Open/Short/Load LCR Meter Calibration**:
   - Perform open/short cable compensation and reference de-embedding on the wideband impedance analyzer / LCR meter across the wideband frequency spectrum from $1\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$ at the probe tip interface using standard $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum test pads.

3. **Multi-Temperature Thermal Cycling Profile**:
   - Step chuck temperature through designated thermal setpoints: **$-50^\circ\text{C}$**, **$25^\circ\text{C}$**, **$85^\circ\text{C}$** (standard DRAM operating reference), and **$125^\circ\text{C}$**.
   - Soak wafer for a minimum of 10 minutes at each setpoint until temperature stabilization reaches within $\pm 0.5^\circ\text{C}$.

4. **Multi-Frequency C-V Sweeps**:
   - Contact top electrode and bottom plate/W-plug contact of test array structures.
   - Apply DC bias voltage sweep from $-1.8\text{ V}$ to $+1.8\text{ V}$ (step voltage: $20\text{ mV}$, hold time: $50\text{ ms}$) superimposed with an AC oscillation signal $V_{\text{ac}} = 25\text{ mV}_{\text{rms}}$.
   - Acquire capacitance ($C$) and conductance ($G$) curves simultaneously at wideband frequencies: $1\text{ kHz}$, $10\text{ kHz}$, $100\text{ kHz}$, and $1\text{ MHz}$.

5. **Dielectric Dispersion & Parameter Extraction**:
   - Extract maximum accumulation capacitance ($C_{\text{max}}$) per cell equivalent.
   - Calculate frequency dispersion across $1\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$ in accumulation ($\Delta C / C_{\text{accum}}$).
   - Evaluate effective high-$k$ dielectric constant ($\kappa$) and equivalent oxide thickness (EOT target $\sim 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$).
   - Perform conductance method analysis ($G_{\text{p}}/\omega$) to extract interface trap state density ($D_{\text{it}}$) as a function of temperature.

---

### 3. Acceptance Criteria

```text
                  ┌────────────────────────────────────┐
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Specification | Exact Physical Units | Verification Method |

| **Minimum Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | **$\ge 25\text{ to }28$** (nominal target $\ge 28$) | $\text{fF/cell}$ | Multi-frequency C-V extraction at $85^\circ\text{C}$, $100\text{ kHz}$ |
| **Dielectric Effective Constant ($\kappa_{\text{eff}}$)** | **$> 15$** | Dimensionless | C-V accumulation extraction with $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ stack |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT)** | **$3\text{ to }4$** | $\text{nm}$ | High-frequency C-V fit in strong accumulation |
| **Cell Leakage Current Target** | **$< 1.0$** | $\text{fA/cell}$ | Quasi-static I-V qualification at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to maintain $> 64\text{ ms}$ refresh |

---

### 4. Literature & Context Citations

1. **Source: *180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench***
   - *Capacitance budget:* Minimum $28\text{ fF}$ per cell to ensure noise immunity against alpha-particle soft errors and bitline coupling capacitance.
   - *Dielectric properties:* $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$ high-$k$ stack providing effective dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$.
   - *Leakage current limit:* Sub-threshold and junction leakage kept below $1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ to guarantee refresh integrity.
   - *Topology:* Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, width $W = 220\text{ nm}$; crown-shaped stacked capacitor over bitline (COB) erected above drain via W-plug.

2. **Source: *Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering***
   - *Capacitance bounds:* Storage capacitor minimum capacitance of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF}$ per cell ensuring retention time $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
   - *Equivalent Oxide Thickness:* EOT around $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ utilizing $\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ or $\text{Si}_3\text{N}_4$ high-$k$ dielectrics.
   - *Gate oxide baseline:* Thermally grown $\text{SiO}_2$ at $850^\circ\text{C}\text{--}900^\circ\text{C}$ dry oxidation with $\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$ physical thickness.

3. **Source: *Ultrasonic Wedge and Ball Wire Bonding Assembly for Die Packaging***
   - *Bonding pad geometry:* $100\ \mu\text{m} \times 100\ \mu\text{m}$ aluminum pad test structures.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal expansion mismatch between the 3D crown polysilicon/TiN bottom electrode and the ALD Al2O3/Ta2O5 dielectric stack during thermal chuck ramping (-50°C to 125°C) induces mechanical shear stress, threatening micro-delamination and interface trap density (Dit) shifts that distort high-frequency C-V accumulation profiles. Parasitic cable inductance and series resistance (Rs) across cryogenic/thermal triaxial lines will severely distort C-V curves above 1 MHz unless open/short/load de-embedding is calibrated across the entire temperature envelope.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Wideband C-V dispersion across -50°C to 125°C on Al2O3/Ta2O5 crowns is dominated by oxygen vacancies and trap states at the dielectric-electrode interfaces. Frequency dispersion in accumulation (1 kHz to 10 MHz) directly flags Fermi-level pinning and border traps, while deep cryogenic freeze-out (-50°C) reveals low-activation-energy shallow defects that otherwise remain masked by thermal generation at 25°C and 125°C. Verifying that accumulation capacitance remains >= 25 fF/cell equivalent across wideband frequencies is essential for cell sensing margin.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Liquid nitrogen (LN2) delivery manifolds and cryogenic probe station thermal chuck controllers (e.g., Temptronic/MPI) face global procurement lead times exceeding 18 weeks. In addition, cryogenic micro-chamber feedthrough seals and low-noise triaxial probe tips rated for -50°C to 150°C have tight single-source constraints with high replacement costs upon thermal cycling fatigue.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Thermal settling time during wideband multi-frequency sweeps across 9 wafer points per temperature step (-50°C, 25°C, 85°C, 125°C) risks exceeding allocated tool metrology time budgets (estimated > 4.5 hours per wafer). Stage automation, triaxial soak stabilization times, and purge dry-air cycling must be rigorously optimized to prevent metrology bottlenecks from holding up the downstream metallization lot release.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Moisture condensation and frost formation on crown capacitor array test pads during sub-ambient (-50°C) testing due to inadequate dry N2/CDA chamber purge dew-point (< -70°C required), causing catastrophic electrical shorting and pad corrosion.
1. Parasitic series resistance roll-off and resonance artifacts at 1 MHz - 10 MHz from uncalibrated thermal chuck cabling, resulting in false apparent dielectric loss and miscalculated Equivalent Oxide Thickness (EOT).
1. Thermal-shock-induced dielectric micro-fracture or delamination of Ta2O5 from TiN/Al2O3 crown sidewalls during rapid chuck ramp (> 15°C/min), causing irreversible gate dielectric breakdown.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-2-01` | **Cryogenic to Elevated Thermal Multi-Frequency C-V Accumulation & Dispersion Mapping** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1520A Multi-Frequency CMU, MPI TS200-SE Thermal Triaxial Shielded Probe Station with Temptronic ThermoChuck (-65°C to 200°C), and Agilent 16442A Test Fixture. | 1. Load wafer onto thermal chuck and initiate N2 purge until ambient RH < 0.1% and dew point < -70°C. 2. Set chuck temperature to -50°C at ramp rate <= 10°C/min; soak for 15 minutes for thermal equilibrium. 3. Land triaxial probe tips on Crown capacitor test arrays (1000-cell array and single 1T1C test structures). 4. Execute wideband multi-frequency C-V sweep from -2.0 V to +2.0 V with AC excitation of 30 mV RMS across 1 kHz, 10 kHz, 100 kHz, 1 MHz, and 5 MHz. 5. Ramp chuck temperature sequentially to 25°C, 85°C, and 125°C with 10-minute soak at each plateau, repeating the multi-frequency C-V sweep at 9 dedicated wafer test sites per temperature. 6. Extract accumulation capacitance C_acc, flatband voltage V_fb, and frequency dispersion delta_C between 10 kHz and 1 MHz at each temperature. | `Cell equivalent capacitance C_cell >= 25.0 fF at 1.0 V accumulation across all temperatures (-50°C to 125°C) at 100 kHz. Frequency dispersion (C_10kHz - C_1MHz) / C_10kHz <= 4.5% at 25°C and <= 7.0% at 125°C across all 9 measured sites. Zero visual frost or condensation artifacts under 50x in-situ optics.` |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-2-02` | **Temperature-Dependent Interface Trap Density (Dit) and Conductance Dispersion Extraction** | Keysight B1500A (B1520A MFCMU + B1517A HRSMU), Cascade Summit 12000B semi-automated thermal probe station with low-noise triax shielding, Keysight Desktop EasyEXPERT software. | 1. Position probes onto designated Crown dielectric test capacitors (area = 10,000 um^2). 2. Stabilize chuck temperature at 25°C and 85°C. 3. Perform Conductance-Frequency (G-w/w vs log w) spectroscopy over a frequency range of 1 kHz to 5 MHz in steps of 10 mV from V_fb - 0.3 V to V_fb + 0.3 V (depletion region). 4. Record parallel conductance G_p and capacitance C_p. 5. Calculate normalized parallel conductance (G_p / w) vs frequency and extract interface trap density (Dit) via the Hill-Coleman / Nicollian-Goetzberger conductance peak method. | `Peak interface trap density Dit <= 2.5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2 at 25°C and <= 6.0e11 eV^-1 cm^-2 at 85°C. Dielectric loss tangent tan(delta) = G / (w * C) <= 0.015 at 100 kHz across the operational voltage window (-1.2 V to +1.2 V).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `High`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cryogenic safety gloves (EN 511 rated) for liquid nitrogen manifold handling, Thermal safety heat-resistant gloves (EN 407 rated for >= 150°C chuck handling), ANSI Z87.1 approved full-face shield and splash-resistant safety glasses, Cleanroom-compatible anti-static flame-retardant lab coat, Closed-toe ESD conductive safety shoes
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For cryogenic frostbite: Do NOT rub affected tissue. Immediately immerse area in warm water bath (38°C - 42°C) for at least 15-30 minutes until tissue softens and color returns. Seek emergency medical response immediately. For thermal burns: Cool immediately under sterile cold running water for 15 minutes; cover with dry, sterile, non-adherent dressing. For oxygen deficiency/asphyxiation from LN2 boil-off: Evacuate victim to fresh air immediately, administer oxygen if trained, and call emergency personnel.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom exhaust over the probe station enclosure providing >= 35 air changes per hour. Dedicated LN2 venting line routed to facility acid/inert exhaust stack. Ambient oxygen monitoring sensors (dual electrochemical sensors interlocked at 19.5% alarm and 18.0% immediate evacuation threshold with audible/visual sirens).
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: LN2 vapor safely routed and dispersed through facility cryogenic relief stack. Waste IPA used during chuck wipe-down collected in FM-approved dedicated solvent waste carboys and disposed of through certified hazardous solvent reclamation.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Liquid Nitrogen (Cryogenic Liquid)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 5.0 (99.999%) | `100%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas** | `7727-37-9` | Semiconductor Ultra-Pure VLSI Grade | `100%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA for chuck de-icing/cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | Electronic/MOS Grade | `99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-deposited and annealed Al2O3/Ta2O5 crown capacitor stack with patterned TiN/polysilicon top electrode pads; surface clean, free of organic residues, and desorbed of surface moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Moisture-free, uncorroded TiN contact pads with chuck thermal cycling complete; stored under dry N2 environment awaiting passivation/metallization-1.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Moisture absorption and atmospheric carbon contamination on exposed dielectric sidewalls and porous interfaces causing trap-assisted tunneling, uncontrolled EOT growth (> 0.2 nm), and premature dielectric breakdown during subsequent backend thermal cycles.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Complete multi-frequency wideband C-V and G-V dispersion profiling of the Gen 3 180nm Crown Al2O3/Ta2O5 capacitor arrays across the entire thermal envelope (-50°C to 125°C), verifying storage capacitance >= 25 fF/cell, extraction of Dit <= 2.5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2, and confirmation of negligible cryogenic/thermal trap-assisted dispersion.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `CV_GV_Dispersion_Matrix_Tminus50_to_T125.csv`
- [ ] `Crown_Dielectric_Dit_and_EOT_Thermal_Report.pdf`
- [ ] `Wafer9Pt_Capacitance_Uniformity_Map.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Equivalent single-cell crown storage capacitance C_cell at 1.0 V operating bias and 100 kHz across -50°C to 125°C** | `27.5 fF` | +/- 2.5 fF (Lower Spec Limit: 25.0 fF) | Keysight B1520A multi-frequency capacitance extraction normalized to single-cell area from 1000-cell Crown test array |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Accumulation frequency dispersion delta_C = (C_10kHz - C_1MHz) / C_10kHz at 25°C at 1.5 V** | `3.2%` | <= 4.5% | Multi-frequency C-V extraction on Keysight B1500A with open/short de-embedded triaxial calibration |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Interface trap state density Dit at mid-gap extracted via parallel conductance method at 25°C** | `1.8e11 eV^-1 cm^-2` | <= 2.5e11 eV^-1 cm^-2 | G-w/w conductance peak frequency-dispersion spectroscopy |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Full automated sign-off requires all 9 wafer sites across 4 temperature setpoints (-50°C, 25°C, 85°C, 125°C) to meet C_cell >= 25.0 fF, accumulation dispersion <= 4.5% at 25°C, dew-point log confirmed <= -70°C throughout testing, zero probe pad mechanical gouging exceeding 15% pad thickness, and engineering sign-off from both Metrology Lead and Integration Architect.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Sub-fA Temperature-Dependent I-V Dielectric Leakage & Frenkel-Poole Conduction Analysis

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-180-FP01`  
**Process Node:** 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Target Module:** Crown Capacitor MIM / High-$k$ ($\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$) Stack Qualification  

---

### Process Workflow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Wafer Mount and     │
│  Triaxial Guard Setup  │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Thermal Stage      │
│  Stabilization 25C to  │
│          85C           │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Sub-fA Low-Noise I-V  │
│    Sweep 0V to 1.8V    │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│     Frenkel-Poole      │
│  Extraction ln J over  │
│      E vs sqrt E       │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│      Leakage and       │
│    Retention Target    │
│     Qualification      │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 1. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

1. **Tool Setup & Triaxial Shielding Integration:**
   - Mount the 180nm wafer on a temperature-controlled thermal chuck inside a dark, electromagnetically shielded cryogenic/thermal probe station.
   - Connect the top electrode (MIM crown capacitor top plate) and bottom electrode (via W-plug drain contact pad) using driven-guard triaxial cabling directly interfaced to a sub-femtoampere Source Measure Unit (SMU).
   - Ensure cable noise floor and open-circuit residual leakage measure $< 0.1\text{ fA}$ at zero bias.

2. **Thermal Chuck Conditioning & Stabilization:**
   - Set the thermal chuck temperature controller to calibrate across the operational range: step from room temperature ($25^\circ\text{C}$) to standard worst-case retention specification temperature ($85^\circ\text{C}$).
   - Allow a minimum thermal dwell time of 10 minutes at each setpoint until chuck temperature variation is within $\pm 0.1^\circ\text{C}$.

3. **Sub-fA Low-Noise $I\text{-}V$ Quasi-Static Leakage Sweeps:**
   - Apply a stair-step DC voltage sweep across the $\text{Al}_2\text{O}_3/\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5$ capacitor dielectric from $V_{\text{app}} = 0.0\text{ V}$ to $1.8\text{ V}$ (nominal cell operating voltage) in increments of $20\text{ mV}$.
   - Set SMU integration aperture to $\ge 10\text{ PLC}$ (Power Line Cycles) with a delay time of $\ge 500\text{ ms}$ per step to bypass displacement charging currents and isolate true steady-state conduction.
   - Record current $I_{\text{leak}}$ versus applied bias across $25^\circ\text{C}$ and $85^\circ\text{C}$ runs.

4. **Conduction Mechanism & Frenkel-Poole Trap Extraction:**
   - Calculate current density $J = I_{\text{leak}} / A_{\text{eff}}$ using 3D crown capacitor effective surface area and electric field $E = V_{\text{app}} / t_{\text{phys}}$ (where dielectric physical thickness corresponds to Equivalent Oxide Thickness $\text{EOT} = 3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$ with high-$k$ relative permittivity $\kappa > 15$).
   - Construct Frenkel-Poole conduction plot: $\ln(J/E)$ as a function of $\sqrt{E}$.
   - From linear high-field region slope $\beta_{\text{FP}} = \frac{q}{k_B T}\sqrt{\frac{q}{\pi \epsilon_0 \epsilon_{\infty}}}$, extract high-frequency optical permittivity $\epsilon_{\infty}$ and trap energy depth $E_{\text{trap}}$ across the $25^\circ\text{C}\text{–}85^\circ\text{C}$ temperature matrix to verify trap-assisted Poole-Frenkel emission against thermionic/direct tunneling bounds.

---

### 2. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

```text
               ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐

   Ret@85C (ms)┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
               │▒▒                                     │
I_leak@85C (fA)┤▒▒                                     │
   EOT max (nm)┤▓▓▓                                    │
               │▓▓▓                                    │
C_cell min (fF)┤██████████████████                     │
               │██████████████████                     │

```

| Parameter Metric | Target Value | Physical Unit | Measurement Method / Condition |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Dielectric Leakage Current ($I_{\text{leak}}$)** | **$\le 1.0$** | **fA/cell** | At $85^\circ\text{C}$ chuck temperature, $V_{\text{app}} = 1.8\text{ V}$ bias |
| **Cell Storage Capacitance ($C_{\text{cell}}$)** | **$28\text{ to }30$** (Min: $\ge 25$) | **fF/cell** | Low-frequency $C\text{-}V$ extraction ($100\text{ kHz}$ to $1\text{ MHz}$) |
| **Equivalent Oxide Thickness ($\text{EOT}$)** | **$3.0\text{ to }4.0$** | **nm** | Extracted from high-$k$ stack with $\kappa > 15$ |
| **Data Retention Interval Time ($t_{\text{ret}}$)** | **$> 64$** | **ms** | Derived memory cell refresh time at $85^\circ\text{C}$ |

---

### 3. Literature Citations & Physical Reference

- **[1] 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench:**
  - *Context:* Access transistor channel $L = 180\text{ nm}$, $W = 220\text{ nm}$; crown-shaped MIM capacitor contacted via tungsten plug (W-plug); high-$k$ dielectric stack ($\text{Ta}_2\text{O}_5 / \text{Al}_2\text{O}_3$) providing effective dielectric constant $\kappa > 15$; minimum cell capacitance budget of $28\text{ fF/cell}$; leakage current requirement of $< 1\text{ fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.
- **[2] Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering:**
  - *Context:* 1T1C stacked capacitor architecture ($8F^2 / 6F^2$); storage capacitance budget of $25\text{ to }30\text{ fF/cell}$; equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) target of $3\text{ to }4\text{ nm}$; retention time requirement $> 64\text{ ms}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Measuring sub-fA current levels (target <1.0 fA/cell at 85°C, equivalent to <3.57e-14 A for a 1000-cell parallel test array or 0.1 fA single-crown resolution) is severely constrained by thermal chuck Johnson-Nyquist noise, triaxial cable triboelectric effects, and chuck displacement currents during temperature ramps. Direct SMU triaxial guard tracing must be maintained up to within 1 mm of the beryllium copper probe tip, and settling times must exceed 15 seconds per voltage step (dV/dt < 5 mV/s) to isolate leakage from dielectric displacement currents (I_disp = C * dV/dt).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At electric fields between 1.0 MV/cm and 3.5 MV/cm across the Al2O3/Ta2O5 crown nanolaminate dielectric, Poole-Frenkel (PF) emission is the dominant conduction mechanism: ln(J/E) vs E^(1/2) must yield linear Arrhenius characteristics yielding a trap depth Phi_t in the range of 1.2 eV to 1.5 eV. Deviation from linearity at low fields (<0.8 MV/cm) indicates Ohmic or trap-assisted tunneling (TAT) mediated by oxygen vacancies in the Ta2O5 sub-layer, whereas steep exponential deviation at >4.0 MV/cm indicates Fowler-Nordheim tunneling pre-breakdown, which degrades the 64 ms DRAM retention refresh interval.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-low-noise triaxial probe cards, guarded thermal chuck stages capable of -40°C to +125°C stabilization with dry N2 continuous purge (<5 ppm moisture), and sub-femtoamp electrometer SMUs (e.g., Keysight B1500A with HRSMU/WGFMU or Keithley 4200A-SCS with 4201-SMU PreAmp) face long import procurement lead times (16-24 weeks in VN regional fabs). Spare triaxial low-noise cables (model Keithley 237-ALG-2) and beryllium copper tips (radius < 5 um) must be pre-stocked.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterization throughput is the primary bottleneck: temperature ramping from 25°C to 85°C and 125°C with 30-minute thermal stabilization per wafer and 100-point fine voltage sweeps at 15 s/pt requires >4.5 hours per test vehicle die. The metrology run must prioritize a 5-point wafer sampling plan (Center, North, South, East, West) rather than full-wafer mapping to meet the Gen-3 MPW tapeout milestone.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Chuck thermal drift and thermal expansion mismatch shearing or lifting probe tips off the 50x50 um crown MIM test pads during 25°C to 125°C ramps, causing catastrophic open-circuits or false sub-fA readings.
1. Moisture condensation and frost formation on the wafer surface when cooling below dew point or during thermal cycling, producing surface parasitic leakage paths in the picoamp to nanoamp range that obscure true bulk dielectric Poole-Frenkel conduction.
1. Dielectric soft breakdown (B-mode degradation) during high-temperature (125°C) positive bias stress sweeps (>1.8V), permanently creating percolation leakage paths through oxygen vacancy chains in the Ta2O5 film.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-3-01` | **Sub-fA Temperature-Dependent (25°C-125°C) I-V Leakage Density Characterization** | Keysight B1500A Semiconductor Device Analyzer with B1517A High Resolution SMU (HRSMU) and ASU (Atto-Sense and Switch Unit), Cascade Microtech Summit 12000 Semi-Automatic Probe Station with Temptronic ThermoChuck (-65°C to 200°C, dry N2 purged enclosure, triaxial shield, chuck guarded). | 1. Set thermal chuck temperature to 25.0°C +/- 0.1°C; soak for 15 minutes. 2. Apply voltage bias from 0.0 V to +1.8 V in 20 mV increments across bottom TiN and top TiN electrodes with 10.0 s integration/settling delay per step (PLC=10, Medium filter). 3. Measure leakage current I_leak. 4. Ramp chuck to 85.0°C +/- 0.1°C at 5°C/min; soak 20 minutes; repeat voltage sweep. 5. Ramp chuck to 125.0°C +/- 0.1°C at 5°C/min; soak 20 minutes; repeat voltage sweep. 6. Normalize measured current to single-cell equivalent (I_cell = I_meas / 1000) and current density J = I_meas / A_eff. | `Single-cell normalized leakage current at V_cell = 0.9 V (half VDD) must be: I_cell <= 0.08 fA at 25°C; I_cell <= 0.85 fA at 85°C (DRAM retention target <= 1.0 fA); and I_cell <= 8.0 fA at 125°C across all 5 test die locations.` |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-1-3-3-3-02` | **Frenkel-Poole Conduction Modeling & Trap Depth (Phi_t) Extraction** | Keysight B1500A HRSMU, Cryogenic/Thermal Chuck System, Python/MATLAB curve extraction pipeline for Poole-Frenkel fitting: ln(J/E) = q/(k*T) * (sqrt(q*E / (pi*eps_0*eps_opt))) - q*Phi_t/(k*T) + C. | 1. Compute electric field E = V_bias / d_phys for each bias point between 1.0 MV/cm and 3.0 MV/cm. 2. Transform (J, E, T) dataset into Poole-Frenkel coordinates: plot ln(J/E) versus sqrt(E). 3. Perform linear least-squares regression over the range 1.2 MV/cm <= E <= 2.8 MV/cm for each temperature. 4. Extract slope S(T) = (q / (k*T)) * sqrt(q / (pi * eps_0 * eps_opt)) to calculate optical dielectric constant eps_opt (refractive index n = sqrt(eps_opt)). 5. Construct Arrhenius plot of the intercept ln(J/E)|_(E->0) versus 1000/T. 6. Extract trap depth activation energy q*Phi_t from the Arrhenius slope. | `Poole-Frenkel linear regression fit R^2 >= 0.985 in the range 1.2 to 2.8 MV/cm across all temperatures; extracted optical dielectric constant eps_opt within 4.2 to 5.5 (consistent with Ta2O5 refractive index n ~ 2.1-2.3); extracted trap energy depth Phi_t must be between 1.25 eV and 1.48 eV.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Thermal-insulating cryo/heat-resistant gloves (rated -50°C to +150°C), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact safety glasses with side shields, Class 100 cleanroom ESD-safe nitrile gloves (double gloving), Static-dissipative cleanroom smock and grounded ESD wrist strap (1 MOhm resistor)
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Thermal burns from hot chuck contact: immediately flush affected skin with cool, clean water for at least 15 minutes; do not apply ice directly; cover with sterile non-adherent dressing. Simple asphyxiation hazard from N2 purge enclosure leak: evacuate personnel to fresh air immediately; initiate artificial respiration or supplemental oxygen if breathing is labored; alert emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous probe chamber nitrogen exhaust routed directly to facility non-hazardous acid/solvent exhaust plenum (minimum exhaust face velocity 0.5 m/s, minimum 60 SCFH dry N2 flow rate during heating/cooling cycles). Ambient O2 room deficiency monitoring with audible alarms set at < 19.5% O2.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA wipes must be collected in closed, fire-resistant, grounded stainless-steel flammables bins and disposed of via hazardous solvent waste stream. No liquid chemical effluent generated during dry electrical metrology.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Ultra-High Purity purge gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100.0%` |
| **Isopropyl Alcohol (IPA, stage and optics cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/MOS Electronic Grade | `>= 99.8%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly completed top-electrode TiN/Al contact pad metallization and post-metallization forming gas anneal (FGA, 400°C 30 min in 5% H2 / 95% N2), pristine hydrophobic passivated surface free of organic residue.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Tested crown MIM pads with probe micro-scrub marks (<5 um lateral scrub mark length), desiccated under continuous dry N2, ready for inter-metal dielectric (IMD-1) deposition.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exposure to ambient air moisture > 30 minutes induces hydroxyl (-OH) chemisorption on top TiN/Al pad sidewalls and pinhole moisture ingress into the crown high-k stack, causing parasitic surface conduction, trap state generation (reducing extracted Phi_t), and false-positive dielectric leakage > 1 fA/cell.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Verified sub-fA temperature-dependent leakage profile (25°C to 125°C) and confirmed Poole-Frenkel trap conduction mechanism for 180nm crown capacitor Al2O3/Ta2O5 MIM stack, proving compliance with the 180nm DRAM refresh retention limit (<1 fA/cell at 85°C at VDD/2).

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `TC_CROWN_ALD_180NM_IV_TEMP_RAW_DATA.csv`
- [ ] `FRENKEL_POOLE_CONDUCTION_EXTRACTION_REPORT.pdf`
- [ ] `PROBE_SCRUB_ALIGNMENT_VERIFICATION_MAP.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Single-cell equivalent leakage current at 85°C chuck temperature under 0.9V bias** | `0.75 fA/cell` | <= 1.00 fA/cell | Keysight B1500A HRSMU 1000-cell array measurement normalized by 1/1000 with noise subtraction |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Poole-Frenkel conduction trap depth (Phi_t) in Al2O3/Ta2O5 high-k stack** | `1.35 eV` | +/- 0.10 eV | Arrhenius slope linear regression of ln(J/E) vs 1000/T between 1.2 MV/cm and 2.8 MV/cm (R^2 >= 0.985) |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Room temperature (25°C) dielectric breakdown field (E_BD) under forward bias** | `4.80 MV/cm` | >= 4.20 MV/cm | Ramped voltage stress (RVS) sweep to breakdown limit defined at J_leak = 1.0 mA/cm^2 |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Researcher exit approval requires all 5 die locations to demonstrate single-cell leakage <= 1.0 fA at 85°C/0.9V, extracted Poole-Frenkel trap activation energy within [1.25 eV, 1.48 eV], linear regression R^2 >= 0.985, and zero probe-scrub damage punch-through verified by post-test optical microscopy.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Conformal CVD/ALD TiN Top Metal Electrode Deposition

**Category**: Thin Film Deposition | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Thermal budget integration is the dominant bottleneck. Sintering or depositing TiN above 450°C risks crystallizing high-k gate/capacitor oxides (e.g., Al2O3/HfO2) and causing excessive interdiffusion or cracking at the bottom electrode interface. Furthermore, residual chlorine (Cl) from TiCl4 precursors must be kept below 0.5 at.% to prevent bitline corrosion and gate leakage degradation during back-end-of-line (BEOL) processing.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Achieving true conformal coverage (>95%) across 3D high-aspect-ratio crown capacitor cavities (aspect ratio >= 12:1 in 180nm DRAM node) necessitates an optimized ALD cycle regime rather than line-of-sight CVD. Precursor pulse and purge durations must be sufficiently prolonged to avoid parasitic gas-phase CVD reactions, prevent premature pinch-off at the crown neck, and control mechanical stress to prevent crown capacitor structural peeling or micro-collapsing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Ultra-high purity Titanium Tetrachloride (TiCl4, 99.999%) and anhydrous NH3 (6N5) require specialized hazardous gas delivery manifolds, heated liquid delivery bubblers, and stringent secondary containment. Lead times for semi-spec hazardous precursor delivery vessels and mass flow verification modules currently exceed 16-20 weeks, presenting a schedule gating item for physical pilot runs in Vietnam.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Module turnaround time (TAT) is constrained by lengthy ALD pulse-purge cycles required for deep crown trenches (approx. 40-60 min per 25-wafer batch for 20-30nm TiN target). Throughput must be balanced against maintenance cycles: TiCl4 byproduct NH4Cl solid salt deposits rapidly clog vacuum forelines and exhaust throttle valves, dictating scheduled foreline bakeouts every 150 process runs to avoid unscheduled tool downtime.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Keyhole voiding and crown neck pinch-off caused by incomplete precursor diffusion and surface saturation inside high-aspect-ratio 3D crown capacitor structures.
1. High dielectric leakage and capacitance loss caused by chlorine contaminant segregation (Cl > 1.0 at.%) and interface oxidation during precursor dosing.
1. Mechanical film delamination and crown pillar tipping/collapse induced by excessive intrinsic tensile stress (> 1.5 GPa) of the deposited TiN top electrode.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-2-01` | **Conformality and Step Coverage Verification of TiN Top Electrode in High-Aspect-Ratio Crown** | High-Resolution Field Emission Scanning Electron Microscopy (FE-SEM) / Cross-Sectional Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) with Focused Ion Beam (FIB) sample prep | 1. Load wafer into ALD loadlock and transfer to deposition chamber under N2 purge. 2. Execute 350 cycles of alternating TiCl4 (0.8s pulse, 4.0s N2 purge) and NH3 (1.2s pulse, 5.0s N2 purge) at 400°C and 1.5 Torr. 3. Unload wafer to FOUP under continuous N2 overpressure. 4. Prepare cross-sectional sample at the center and wafer edge using dual-beam FIB. 5. Acquire HR-TEM images of the crown top lip, sidewall midpoint, and bottom base; measure TiN film thickness at each location. | `Step coverage ratio (t_bottom / t_top and t_sidewall / t_top) >= 95.0%; absolute TiN thickness = 25.0 nm ± 2.0 nm; zero keyhole voids or discontinuity along crown sidewalls.` |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-2-02` | **Sheet Resistance and Residual Chlorine Content Characterization** | Four-Point Probe (4PP) Resistivity Mapping System & X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) / Secondary Ion Mass Spectrometry (SIMS) | 1. Perform 49-point automated sheet resistance (R_s) map using Four-Point Probe across 200mm monitor wafer with 3mm edge exclusion. 2. Calculate mean sheet resistance and across-wafer 1-sigma uniformity. 3. Transfer wafer coupon into ultra-high vacuum XPS chamber (base pressure < 5x10^-9 Torr). 4. Sputter clean surface with 1 keV Ar+ beam for 30s to remove adventitious carbon. 5. Acquire core-level spectra for Ti 2p, N 1s, O 1s, and Cl 2p; quantify atomic concentrations using sensitivity factors. | `Mean sheet resistance R_s <= 80.0 Ohm/sq with 1-sigma non-uniformity <= 3.0%; residual chlorine concentration [Cl] < 0.5 at.%; stoichiometric ratio N/Ti between 0.95 and 1.05.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Level B/C chemical apron and full-face respirator with multi-gas/vapor/acid gas P100 cartridge during maintenance, Dual-layer chemical gloves (Butyl outer glove over Nitrile inner glove), Safety goggles with side shields conforming to ANSI Z87.1, Electrostatic dissipative cleanroom booties and antistatic bunny suit
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: In case of skin/eye contact with TiCl4 or acid byproducts: immediately flush with copious amounts of tempered water for at least 15 minutes at nearest emergency shower/eyewash station while removing contaminated garments. Do not apply neutralizing chemical agents to skin. Inhalation: evacuate victim to fresh air, administer humidified oxygen if breathing is difficult, keep warm and at rest, and immediately transfer to emergency medical center with SDS documentation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated corrosive acid/toxic exhaust ducting maintained under negative pressure (static pressure differential <= -0.75 in. w.g.); continuous toxic gas monitoring system (TGMS) with electrochemical sensors calibrated for HCl (< 5 ppm alarm) and NH3 (< 25 ppm alarm) positioned at gas cabinet, valve manifold box (VMB), and vacuum pump enclosure; dry mechanical pump equipped with heated N2 ballast.

High-temperature oxidation decomposes volatile metal chlorides and unreacted ammonia, followed by counter-current packed-bed aqueous caustic (NaOH) scrubbing to neutralize HCl exhaust down to < 1 ppm before municipal air release. | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly deposited and post-annealed capacitor high-k dielectric (Al2O3/ZrO2); chemically clean, hydroxyl-terminated surface free of airborne molecular organic contaminants (VOCs) and particle defects.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Successful baseline qualification and physical signoff of the Conformal ALD TiN Top Metal Electrode Deposition process on 3D high-aspect-ratio (12:1) crown capacitors for the 180nm Open-Source DRAM node, verifying conformal step coverage >= 95%, low resistivity, low residual chlorine, and pinhole-free interface integrity.

| `ASSERT-02` | **Residual chlorine concentration in bulk TiN film** | `0.30 at.%` | <= 0.50 at.% | High-Resolution X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) depth profile and SIMS calibrated against standard reference |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Mean sheet resistance of 25nm TiN film** | `72.0 Ohm/sq` | <= 80.0 Ohm/sq (1-sigma non-uniformity <= 3.0%) | Standard 49-point automated Four-Point Probe resistivity mapping with 3mm edge exclusion |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:

critics.systems_engineer: Thermal budget integration is the dominant bottleneck. Sintering or depositing TiN above 450°C risks crystallizing high-k gate/capacitor oxides (e.g., Al2O3/HfO2) and causing excessive interdiffusion or cracking at the bottom electrode interface. Furthermore, residual chlorine (Cl) from TiCl4 precursors must be kept below 0.5 at.% to prevent bitline corrosion and gate leakage degradation during back-end-of-line (BEOL) processing.
critics.domain_expert: Achieving true conformal coverage (>95%) across 3D high-aspect-ratio crown capacitor cavities (aspect ratio >= 12:1 in 180nm DRAM node) necessitates an optimized ALD cycle regime rather than line-of-sight CVD. Precursor pulse and purge durations must be sufficiently prolonged to avoid parasitic gas-phase CVD reactions, prevent premature pinch-off at the crown neck, and control mechanical stress to prevent crown capacitor structural peeling or micro-collapsing.
critics.supply_chain: Ultra-high purity Titanium Tetrachloride (TiCl4, 99.999%) and anhydrous NH3 (6N5) require specialized hazardous gas delivery manifolds, heated liquid delivery bubblers, and stringent secondary containment. Lead times for semi-spec hazardous precursor delivery vessels and mass flow verification modules currently exceed 16-20 weeks, presenting a schedule gating item for physical pilot runs in Vietnam.
critics.laya_pm: Module turnaround time (TAT) is constrained by lengthy ALD pulse-purge cycles required for deep crown trenches (approx. 40-60 min per 25-wafer batch for 20-30nm TiN target). Throughput must be balanced against maintenance cycles: TiCl4 byproduct NH4Cl solid salt deposits rapidly clog vacuum forelines and exhaust throttle valves, dictating scheduled foreline bakeouts every 150 process runs to avoid unscheduled tool downtime.

nodes.sop_content:
# Standard Operating Procedure: Crown Capacitor Pre-Clean and ALD TiN Surface Degas/Precursor Balancing

**Category**: Wet Chemistry | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Integration of the RCA pre-clean wet bench with the ALD TiN cluster tool requires strict automation of transfer logistics to mitigate native oxide regrowth and moisture physisorption inside 3D high-aspect-ratio (HAR 12:1 to 15:1) crown capacitor cylinders. If the degas profile in the ALD loadlock/degas chamber fails to completely desorb interfacial hydroxyl (-OH) groups and capillary-condensed water before TiCl4/NH3 pulse introduction, uncontrolled CVD-mode parasitical reactions will induce localized pinholes, non-uniform film nucleation, and Cl- contamination at the bottom electrode interface.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Capillary forces in deep cylindrical crown nodes require strict Marangoni or IPA vapor drying post SC-2/DHF rinse; standard spin-rinse dryers create surface tension gradients that cause mechanical collapse or pattern stiction of free-standing crown cylinders. Furthermore, during ALD surface degas, vacuum bake must be precisely tuned to 250°C-300°C under ultra-high-purity N2 sweep to prevent parasitic TiOxNy interfacial formation prior to precursor dosing, balancing the steric hindrance and saturation time of TiCl4 in aspect ratios exceeding 10:1.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Electronic-grade UPW (18.2 MOhm-cm, TOC < 1 ppb) and semiconductor-grade (SEMI Tier 5 / Megabit Grade) NH4OH, HCl, H2O2, and aqueous HF must be continuously qualified with strict lot-to-lot trace-metal certificates (< 10 ppt Fe, Cu, Ni). In addition, optical/bubbler sources for anhydrous TiCl4 and UHP 99.9999% NH3 require dedicated dual-canister manifolds with automated purge loops to avoid delivery bottlenecks and supply disruptions across multi-wafer MPW lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Module cycle time for wet bench pre-clean, Marangoni dry, vacuum loadlock transfer, and pre-heat degas must be scheduled tightly within a 45-minute window per lot to avoid bottlenecking the shared ALD deposition cluster. Any recipe abort or extended Q-time violation necessitates a costly re-clean loop, risking crown capacitor sidewall thinning, oxide re-etch budget loss, and gate oxide integrity degradation.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Capillary-induced crown capacitor wall pattern collapse/stiction during wet chemical rinse and standard centrifugal drying due to unoptimized surface tension.
1. Uncontrolled gas-phase CVD parasitic reaction inside the high-aspect-ratio cylinder caused by residual trapped moisture/hydroxyls, causing severe TiN thickness non-uniformity and particulate generation.
1. Residual halogen/chloride (Cl-) trapping and native TiO2/SiOx interfacial layer growth resulting in high equivalent oxide thickness (EOT) and excessive dielectric leakage current.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-2-1-01` | **Post-Clean Interfacial Metallic Contamination & Native Oxide Thickness Verification** | Total Reflection X-Ray Fluorescence (TXRF) spectrometer and spectroscopic ellipsometer (SE) with focused micro-spot optics. | 1. Transfer wafer within 15 minutes of Marangoni drying to cleanroom TXRF load port under class 1 laminar flow hood. 2. Execute 9-point surface scan across wafer diameter to quantify Fe, Cu, Ni, and Zn surface metal concentrations. 3. Transfer to spectroscopic ellipsometer and measure remaining native oxide thickness at 13 sites across the wafer. | `Surface metallic impurities (Fe, Cu, Ni, Zn) must each be <= 1.0E+10 atoms/cm2; residual native oxide thickness must be <= 0.30 nm (equivalent to a clean hydrophobic H-terminated surface).` |
| `TC-CROWN-ALD-MODULE-2-1-02` | **In-Situ Degas Desorption Efficiency & Precursor Saturation Balancing Test** | In-situ Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA, quadrupole mass spectrometer) attached to ALD loadlock/degas chamber and Cross-Sectional TEM/EDS. | 1. Monitor RGA mass channels m/z 18 (H2O), m/z 17 (OH), and m/z 28 (N2/CO) during a 10-minute degas cycle until partial pressure of m/z 18 drops below threshold. 2. Transfer in-vacuo to ALD reaction chamber and run 15 test cycles of TiCl4 (0.8s pulse / 5s N2 purge) and NH3 (1.2s pulse / 6s N2 purge). 3. Unload wafer, cleave, and perform cross-sectional TEM/EDS from top rim to bottom floor of crown cylinders. | `H2O partial pressure on RGA must reach <= 5.0E-8 Torr prior to chamber transfer; TEM/EDS step coverage of initial TiN seed layer must be >= 95% from top to bottom of the 12:1 HAR cylinder with atomic Cl concentration <= 0.8 at%.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Critical`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Acid- and base-resistant neoprene/butyl rubber dual-layer gloves over nitrile examination gloves, Chemical splash face shield complying with ANSI Z87.1 paired with chemical splash goggles, Full-body acid/chemical splash apron with integrated sleeves, Safety toe boots with chemical-resistant neoprene overboots, Calibrated portable HF/Cl2 gas detector badge
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For Hydrofluoric Acid exposure: Immediately flush affected skin area with copious cold water for 2-3 minutes, followed by continuous massage of Calcium Gluconate Gel (2.5%) into the dermal site until medical care arrives. In case of ocular exposure, irrigate immediately with sterile 1% calcium gluconate eye wash or normal saline for at least 15 minutes. For TiCl4 exposure, avoid immediate high-pressure water contact if pure liquid pool forms due to exothermic violent hydrolysis producing HCl gas; isolate, blot gently, and flush with low-pressure water while providing oxygen for vapor inhalation.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated segregated wet bench exhaust: Acid/HF exhaust plenum maintained at static negative pressure of -1.5 to -2.0 in. w.g. with continuous scrubbed acidic exhaust ducting; alkaline SC-1 exhaust routed through dedicated ammonia scrubber line. ALD gas cabinet and vacuum pump effluent connected to high-efficiency point-of-use thermal/wet toxic gas burn-box scrubbers with minimum face velocity of 120 fpm at cabinet louvers.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Segregated fluorinated (HF) waste stream plumbed to automated fluoride precipitation system using calcium hydroxide (Ca(OH)2) forming insoluble CaF2 cake. General acid/base effluent routed to two-stage continuous pH equalization tank neutralized with 10% NaOH / 10% H2SO4 to maintain pH between 6.5 and 8.5 before permitted POTW discharge.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Hydrofluoric Acid (Aqueous)** | `7664-39-3` | SEMI C12 Tier 5 (Megabit/Giga Grade) | `0.5% - 2.0% wt (1:50 dilution)` |
| **Hydrochloric Acid** | `7647-01-0` | SEMI C8 Tier 5 | `37% wt` |
| **Ammonium Hydroxide** | `1336-21-6` | SEMI C7 Tier 5 | `29% wt` |
| **Hydrogen Peroxide** | `7722-84-1` | SEMI C9 Tier 5 | `30% wt` |
| **Titanium Tetrachloride** | `7550-45-0` | Electronic Grade (99.999% trace metals) | `100% anhydrous liquid` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: As-etched and ash-stripped silicon/polysilicon crown capacitor cylindrical 3D structures with fluorocarbon polymer residue and non-uniform native oxide (1.2 - 2.0 nm).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Atomically clean, particle-free, fully hydrogen-passivated (hydrophobic) and thermally degassed surface ready for immediate ALD TiN chemisorption.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding the 30-minute cleanroom air Q-time induces spontaneous atmospheric moisture adsorption and uncontrolled native oxide re-oxidation (> 0.5 nm), degrading cell capacitance by > 15% and increasing bottom-electrode contact resistance.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full completion and sign-off of the Crown Capacitor Pre-Clean and ALD TiN surface conditioning process, delivering particle-free, pristine, low-defect capacitor nodes with complete precursor balancing in deep 3D aspect ratios ready for top electrode encapsulation.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `DRAM180_CROWN_PRECLEAN_TXRF_REPORT.csv`
- [ ] `ALD_TIN_DEGAS_RGA_SPECTRUM_LOG.pdf`
- [ ] `CROWN_CAP_POST_CLEAN_CROSS_SECTION_TEM.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Post-SC-1/HF/SC-2 clean surface transition metals (Fe, Ni, Cu)** | `1.0E+10 atoms/cm2` | Maximum upper bound <= 1.0E+10 atoms/cm2 | TXRF 9-point surface measurement |
| `ASSERT-02` | **ALD degas chamber residual moisture partial pressure prior to TiCl4 dosing** | `5.0E-8 Torr` | Maximum upper bound <= 5.0E-8 Torr | In-situ quadrupole Residual Gas Analyzer (RGA) tracking m/z 18 |
| `ASSERT-03` | **ALD TiN seed layer bottom-to-top step coverage inside 12:1 crown capacitor cylinders** | `98%` | +/- 2% | High-Resolution Cross-Sectional TEM metrology at bottom, middle, and top of capacitor cylinder |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Zero structural pattern collapse across all crown test arrays verified via top-down tilt SEM, TXRF metal impurity sum <= 3.0E+10 atoms/cm2, RGA moisture baseline <= 5.0E-8 Torr, and formal approval by both Nanofabrication Lead and Process Integration Manager.
