### 4. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria

| Metric Identifier | Parameter Description | Target Specification | Physical Units | Evaluation Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **AC-CD-01** | Corrected Gate Critical Dimension ($CD_0$) | $180.0 \pm 5.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Extrapolated SE profile at zero dose ($N=0$) |
| **AC-PITCH-02** | Array Wordline Gate Pitch | $360.0 \text{ to } 400.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Multi-line pitch verification |
| **AC-SHRINK-03** | Max E-Beam Induced Shrinkage ($\Delta CD_{64}$) | $\le 4.5$ | $\text{nm}$ | $|CD_0 - CD(64\text{ frames})|$ |
| **AC-UNIF-04** | Across-Wafer Gate CD Uniformity ($3\sigma$) | $\le 6.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | 13-site full wafer statistical distribution |

---

### 5. Verified Literature Citations

- **Source 1: 180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
  - *Context:* Defined unit cell geometry: access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$ and width $W = 220\text{ nm}$ with stacked capacitor over bitline layout.
- **Source 2: Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
  - *Context:* Verified wordline and bitline pitch range ($360\text{ nm} \text{ to } 400\text{ nm}$) and thermal dry $\text{SiO}_2$ gate dielectric physical thickness ($\sim 3.5\text{ nm}$).
- **Source 3: High-Voltage Wordline Charge Pump (VPP) Dickson Oscillator Architecture**
  - *Context:* Wordline drive voltage dynamics and NMOS threshold voltage constraints ($V_{\text{th}} \sim 0.5\text{V} - 0.7\text{V}$) necessitating tight gate CD control to prevent sub-threshold leakage exceeding $1\text{ fA/cell}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: In-line gate CD extraction at the 180nm node must balance electron-dose-induced charging against measurement signal-to-noise ratio (SNR). EBDW resists (e.g., HSQ or chemically amplified resists like UV6/ZEP520A) deposited over ultrathin 3.5nm–7.0nm thermal gate oxide on Si substrates accumulate negative space charge when secondary electron yield eta + delta < 1 under landing energies exceeding E2 (~800 eV). This surface charging deflects the primary electron probe, introducing artificial spatial distortions, edge-blooming, and perceived CD shrinkage. The metrology pipeline must decouple electrostatic beam deflection from physical resist polymer shrinkage (scission/crosslinking compaction) to avoid corrupting feed-forward process control into reactive ion etching (RIE).
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Electron beam exposure during automated multi-site CD-SEM scanning initiates both chemical scission/crosslinking shrinkage and localized electrostatic repelling. For 180nm polysilicon gate mandrels, repetitive electron dose scanning creates a characteristic exponential shrinkage curve: CD(D) = CD_inf + (CD_0 - CD_inf)*exp(-D/D_0). Without a multi-frame dynamic shrinkage extrapolation algorithm calculating zero-dose physical CD (CD_0), systematic measurement offsets of 3 nm to 8 nm will skew pass-transistor threshold voltage (V_th) distributions, directly degrading pass-gate drive current and wordline boost overdrive margin (V_PP overdrive) in Dickson charge pump circuits.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-supplier lock-in for certified low-voltage CD-SEM calibration pitch standards (such as VLSI Standards NanoCD or SwissLitho 100nm pitch standards) poses lead-time risks of 16 to 24 weeks. Wafer-level charging compensation units (e.g., localized gas-injection charge neutralizing systems or flood-gun modules) require specialized consumables and vendor-proprietary autofocus targets. Domestic second-sourcing of sub-nanometer reference standards and qualification of open-source automated edge-detection algorithms (such as threshold/maximum-derivative vs. model-based library matching) are critical to ensure tool-independent verification across foundry lots.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Automated in-line CD extraction and shrinkage modeling directly gate lot release between EBDW develop-inspect (ADI) and poly etch-inspect (AEI). Unmitigated charging artifacts cause false-alarm excursions that stall the pilot line by >12 hours per wafer lot. Metrology cycle times must be constrained to under 45 seconds per site across a 9-point wafer map, and recipe parameters (landing energy, beam current, dwell time) must be locked to prevent throughput degradation while preserving statistical repeatability across 180nm DRAM prototype runs.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron-beam charging-induced edge bloom: Localized negative charge accumulation on ungrounded gate resist structures deflects secondary electrons, causing an apparent line expansion or loss of edge contrast that leads to automated algorithm measurement aborts.
1. Polymer resist radiation compaction: High electron dose density (>2.5 uC/cm2) triggers excessive carbon-chain scission and densification, shrinking the physical gate resist line by >5 nm and permanently biasing the subsequent reactive ion etch profile.
1. Autofocus hysteresis and image drift: Surface potential buildup alters the focal plane of the immersion objective lens, causing z-axis focus hunting, prolonged site dwell times, and intensified localized charging.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-2-3-01` | **Multi-Frame Beam Dose Shrinkage Curve Extraction & Zero-Dose CD Extrapolation** | Automated In-Line Cold Field-Emission CD-SEM (Hitachi S-9380 / Applied Materials VeritySEM or equivalent) with beam deceleration and multi-frame line capture capability; offline CD data analysis engine. | 1. Load wafer into CD-SEM loadlock and align on global wafer alignment targets. 2. Navigate automated stage to 9 predetermined die locations across the wafer (center, inner ring, outer ring). 3. At each site, acquire 16 sequential image frames of a 180nm nominal isolated and dense gate resist line using 500 eV landing energy, 512x512 pixel resolution, 100 nm field of view, and 100 ns pixel dwell time without stage movement. 4. Extract the line edge positions and compute the mean critical dimension (CD) for each individual frame (frames 1 through 16). 5. Fit the sequential 16-frame CD measurements to the exponential radiation shrinkage model: CD(N) = CD_inf + (CD_0 - CD_inf)*exp(-N/N_0), where N is frame index. 6. Extrapolate to compute the true unperturbed zero-dose critical dimension (CD_0) and compute the shrinkage rate parameter delta_CD = CD_1 - CD_16. | `Zero-dose extrapolated critical dimension CD_0 must measure 180.0 nm +/- 5.0 nm across all 9 dies. Total shrinkage magnitude from Frame 1 to Frame 16 (delta_CD) must not exceed 4.0 nm. Regression coefficient of determination (R^2) for the exponential shrinkage fit must be >= 0.980.` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-2-3-02` | **Low-Landing-Energy Surface Charging Potential & Edge-Blooming Verification** | Low-voltage CD-SEM equipped with secondary electron energy spectrometer / retarding field analyzer and automated 50% threshold edge-detection software. | 1. Position beam over dedicated isolated 180nm gate resist test structures surrounded by large unpatterned thermal oxide fields. 2. Step landing energy through 300 eV, 500 eV, and 800 eV. 3. At each landing energy, capture high-resolution secondary electron (SE) intensity profiles across the gate line and calculate the left-to-right peak-to-baseline contrast ratio (SNR). 4. Measure the apparent CD change across a 30-second continuous stationary field irradiation (dwell stress test). 5. Compute surface potential shift Delta_V_surf via secondary electron energy distribution peak shift relative to grounded substrate. | `Apparent CD variation due to electrostatic charging distortion during 30s dwell stress test must be <= 2.5 nm at 500 eV landing energy. Surface potential shift Delta_V_surf must remain within -1.5 V to +0.5 V. Edge-blooming contrast degradation must not exceed 10% relative to baseline.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom compatible nitrile gloves (double-gloved, ESD-safe), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/radiation safety glasses, ESD cleanroom gowning with conductive footwear and grounding wrist strap
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin exposure to IPA: Wash affected area immediately with mild soap and copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes; remove contaminated cleanroom attire. Eye contact: Flush eyes immediately at eyewash station for 15 minutes holding eyelids open; seek immediate ophthalmological attention. High-voltage interlock trip / electrical shock: De-energize high-voltage power rack (20kV column supply) via emergency machine off (EMO); initiate CPR if pulse absent; call emergency response team immediately. Inhalation of nitrogen asphyxiant: Evacuate victim to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing is labored.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cleanroom recirculating laminar flow air handling units maintaining ISO Class 4 (FED-STD-209E Class 10); dedicated turbo-molecular vacuum pump roughing line exhaust ducted directly to acid/solvent fab exhaust scrubber; oxygen depletion sensors with audio/visual strobe alarms set at 19.5% O2 threshold inside CD-SEM equipment bay.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Solvent wipes and lint-free swabs saturated with IPA must be collected in dedicated airtight, antistatic, red hazardous solvent waste cans grounded to earth. Vacuum pump oils and cleaning effluents must be segregated into organic solvent waste barrels for certified incineration; no direct chemical drain disposal permitted.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, optical lens and wafer back cleaning)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI/Electronic Grade (SEMI C12) | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (N2, carrier/vent gas)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity Grade 6.0 (99.9999%) | `100%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Post-EBDW developer rinse and spin-dry; clean crosslinked resist lines on pristine 3.5nm thermal gate oxide; free of water marks, developer scum, or airborne particulate contamination.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Inspected gate resist features; non-destructive electron-dosed sites marked; surface electrostatic charge neutralized via N2 ionization or stage grounding; ready for poly RIE etch transfer.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Airborne molecular contamination (AMC) adsorption (amines and volatile organic compounds) neutralizes unreacted resist components and induces moisture absorption into hygroscopic resist matrices, altering secondary electron yield, exacerbating charging distortion, and causing resist footing/slumping that skews etched polysilicon gate CD by >6 nm.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Demonstrated robust, automated in-line CD-SEM measurement protocol for 180nm EBDW gate resist structures with real-time dynamic beam-induced shrinkage compensation, automated charging mitigation at low landing energy (500 eV), and zero-dose extrapolated gate CD extraction yielding sub-nanometer measurement repeatability across full 200mm wafers.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `inline_gate_cd_multisite_extraction_report.csv`
- [ ] `ebdw_resist_shrinkage_charging_analysis_summary.pdf`
- [ ] `calibrated_gate_cdsem_contour_profiles.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Zero-dose extrapolated critical dimension (CD_0) across wafer 9-point inspection map** | `180.0 nm` | +/- 3.0 nm (3-sigma <= 2.5 nm) | Non-linear regression analysis of 16-frame sequential CD-SEM measurements using exponential shrinkage model |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Static beam landing energy induced apparent CD drift under 30s electron exposure** | `0.0 nm` | <= 2.0 nm | Stationary field dwell stress capture comparing Frame 1 to Frame 30 edge positions at 500 eV landing energy |
| `ASSERT-03` | **Measurement precision repeatability (gauge R&R 10-cycle static wafer reload)** | `0.5 nm` | <= 0.8 nm (1-sigma) | 10-run unloader-reloader cycle measurement on identical site with dynamic image shift correction |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> Completion of 9-point wafer mapping across three qualification wafers meeting all three quantitative assertions; zero automated edge-detection recipe aborts; mathematical convergence of the dynamic shrinkage compensation model on all dies; signoff by Metrology Lead and DRAM Device Integration Lead.

# Standard Operating Procedure: High-Frequency Line-Edge Roughness (LER) & Line-Width Roughness (LWR) Spectral Analysis

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Power Spectral Density (PSD) analysis of high-frequency LER/LWR must decouple measurement noise (SEM shot noise and detector Poisson noise) from real high-spatial-frequency physical sidewall roughness. Unfiltered high-frequency components will corrupt gate dielectric breakdown field extraction and artificially increase modeled subthreshold swing variations across 180nm poly-Si access transistors.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At the 180nm EBDW gate level, high-frequency LER (spatial frequencies f > 1/(30 nm)) is primarily driven by shot noise during e-beam resist exposure, polymer aggregate size (HSQ or chemically amplified resists), and post-exposure bake acid diffusion blur. The extracted correlation length (xi) must be modeled with a Palasantzas rough surface self-affine fractal model (roughness exponent alpha ~ 0.5-0.7) to avoid underestimating gate leakage currents caused by local dielectric narrowing.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: CD-SEM edge-detection algorithm licenses (such as offline fractographic PSD or offline LER analytical engines) and ultra-high-resolution calibration grids (pitch standard 100nm ± 0.2nm NIST-traceable) require long lead times and vendor lock-in. Cross-platform calibration between in-line CD-SEM toolsets and atomic force microscopy (AFM) standard reference tools must be maintained with domestic secondary standards.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Characterizing high-frequency LWR PSD curves on 49-point wafer maps threatens inline cycle time, adding up to 45 minutes per wafer in beam dwell and image-processing time. Metrology recipes must balance frame averaging (typically 16-32 frames) to suppress beam charging and resist shrinkage against the statistical edge length required (L_box >= 2 um) to reach the 95% confidence interval for unbiased LWR.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron beam-induced resist shrinkage and carbonaceous contamination growth during repeated high-magnification CD-SEM scanning, artificially flattening high-frequency roughness peaks.
1. Aliasing and white-noise floor misestimation in PSD curves leading to inaccurate extraction of standard deviation (3-sigma LWR) and false correlation length values.
1. Uncompensated charging on isolated gate poly structures causing distorted secondary electron emission profiles and artificial edge-skew.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-01` | **High-Frequency CD-SEM Spatial Frequency PSD Extraction and Noise Floor Subtraction** | Automated In-Line High-Resolution CD-SEM (acceleration voltage 500 V, probe current 8 pA) with integrated off-line Digital Image PSD Metrology Software | 1. Load wafer into CD-SEM chamber and navigate to automated 9-point die locations on 180nm DRAM test array. 2. Acquire top-down secondary electron images of 5 parallel gate lines per site with FOV 2.0 um, line length 1.8 um, pixel size <= 1.0 nm/pixel, integrating 16 frames with beam-tilt compensation. 3. Apply threshold edge-detection algorithm (50% threshold on secondary electron derivative profile) to extract left and right line edges. 4. Compute the 1D discrete Power Spectral Density PSD(f) of both edges and line width: PSD(f) = (1/L) * |FFT[d(x)]|^2. 5. Identify the high-frequency white noise plateau (f > 0.05 nm^-1) and perform spectral noise-floor subtraction to derive unbiased high-frequency LER and LWR. | `Unbiased 3-sigma High-Frequency LWR <= 5.8 nm across all 9 inspection sites; Correlation length xi >= 22.0 nm; Baseline SEM white noise floor PSD_noise <= 0.45 nm^3.` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-02` | **Electron Dose and Resist Shrinkage Sensitivity Verification on LWR PSD Metrics** | CD-SEM with motorized stage and beam blanking shutter, coupled with Offline Metrology Analytical Workstation | 1. Position beam on target 180nm gate feature and acquire initial baseline image at 8 frames (Dose D0). 2. Subject target gate feature to continuous exposure iterations (2x, 4x, and 8x standard measurement frame doses). 3. Extract 3-sigma LWR, roughness exponent alpha, and correlation length xi at each cumulative dose step. 4. Quantify physical critical dimension shrinkage rate (dCD/dDose) and verify that high-frequency spectral components (f between 0.02 nm^-1 and 0.05 nm^-1) do not shift by more than the critical measurement threshold. | `High-frequency LWR spectral drift between 1x and 4x cumulative dose <= 0.4 nm; Total CD shrinkage after measurement <= 1.2 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Cleanroom Class 100 compatible nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV/radiation safety goggles, Full static-dissipative cleanroom bunny suit with ESD-compliant booties, ESD wrist strap connected to grounded chassis
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin/eye contact with IPA, flush thoroughly with eyewash station or copious DI water for at least 15 minutes and remove contaminated garments. In case of inhalation in confined cleanroom areas, immediately move personnel to fresh air; administer oxygen if breathing becomes labored. For nitrogen-induced displacement/asphyxiation risk, clear area immediately and administer CPR/oxygen as necessary.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: CD-SEM vacuum roughing pumps (dry scroll/turbo) must be vented directly to dedicated industrial cleanroom general solvent exhaust with continuous differential pressure monitoring (flow rate >= 35 CFM, negative pressure >= -0.5 in. w.g.). Loadlock purge exhaust must discharge directly into facility toxic/inert abatement line.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Spent solvent cleaning wipes and sample transfer containers contaminated with IPA must be collected in closed, flame-retardant, grounded solvent-waste bins and disposed of according to hazardous organic waste protocols. - **Max Air Exposure Window**: `30 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `4 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly developed or post-bake e-beam resist pattern on poly-Si/gate dielectric, dry, clean, free from organic residue and moisture condensation.

**Exit Objective Summary**:

critics.systems_engineer: Power Spectral Density (PSD) analysis of high-frequency LER/LWR must decouple measurement noise (SEM shot noise and detector Poisson noise) from real high-spatial-frequency physical sidewall roughness. Unfiltered high-frequency components will corrupt gate dielectric breakdown field extraction and artificially increase modeled subthreshold swing variations across 180nm poly-Si access transistors.
critics.domain_expert: At the 180nm EBDW gate level, high-frequency LER (spatial frequencies f > 1/(30 nm)) is primarily driven by shot noise during e-beam resist exposure, polymer aggregate size (HSQ or chemically amplified resists), and post-exposure bake acid diffusion blur. The extracted correlation length (xi) must be modeled with a Palasantzas rough surface self-affine fractal model (roughness exponent alpha ~ 0.5-0.7) to avoid underestimating gate leakage currents caused by local dielectric narrowing.
critics.supply_chain: CD-SEM edge-detection algorithm licenses (such as offline fractographic PSD or offline LER analytical engines) and ultra-high-resolution calibration grids (pitch standard 100nm ± 0.2nm NIST-traceable) require long lead times and vendor lock-in. Cross-platform calibration between in-line CD-SEM toolsets and atomic force microscopy (AFM) standard reference tools must be maintained with domestic secondary standards.
critics.laya_pm: Characterizing high-frequency LWR PSD curves on 49-point wafer maps threatens inline cycle time, adding up to 45 minutes per wafer in beam dwell and image-processing time. Metrology recipes must balance frame averaging (typically 16-32 frames) to suppress beam charging and resist shrinkage against the statistical edge length required (L_box >= 2 um) to reach the 95% confidence interval for unbiased LWR.
critical_failure_modes: Electron beam-induced resist shrinkage and carbonaceous contamination growth during repeated high-magnification CD-SEM scanning, artificially flattening high-frequency roughness peaks.
Aliasing and white-noise floor misestimation in PSD curves leading to inaccurate extraction of standard deviation (3-sigma LWR) and false correlation length values.
Uncompensated charging on isolated gate poly structures causing distorted secondary electron emission profiles and artificial edge-skew.

testcases.title: High-Frequency CD-SEM Spatial Frequency PSD Extraction and Noise Floor Subtraction
testcases.instrumentation: Automated In-Line High-Resolution CD-SEM (acceleration voltage 500 V, probe current 8 pA) with integrated off-line Digital Image PSD Metrology Software
testcases.pre_conditions: 180nm gate lines patterned via EBDW in positive/negative e-beam resist on poly-Si stack; wafer cleaned and de-gassed in loadlock chamber (< 1e-6 Torr) for >= 15 min; FOV calibrated to 2.0 um x 2.0 um at 512x512 pixels minimum.
testcases.procedure:
1. Load wafer into CD-SEM chamber and navigate to automated 9-point die locations on 180nm DRAM test array.
2. Acquire top-down secondary electron images of 5 parallel gate lines per site with FOV 2.0 um, line length 1.8 um, pixel size <= 1.0 nm/pixel, integrating 16 frames with beam-tilt compensation.
3. Apply threshold edge-detection algorithm (50% threshold on secondary electron derivative profile) to extract left and right line edges.
4. Compute the 1D discrete Power Spectral Density PSD(f) of both edges and line width: PSD(f) = (1/L) * |FFT[d(x)]|^2.
5. Identify the high-frequency white noise plateau (f > 0.05 nm^-1) and perform spectral noise-floor subtraction to derive unbiased high-frequency LER and LWR.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Unbiased 3-sigma High-Frequency LWR <= 5.8 nm across all 9 inspection sites; Correlation length xi >= 22.0 nm; Baseline SEM white noise floor PSD_noise <= 0.45 nm^3.

2. Subject target gate feature to continuous exposure iterations (2x, 4x, and 8x standard measurement frame doses).

testcases.pass_fail_criteria: High-frequency LWR spectral drift between 1x and 4x cumulative dose <= 0.4 nm; Total CD shrinkage after measurement <= 1.2 nm.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)
## High-Magnification CD-SEM Top-Down Image Acquisition & Edge Digitization Recipe Setup

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-CDSEM-003`  
**Process Generation:** Gen 3 (180nm / SKY130 Hybrid Node)  
**Action Type:** Make  
**Target Unit Cell:** Folded bitline 8F² / 6F² DRAM cell access transistor gate & open-source logic poly line  
**Knowledge Record:** [`cd_sem_image_acquisition_recipe.md`](./docs/knowledge/cd_sem_image_acquisition_recipe.md)

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Lifecycle

The following vertical workflow outlines the automated inspection sequence from wafer load to edge digitization:

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Wafer Load & Vacuum   │
│        Pumpdown        │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Beam Calibration:    │
│  500V Landing Energy   │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Field Alignment to   │
│    5nm Grid Anchor     │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│  Multi-Frame Top-Down  │
│     Capture 150kX      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│    Derivative Edge     │
│     Digitization &     │
│      Thresholding      │
│                        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│                        │
│   Metrology Gate CD    │
│  150-180nm Validation  │
│                        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

#### Step 1: Substrate Load and Vacuum Pumpdown
1. Load patterned 180nm wafer (EBDW/DUV patterned photoresist or etched polysilicon substrate) onto the automated electrostatic chuck (E-chuck).
2. Evacuate main load lock down to high-vacuum base pressure ($\le 1.0 \times 10^{-4}\,\text{Pa}$) to eliminate hydrocarbon contamination and beam scatter.

#### Step 2: Electron Gun Column & Beam Condition Setup
1. Set the field emission electron gun primary acceleration landing energy to **$V_{acc} = 500\,\text{V}$** (low voltage to prevent photoresist shrinkage, trench charging, and substrate damage).
2. Configure probe emission current to **$I_p = 8.0\,\text{pA}$** to preserve edge resolution while mitigating charging effects.
3. Align electron optical column: perform stigmator centering and dynamic focal tracking at the edge target fiducial.

#### Step 3: Coordinate Navigation & 5 nm Manufacturing Grid Alignment
1. Navigate motorized laser interferometer stage to coordinates of the DRAM array test macro.
2. Synchronize scan deflection coils with the layout coordinate system: lock step resolution strictly to integer multiples of the **$0.005\,\mu\text{m}\ (5\,\text{nm})$ physical manufacturing grid** to prevent quantization interpolation skew.

#### Step 4: High-Magnification Top-Down Scan Acquisition
1. Switch to high magnification: **$150,000\times$ nominal magnification** with field of view (FOV) centered over the DRAM access transistor active channel ($L = 180\,\text{nm},\ W = 220\,\text{nm}$).
2. Acquire image raster: $1024 \times 1024$ pixels at $0.005\,\mu\text{m} / \text{pixel}$ sampling.
3. Apply multi-frame averaging ($N = 16$ to $32$ scan frames) via fast raster scan to boost Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) without causing severe resist line slump.

#### Step 5: Secondary Electron (SE) Edge Digitization Recipe Execution
1. Extract line intensity profiles perpendicular to the poly gate longitudinal axis across the active diffusion region.
2. Apply a derivative-maximum threshold algorithm: compute the first spatial derivative of the SE profile ($dI/dx$). Define the physical edge boundary at the inflection point ($50\%$ threshold between peak blooming intensity and base floor level).
3. Record digitized edge coordinates $x_L(y)$ and $x_R(y)$ along the inspection window length ($L_{box} = 1.0\,\mu\text{m}$) at $5\,\text{nm}$ pixel pitch intervals for LER/LWR analysis.

---

---

### 4. Verified Literature Citations

1. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
   - Minimum drawn poly gate length: $150\,\text{nm}$ ($0.15\,\mu\text{m}$).
   - Minimum active diffusion width: $0.15\,\mu\text{m}$ ($150\,\text{nm}$).
   - Minimum contact hole dimension: $0.17\,\mu\text{m} \times 0.17\,\mu\text{m}$.
   - Manufacturing grid resolution: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$).
   - Maximum allowable overlay error between gate poly and active diffusion: $\le 35\,\text{nm}$.
   - Minimum resolvable half-pitch under DUV 248 nm KrF excimer laser exposure ($NA = 0.65, k_1 = 0.40$): $152\,\text{nm}$.
2. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
   - Access transistor unit geometry: channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$.
   - DRAM cell target: folded bitline 8F² / 6F² layout with minimum cell capacitance of $28\,\text{fF/cell}$ and leakage current target $< 1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Top-down CD-SEM edge digitization at high magnification (>150,000x) introduces electron-beam-induced charging and hydrocarbon deposition on 180nm polysilicon gate profiles, skewing edge-detection thresholds. The digitization algorithm must decouple secondary electron intensity drift from physical line-edge roughness (LER) by employing a normalized maximum-derivative edge-detection algorithm integrated with automated beam de-scanning.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: At 180nm critical dimension gates, e-beam shrinkage and resist/poly edge shrinkage during repeat scans corrupt LER/LWR power spectral density (PSD) high-frequency regimes. To achieve valid sub-nanometer edge digitization, beam landing energy must be strictly limited to <=500 eV with beam current <=8 pA, utilizing single-frame scan averaging to prevent line slimming while maintaining an edge signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) above 12 dB.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Procuring OEM automated CD-SEM recipes and certified magnification calibration artifacts (such as MetroCal or VLSI Standards 100nm pitch gratings traceable to NIST) incurs lead times of 12-16 weeks. The open-source DRAM foundation must standardize on vendor-agnostic 16-bit uncompressed TIFF image export formats and Python-based open edge-digitization scripts to avoid proprietary software lock-in.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: The gate metrology qualification milestone is gated by recipe throughput: edge digitization and field-of-view (FOV) acquisition must execute within 45 seconds per site across a 9-point wafer map to avoid starving downstream poly etch and oxidation furnaces, preventing fatal queue-time excursions in cleanroom pilot production.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron beam charging artifact leading to false edge blooming, introducing a >3.5 nm artificial positive bias in gate critical dimension measurements.
1. Hydrocarbon contamination build-up from vacuum chamber residual outgassing during extended raster scans, causing artificial edge roughness smoothing in LWR spectral analysis.
1. Misalignment of FOV pattern recognition leading to recipe failure or measurement of adjacent dummy gate structures instead of functional DRAM cell array access transistors.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-1-01` | **High-Magnification CD-SEM Metric Scale Calibration & Static Repeatability Verification** | Automated Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM) equipped with Schottky field emission gun (FEG), calibrated NIST-traceable 100nm pitch standard grid, and 16-bit low-noise image capture board. | 1. Navigate automated stage to the pitch standard alignment mark and perform automated autofocus, stigmation, and beam centering at 50,000x magnification. 2. Increase magnification to 200,000x over the 100nm pitch grating. 3. Execute 10 consecutive image acquisitions of the same target structure without unloading, using frame averaging of 16 frames per capture. 4. Apply 50% threshold linear approximation edge-detection algorithm to extract pitch and critical dimension values across all 10 acquired frames. | `Static pitch measurement mean must equal 100.0 nm +/- 0.5 nm; 3-sigma measurement repeatability across 10 consecutive acquisitions must be <= 0.45 nm.` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-1-02` | **180nm Gate Profile Edge Digitization and Line-Width Roughness (LWR) Robustness Test** | CD-SEM with automated image export pipeline, offline high-frequency edge analysis software (PSD and LER extraction engine), and automated optical/SEM pattern recognition alignment module. | 1. Run automated pattern recognition to locate 9 DRAM array test sites across center, mid-radius, and edge die positions. 2. Acquire top-down images at 180,000x magnification (pixel size <= 0.65 nm/pixel, 1024x1024 resolution) using 300 V landing energy and 5 pA beam current. 3. Automatically extract left and right line edges using normalized derivative peak detection across a 1.0 um line length inspection box. 4. Compute 3-sigma Line-Width Roughness (LWR) and edge position uncertainty profile across 5 consecutive repeat scans per site. | `Edge detection successfully locks on 100% of the 9 die locations without operator intervention; mean line width equals 180.0 nm +/- 5.0 nm; extracted 3-sigma LWR measurement error due to beam scan repeatability <= 0.80 nm.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (antistatic, double gloved), ANSI Z87.1 certified UV and impact safety glasses, Full cleanroom ESD gowning suit with conductive booties and grounded wrist strap, Particulate respirator (N95 or equivalent) during chamber load lock cleaning maintenance
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with IPA: Remove contaminated clothing and rinse skin thoroughly with copious running water for 15 minutes. Eye exposure: Flush eyes at cleanroom emergency eyewash station for at least 15 minutes holding eyelids open. Inhalation of nitrogen purge gas (asphyxiant risk): Move victim to fresh outdoor air immediately; administer CPR if breathing has ceased and seek immediate emergency medical services.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Continuous cleanroom recirculating air handling with dedicated dedicated local exhaust ventilation (LEV) on CD-SEM vacuum turbomolecular pump backing lines (minimum face velocity 0.5 m/s); room oxygen monitoring with audible low-O2 (<19.5%) alarm sensors.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Used IPA lint-free cleanroom wipes must be segregated into closed, grounded, flame-proof hazardous waste disposal bins; spent solvent waste collected for certified hazardous waste incineration according to ISO 14001 environmental protocols.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (IPA, semiconductor grade for chamber wipe-down)** | `67-63-0` | SEMI Grade 1 / VLSI Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen (Dry N2 for load lock vent and purge)** | `7727-37-9` | Grade 5.0 Ultra-High Purity (UHP) | `>= 99.999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `12 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly developed 180nm electron-beam resist or etched polysilicon gate lines, post-rinse and bake, strictly free of airborne molecular organic contaminants and moisture.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Metrology-cleared wafer surface with verified beam dose threshold (<0.05 C/cm2 accumulated exposure), free of localized carbonaceous pitch rings, ready for post-inspection ash or downstream gate oxide/etch processing.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Exceeding cleanroom air queue time induces ambient airborne hydrocarbon and amine condensation onto resist sidewalls, causing T-topping, sidewall footing, and artificial skew in CD-SEM edge-detection thresholds exceeding 4 nm.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full turnkey CD-SEM recipe package enabling automated high-magnification (>=180,000x) top-down image acquisition, sub-pixel edge digitization, and 3-sigma LER/LWR quantification across 180nm DRAM access gate arrays with sub-nanometer repeatability.

testcases.instrumentation: Automated Critical Dimension Scanning Electron Microscope (CD-SEM) equipped with Schottky field emission gun (FEG), calibrated NIST-traceable 100nm pitch standard grid, and 16-bit low-noise image capture board.
testcases.pre_conditions: CD-SEM chamber high vacuum <= 5e-7 Pa; electron gun accelerating voltage set to 500 V; beam current stabilized at 8.0 pA; stage temperature stabilized at 21.0 +/- 0.1 deg C; NIST-traceable pitch standard loaded onto stage.
testcases.procedure:
1. Navigate automated stage to the pitch standard alignment mark and perform automated autofocus, stigmation, and beam centering at 50,000x magnification.
2. Increase magnification to 200,000x over the 100nm pitch grating.
3. Execute 10 consecutive image acquisitions of the same target structure without unloading, using frame averaging of 16 frames per capture.
4. Apply 50% threshold linear approximation edge-detection algorithm to extract pitch and critical dimension values across all 10 acquired frames.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Static pitch measurement mean must equal 100.0 nm +/- 0.5 nm; 3-sigma measurement repeatability across 10 consecutive acquisitions must be <= 0.45 nm.

testcases.title: 180nm Gate Profile Edge Digitization and Line-Width Roughness (LWR) Robustness Test
testcases.instrumentation: CD-SEM with automated image export pipeline, offline high-frequency edge analysis software (PSD and LER extraction engine), and automated optical/SEM pattern recognition alignment module.
testcases.pre_conditions: 180nm post-EBDW gate pattern wafer loaded; patterned lines oriented perpendicular to SEM fast raster scan axis; vacuum pre-pump cycle complete with zero contamination interlock alarms.
testcases.procedure:
1. Run automated pattern recognition to locate 9 DRAM array test sites across center, mid-radius, and edge die positions.
2. Acquire top-down images at 180,000x magnification (pixel size <= 0.65 nm/pixel, 1024x1024 resolution) using 300 V landing energy and 5 pA beam current.
3. Automatically extract left and right line edges using normalized derivative peak detection across a 1.0 um line length inspection box.
4. Compute 3-sigma Line-Width Roughness (LWR) and edge position uncertainty profile across 5 consecutive repeat scans per site.
testcases.pass_fail_criteria: Edge detection successfully locks on 100% of the 9 die locations without operator intervention; mean line width equals 180.0 nm +/- 5.0 nm; extracted 3-sigma LWR measurement error due to beam scan repeatability <= 0.80 nm.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

## Document Title: Spatial Edge-Detection Algorithm & High-Frequency LER/LWR Signal Extraction
- **Module**: Metrology / In-Line CD-SEM & Lithography Verification
- **Technology Node**: 180nm Open-Source DRAM (DRAM Foundation VN) / SkyWater SKY130 Compatible
- **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)
- **Action Type**: Make

---

### 1. Workflow Architecture & Visual Execution Flow

```text
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Raw CD-SEM Line Scan  │
│         Image          │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Spatial Edge      │
│       Detection        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│    Edge Coordinate     │
│   Extraction: x_left   │
│      and x_right       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│  Baseline CD: W(y) =   │
│      x_right(y) -      │
│       x_left(y)        │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│     High-Frequency     │
│     LER/LWR Signal     │
│       Extraction       │
└────────────┬───────────┘
             │
             ▼
┌────────────────────────┐
│      Statistical       │
│     Acceptance and     │
│        Sign-Off        │
└────────────────────────┘
```

---

### 2. Concise Step-by-Step Procedure

1. **In-Line Image Acquisition & Sampling Grid Alignment**:
   - Load secondary electron (SE) CD-SEM raw micrographs acquired across the 180nm poly gate access transistor channel array ($L = 180\text{ nm}$, active diffusion width $W = 220\text{ nm}$).
   - Align the physical scan grid strictly with the foundry manufacturing grid resolution of $\Delta x = \Delta y = 0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
2. **Spatial Edge Detection (Threshold & Derivative Operator)**:
   - Apply a sub-pixel spatial derivative kernel along each orthogonal scan line $y_i$ perpendicular to gate line orientation:
     $$I'(x, y_i) = \frac{\partial I(x, y_i)}{\partial x}$$
   - Extract the local edge coordinates $x_{\text{left}}(y_i)$ and $x_{\text{right}}(y_i)$ using a normalized threshold algorithm set at the maximum secondary electron emission inflection point, bounded by the $5\text{ nm}$ manufacturing grid.
3. **Local CD & Roughness Profile Decomposition**:
   - Compute line width $W(y_i) = x_{\text{right}}(y_i) - x_{\text{left}}(y_i)$ along the inspection length.
   - De-trend low-frequency systematic taper and bowing to isolate local residual deviations:
     $$\delta x_{\text{left}}(y_i) = x_{\text{left}}(y_i) - \langle x_{\text{left}} \rangle, \quad \delta W(y_i) = W(y_i) - \langle W \rangle$$
4. **High-Frequency Spectral Extraction (PSD / Fourier Filtering)**:
   - Compute the Power Spectral Density (PSD) using discrete Fourier transformation of $\delta x(y)$ and $\delta W(y)$.
   - Apply a high-pass spatial filter with cutoff spatial wavelength corresponding to the $5\text{ nm}$ manufacturing grid limit ($f_{\text{max}} = 1 / (2 \times 5\text{ nm}) = 0.1\text{ nm}^{-1}$) to isolate high-frequency roughness components, preventing low-frequency drift and overlay offsets from corrupting LER/LWR metrics.
5. **Statistical Metric Evaluation & GDSII Grid Validation**:
   - Calculate high-frequency $3\sigma$ Line-Edge Roughness ($\text{LER} = 3\sigma_{\delta x}$) and Line-Width Roughness ($\text{LWR} = 3\sigma_{\delta W}$).
   - Verify that edge deviations do not exceed physical overlay error budgets against active diffusion boundaries.

---

### 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Targets

```text
              Critical Dimension & Metrology Bounds (nm)
              ┌────────────────────────────────────────┐
              │███████                                 │
 Overlay Limit┤███████                                 │
              │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
 Active Diff W┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓│
   CD Target L┤▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒       │
              │▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒▒       │
Spatial Cutoff┤░░                                      │
              │░░                                      │
              └┬─────────┬─────────┬────────┬─────────┬┘
               0        55        110      165      220 
```

| Metric / Parameter | Target Value | Tolerance / Constraint | Unit | Verification Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Nominal Access Gate CD ($L$)** | `180` | Minimum poly gate length $\ge 150$ | $\text{nm}$ | In-Line CD-SEM Mean Profile |
| **Active Diffusion Channel Width ($W$)** | `220` | Minimum active diff width $\ge 150$ | $\text{nm}$ | Automated CD Metrology |
| **Spatial Sampling Grid Resolution** | `5` ($0.005\ \mu\text{m}$) | Exact SkyWater manufacturing grid | $\text{nm}$ | Metrology Calibration Grid |
| **Maximum Gate-to-Active Overlay Limit** | $\le 35$ | Process boundary limit | $\text{nm}$ | Automated In-Line Overlay Station |

---

### 4. Verified Context Citations

- **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**:
  - Access transistor channel length $L = 180\text{ nm}$, access transistor width $W = 220\text{ nm}$.
  - Storage node capacitance requirement: minimum $28\text{ fF}$ per cell.
- **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**:
  - Manufacturing physical placement grid resolution: $0.005\ \mu\text{m}$ ($5\text{ nm}$).
  - Minimum active diffusion (`diff`) width: $0.15\ \mu\text{m}$ ($150\text{ nm}$).
  - Minimum poly gate length: $0.15\ \mu\text{m}$ ($150\text{ nm}$).
  - Permissible overlay error between gate poly and active diffusion: $\le 35\text{ nm}$.
- **1T1C DRAM Cell Operation, Folded Bitline Topology & Capacitance Budgets**:
  - Feature size $F = 180\text{ nm}$ in standard $8F^2$ folded bitline layout ($0.259\ \mu\text{m}^2$ cell area).

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Extracting spatial edges directly from raw CD-SEM secondary electron intensity profiles across 180nm poly gates introduces noise alias folding into the high-frequency domain. Without rigorous baseline polynomial background subtraction and sub-pixel edge interpolation (such as spline-fitted normalized thresholding at 50% max gradient), SEM scan line jitter will artificially inflate 3-sigma LER, skewing downstream OPC/EBDW dose correction tables.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: In 180nm open-source DRAM peripheral logic and folded bitline sense amplifiers, poly gate length is nominally 180 nm on a 360 nm minimum pitch. High-frequency LWR components above the spatial frequency cutoff of f_c = 1 / (2 * gate_length) directly induce channel length variation and threshold voltage (V_th) mismatch across differential pair transistors. The spatial edge-detection algorithm must isolate high-frequency white noise (SEM electron shot noise) from correlated physical gate edge roughness using Power Spectral Density (PSD) unbiased estimators.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Standardizing metrology scripts on proprietary CD-SEM vendor software (e.g., Hitachi or Applied Materials proprietary offline engines) violates open-source DRAM reproducibility. The pipeline must rely on standardized, vendor-agnostic 16-bit uncompressed TIFF outputs with verifiable open-source algorithmic parsing (Python/NumPy/OpenCV/SciPy) to avoid vendor software lock-in and unexpected licensing cost escalations.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Algorithm development must integrate seamlessly with our MPW tapeout execution timeline. The automated high-frequency edge-detection routine must process a standard 2048x2048 high-magnification CD-SEM field of view in under 1.5 seconds per site to maintain inline throughput for 49-point wafer mapping without delaying post-develop inspection (PDI) lot movement.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. High-frequency SEM secondary electron shot noise mistaken for intrinsic physical resist/poly gate edge roughness due to failure to apply Wiener deconvolution or high-frequency PSD baseline noise floor subtraction.
1. Threshold algorithm instability under local beam charging or sidewall slope variations, causing edge detection tracking loss along poly lines and false line-bridging or line-pinching alerts.
1. Aliasing of SEM scan raster pixel spacing against periodic bitline gate patterns (360 nm pitch), producing phantom low-frequency harmonic beats in the extracted LWR spectrum.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-2-01` | **Sub-Pixel Poly Gate Edge Position Detection & LER 3-Sigma Precision Verification** | Automated In-Line CD-SEM (500V to 800V landing energy, 8 pA beam current, calibrated with NIST-traceable 100nm pitch standard) paired with Offline Metrology Image Processor | 1. Acquire 10 consecutive frame-averaged 16-bit TIFF top-down CD-SEM micrographs of the 180nm poly gate test structure across center, mid-radius, and edge wafer die. 2. Execute spatial edge-detection algorithm using maximum derivative baseline fitting with 50% normalized signal threshold to extract left and right line edge profiles x_L(y) and x_R(y) over 1000 scan lines (step = 1 nm along gate length). 3. Calculate 3-sigma LER = 3 * sqrt(mean((x(y) - mean(x(y)))^2)) for both edges. 4. Verify repeatability across 5 repeated static image captures without wafer movement. | `Static measurement repeatability 3-sigma LER precision must be <= 0.35 nm; extracted mean CD must be 180.0 nm ± 2.5 nm; sub-pixel edge detection localization error must remain <= 0.15 nm.` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-2-02` | **High-Frequency LWR Power Spectral Density (PSD) and White Noise Unbiasing Extraction** | Analytical Metrology Server running Open-Source Spatial Analysis Pipeline with FFT/Periodogram modules; NIST SRM-2800 pitch standard reference database | 1. Compute discrete fast Fourier transform of w(y) to obtain raw 1D LWR Power Spectral Density PSD(f) from f_min = 1 um^-1 to f_max = 500 um^-1. 2. Identify and subtract the high-frequency white noise floor (flat plateau region between 200 um^-1 and 500 um^-1 corresponding to SEM shot noise). 3. Fit the physical roughness spectrum to the Palasantzas/HHCF (Height-Height Correlation Function) model to extract correlation length xi and roughness exponent alpha. 4. Compute unbiased LWR_3sigma_unbiased from the integrated physical PSD. | `High-frequency noise floor plateau extraction must show flat spectral slope (d(log PSD)/d(log f) between -0.05 and +0.05 in high-frequency limit); physical LWR (3-sigma, unbiased) must be <= 5.5 nm for 180nm target gate lines.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 Cleanroom Nitrile Gloves (anti-static), ANSI Z87.1 approved UV/Laser/Impact Safety Glasses, Full static-dissipative cleanroom gown, hood, and ESD conductive booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For skin or eye contact with cleaning IPA: Flush immediately with emergency eyewash/drench shower for 15 minutes. For inhalation of vapor: Relocate personnel to fresh air immediately; seek medical attention if irritation or dizziness persists.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Cleanroom air recirculation with dedicated laminar flow HEPA/ULPA filtration maintaining 90 fpm velocity; dedicated dry turbo pump exhaust vented directly to facility acid/solvent scrubbed exhaust line.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Dispose of IPA-saturated cleanroom wipes in sealed, FM-approved flammable waste containers; wafer handling occurs under non-hazardous inert environment (no liquid chemical discharge during metrology extraction).

| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `60 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `24 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Freshly developed EBDW resist on polysilicon / dry-etched polysilicon gate stack, free from airborne organic amine contamination and moisture condensation.
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: CD-SEM inspected polysilicon gate surface with minimal localized electron beam carbon deposition (charging/hydrocarbon contamination pad < 0.2 nm delta thickness).
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive environmental queue time causes airborne hydrocarbon/organic amine chemisorption on resist sidewalls, inducing resist line reflow, CD swelling (>3 nm drift), and artificial distortion of high-frequency edge profiles.

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full deployment and validation of an open-source, automated spatial edge-detection and PSD-based LER/LWR signal extraction algorithm, capable of sub-pixel edge resolution, automated SEM noise-floor unbiasing, and correlation parameter extraction on 180nm open-source DRAM gate structures.

# Standard Operating Procedure (SOP): Power Spectral Density (PSD) Analysis & Spatial Frequency Cutoff Characterization

**Document ID:** `SOP-MET-PSD-180NM`  
**Classification:** Metrology & Lithography / 180nm DRAM Generation (DRAM Foundation VN)  
**Process Step:** Electron Beam Direct Write (EBDW) / KrF 248nm Photolithography & CD-SEM LER/LWR Metrology  
**Equipment Class:** High-Resolution Automated CD-SEM with Spatial Metrology & Spectral Edge Detection  

---

## 1. Process Overview & Objective

This SOP defines the quantitative extraction, noise-floor subtraction, and spatial frequency cutoff characterization of gate line edge roughness (LER) and line width roughness (LWR) using 1D Power Spectral Density ($PSD(f)$) analysis on 180nm DRAM access transistor polysilicon gates ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, wordline pitch $360\text{--}400\,\text{nm}$).

By transforming spatial edge coordinates into the frequency domain, this protocol separates SEM high-frequency white noise (measurement noise floor) from true lithographic resist roughness, extracting the intrinsic roughness parameters: correlation length ($\xi$), roughness exponent ($\alpha$), and low-frequency plateau ($PSD(0)$).

```
                      +------------------------------------------+
                      | CD-SEM Image Acquisition (EBDW/DUV Poly) |
                      | FOV = 2.0 um x 2.0 um, Pixel Size = 1 nm |
                      +--------------------+---------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
                      +------------------------------------------+
                      | Multi-Threshold Edge Detection (e.g. 50%)|
                      | Extract Left/Right Edge Contours x_i(y)  |
                      +--------------------+---------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
                      +------------------------------------------+
                      | Discrete Fourier Transform / Periodogram |
                      | Compute Raw 1D Power Spectral Density    |
                      +--------------------+---------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
                      +------------------------------------------+
                      | Noise Floor De-biasing & Palasantzas Fit |
                      | Extract PSD(0), Cutoff (1/xi), LWR_unbias|
                      +--------------------+---------------------+
                                           |
                                           v
                      +------------------------------------------+
                      | Acceptance Verification against Specs    |
                      +------------------------------------------+
```

---

## 2. Step-by-Step Operating Procedure

### Step 1: In-Line CD-SEM Recipe Setup & Image Acquisition
1. Load 180nm DRAM patterned wafers post-poly gate etch / resist develop onto the automated CD-SEM chuck.
2. Align to cell array coordinate sites covering the access transistor array ($L = 180\,\text{nm}$, $W = 220\,\text{nm}$, active pitch and wordline pitch $360\text{--}400\,\text{nm}$).
3. Configure electron optics:
   - **Beam Energy ($V_{\text{acc}}$):** $500\,\text{V} - 800\,\text{V}$ (low voltage to prevent resist shrinkage).
   - **Beam Current ($I_b$):** $8\,\text{pA} - 12\,\text{pA}$.
   - **Field of View (FOV):** $2.0\,\mu\text{m} \times 2.0\,\mu\text{m}$ (yielding measurement length $L_{\text{box}} \ge 1.8\,\mu\text{m}$ along the gate line).
   - **Pixel Resolution:** $2048 \times 2048$ pixels (spatial sampling interval $\Delta y \approx 0.98\,\text{nm} \le 1.0\,\text{nm}$, satisfying Nyquist cutoff frequency $f_{\text{Nyquist}} \ge 0.5\,\text{nm}^{-1}$).
   - **Frame Averaging:** 16 frames to establish a stable signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).

### Step 2: Edge Contour Extraction & Profile Pre-Processing
1. Execute multi-threshold derivative edge detection at the $50\%$ intensity threshold on both left and right poly gate edges.
2. Record discrete edge deviations $x_L(y_i)$ and $x_R(y_i)$, and local critical dimension $w(y_i) = x_R(y_i) - x_L(y_i)$ across $N \ge 1800$ scan lines.
3. Remove low-frequency linear trend (wafer tilt / stage drift) via 1st-order polynomial detrending:
   $$\delta w(y_i) = w(y_i) - \langle w \rangle - (m \cdot y_i + c)$$
4. Apply a Hann window $W(y_i)$ to suppress spectral leakage at the line boundaries prior to fast Fourier transform.

### Step 3: Power Spectral Density (PSD) Computation
1. Compute the discrete periodogram for the line width variation:
   $$PSD_{\text{raw}}(f_k) = \frac{\Delta y}{N} \left| \sum_{j=0}^{N-1} \delta w(y_j) \cdot e^{-i 2\pi f_k y_j} \right|^2$$
   for spatial frequencies $f_k = \frac{k}{N \Delta y}$ where $k \in \left[1, \frac{N}{2}\right]$.
2. Average PSD across $M \ge 20$ identical poly line segments within the DRAM array to suppress stochastic periodogram variance.

### Step 4: High-Frequency Noise Floor Extraction & De-biasing
1. Identify the high-frequency measurement white-noise regime where $f \ge 0.1\,\text{nm}^{-1}$ ($100\,\mu\text{m}^{-1}$), where the spectral power flattens out into an asymptotic horizontal floor ($PSD_{\text{noise}}$).
2. Calculate the average baseline noise power density:
   $$PSD_{\text{noise}} = \frac{1}{K} \sum_{f_k > 0.1\,\text{nm}^{-1}} PSD_{\text{raw}}(f_k)$$
3. Subtract the white-noise floor to isolate the unbiased physical roughness spectrum:
   $$PSD_{\text{unbiased}}(f) = PSD_{\text{raw}}(f) - PSD_{\text{noise}}$$

### Step 5: Self-Affine Spectral Fitting & Cutoff Frequency Extraction
1. Fit $PSD_{\text{unbiased}}(f)$ to the Palasantzas (HHCF-equivalent) analytic roughness model:
   $$PSD(f) = \frac{PSD(0)}{\left(1 + (2\pi f \xi)^2\right)^{\alpha + 0.5}}$$
2. Extract the physical roughness parameters:
   - **Low-frequency spectral density plateau:** $PSD(0)$ (in $\text{nm}^3$).
   - **Correlation length ($\xi$):** Inverse of the spatial transition "knee" or corner frequency ($f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi \xi}$).
   - **Roughness exponent ($\alpha$ / Hurst exponent $H$):** Slope of the high-frequency roll-off in the log-log domain ($PSD \propto f^{-(2\alpha+1)}$).
3. Compute the unbiased $3\sigma$ LWR by integrating the debiased PSD up to the physical cutoff:
   $$\sigma_{\text{LWR, unbiased}} = \sqrt{2 \int_{f_{\text{min}}}^{f_{\text{cutoff}}} PSD_{\text{unbiased}}(f)\, df}, \quad 3\sigma_{\text{LWR}} = 3 \times \sigma_{\text{LWR, unbiased}}$$

---

## 3. Machine-Measurable Acceptance Criteria Target Metrics

```text
                      Target PSD & Roughness Metrology Metrics
                      ┌────────────────────────────────┐
                      │░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
    PSD(0) White Noise┤░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░│
                      │▒                               │
     Roughness Exp (α)┤▒                               │
Correlation Length (ξ)┤▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                     │
                      │▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓▓                     │
     Unbiased LWR (3σ)┤██████                          │
                      │██████                          │
                      └┬───────┬───────┬──────┬───────┬┘
                      0.0    21.2    42.5   63.8   85.0 
```

| Parameter / Metric | Target Value | Tolerance / Specification Limit | Unit | Physical Significance & Measurement Method |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Unbiased $3\sigma$ LWR** | $\le 14.4$ | $\le 18.0$ (Max $10\%$ of drawn $L=180\,\text{nm}$) | $\text{nm}$ | Integral of debiased PSD over $f \in [f_{\text{min}}, f_c]$; prevents threshold voltage variation ($\Delta V_{\text{th}}$) in the $L=180\,\text{nm}$ access transistor. |
| **Spatial Correlation Length ($\xi$)** | $25.0 - 32.0$ | $\le 35.0$ | $\text{nm}$ | Corner frequency cutoff parameter ($f_c = \frac{1}{2\pi \xi} \approx 0.005\,\text{nm}^{-1}$); defines scale of molecular resist aggregate clusters. |
| **Roughness Exponent ($\alpha$)** | $0.60 - 0.70$ | $\ge 0.50$ | dimensionless | High-frequency spectral roll-off slope; higher $\alpha$ indicates smoother high-frequency gate profiles. |
| **Noise-Floor Plateau $PSD(0)$** | $\le 85.0$ | $\le 110.0$ | $\text{nm}^3$ | Extrapolated zero-frequency power spectral density; governs total macroscopic edge variability along gate length. |

---

## 4. Context References & Traceability

1. **180nm DRAM Cell Layout Topology: Stacked Capacitor vs Deep Trench**
   - Access transistor geometry: Drawn channel length $L = 180\,\text{nm}$, channel width $W = 220\,\text{nm}$. LWR must be held within $\le 10\%$ of drawn gate length ($18\,\text{nm}$) to maintain leakage current below $1\,\text{fA/cell}$ at $85^\circ\text{C}$ and guarantee refresh intervals.
2. **SkyWater SKY130 Open PDK Design Rules & Lithography Grid**
   - Physical placement manufacturing grid: $0.005\,\mu\text{m}$ ($5\,\text{nm}$).
   - Critical poly gate dimensions ($L_{\text{poly}} \ge 0.15\,\mu\text{m}$, space $\ge 0.21\,\mu\text{m}$), DUV KrF $\lambda = 248\,\text{nm}$, $\text{NA} = 0.65$, overlay budget $\le 35\,\text{nm}$.
3. **Legacy 180nm DRAM Architecture & Cell Capacitor Engineering**
   - Bitline and wordline pitch ($360\,\text{nm} - 400\,\text{nm}$), gate oxide thickness $\approx 3.5\,\text{nm}$, requiring strict suppression of high-frequency LWR to avoid localized gate oxide breakdown and soft error retention loss.

---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: PSD decomposition of gate edge roughness must decouple primary beam shot-noise and pixel placement grid artifacts from resist molecular weight distribution. Integrating CD-SEM edge detection across spatial frequencies from 1 um^-1 to 100 um^-1 requires strict Nyquist sampling control without allowing frame-averaging electron dose to induce resist shrinkage (slumping) greater than 0.8 nm during offline image acquisition.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Unbiased LWR/LER extraction must apply the Palasantzas self-affine fractal model (PSD(f) = PSD(0) / (1 + (2*pi*f*xi)^2)^(H + 0.5)) to isolate the white noise floor from actual resist correlation length (xi) and roughness exponent (H). At the 180nm gate node with EBDW patterning, high-frequency cutoff f_cut must be strictly bounded beyond 30 um^-1 to prevent overestimating transistor threshold voltage variability (sigma-Vth) induced by gate dielectric leakage hot-spots.
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Single-vendor dependencies on automated offline LER/LWR metrology software licenses (e.g., Fractilia MetroLER or ProSEM) and high-brightness ZrO/W Schottky field-emission electron gun emitters threaten inspection throughput; multi-platform exportability to open-source Python-based PSD algorithms (using standardized TIFF/GDSII SEM metadata) must be validated.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: High-resolution SEM scanning of multi-die arrays to generate statistically significant line edge samples (minimum 2.0 um line length across 50 discrete gate tracks per die) risks adding 45 minutes of tool time per wafer, creating an inspection bottleneck ahead of dry polysilicon gate etch.

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Electron beam-induced resist shrinkage and carbonaceous contamination during multi-frame acquisition artificially damping high-frequency PSD amplitude and shifting apparent correlation length xi.
1. Improper SEM algorithm baseline noise subtraction causing false-positive spatial frequency peaks coinciding with 50/60 Hz mains interference or scan generator raster quantization.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-3-01` | **Unbiased Power Spectral Density (PSD) and White Noise Floor Extraction** | Automated Critical Dimension SEM (CD-SEM) at 500 V landing energy, 8.0 pA beam current, 150kX magnification, coupled with offline spectral analysis workstation. | 1. Position beam at 5 designated metrology sites across the wafer (center, top, bottom, left, right). 2. Acquire top-down CD-SEM micrographs of 180nm nominal lines over a 2.0 um continuous scan length with 1.0 nm/pixel sampling pitch. 3. Extract discrete edge coordinates x_left(y) and x_right(y) via 50% threshold derivative algorithm. 4. Compute 1D Fourier Transform periodograms and fit the Palasantzas model to extract the white noise floor PSD_floor. 5. Subtract white noise floor to calculate unbiased LWR_unbiased. | `Spatial frequency cutoff f_cut must exceed 35 um^-1; unbiased 3-sigma LWR must be <= 5.4 nm (3% of nominal 180nm CD); SEM image noise floor PSD_floor must remain <= 1.2 nm^2*nm.` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-2-3-3-02` | **Spatial Frequency Correlation Length (xi) and Roughness Exponent (H) Verification** | High-Resolution CD-SEM Metrology Tool with automated edge detection engine and FFT spectral analyzer. | 1. Acquire 50 gate line edge profiles across isolated and dense test structures. 2. Calculate the autocorrelation function R(r) and power spectral density PSD(f) from f_min = 0.5 um^-1 to f_max = 500 um^-1. 3. Perform non-linear least squares fit to determine correlation length xi and Hurst roughness exponent H. 4. Verify cross-correlation between left and right edges (c_LR) to ensure line-width variation is decoupled from placement drift. | `Correlation length xi must satisfy 15 nm <= xi <= 35 nm; Hurst roughness exponent H >= 0.50; left-right edge cross-correlation coefficient c_LR <= 0.15 at spatial frequencies f > 10 um^-1.` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Low`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Class 100 cleanroom nitrile gloves (double gloving), ANSI Z87.1 certified safety glasses with UV/laser radiation side shields, Electrostatic discharge (ESD) cleanroom suit and conductive booties
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: For vapor inhalation, remove subject to fresh air immediately; for skin/eye contact with IPA, flush with copious deionized water for at least 15 minutes. In case of high-voltage arc event, isolate primary 480V breaker and initiate standard electrical shock protocol.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dedicated CD-SEM vacuum turbomolecular pump exhaust routed to central cleanroom solvent scrubbed exhaust at >= 50 SCFM; loadlock nitrogen purge vent line tied directly to general scrubbed exhaust.
- **Waste Disposal & Neutralization**: Wetted cleanroom wipes and lint-free swabs saturated with IPA sealed in airtight, fire-rated polyethylene containers and managed under Class IB flammable solvent waste disposal.

**Chemical CAS Registry & Sourcing Specifications**:

| Reagent / Chemical Name | CAS Registry No. | Required Purity Grade | Target Concentration |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Isopropanol (wafer/loadlock cleaning solvent)** | `67-63-0` | VLSI Electronic Grade | `99.9%` |
| **Compressed Nitrogen Gas (chamber venting)** | `7727-37-9` | Ultra-High Purity 6.0 | `99.9999%` |

### Queue-Time (Q-Time) & Surface State Handshake Constraints

- **Max Air Exposure Window**: `45 minutes` | **Max N2 Storage Window**: `8 hours`
- **Incoming Wafer Surface State**: Developed and hard-baked chemically amplified e-beam resist on 180nm poly-Si/gate oxide stack, free of organic solvent residue and airborne molecular contamination (AMC).
- **Outgoing Wafer Surface State**: Vacuum-stabilized, metrology-cleared resist patterns with inspected beam spots uncharred and ready for reactive ion etching (RIE) of gate stack.
- **Critical Degradation on Q-Time Expiry**: Excessive exposure to cleanroom ambient moisture and airborne basic amines (NH3) causes resist footing/scumming and environmental degradation, altering line edge roughness and shifting PSD baseline by > 15% prior to poly etch.

### Verifiable Completion Assertions & Expected Results (Definition of Done)

**Exit Objective Summary**:
> Full spectral decomposition and automated PSD characterization of 180nm EBDW gate lines across 5 wafer sites, successfully decoupling high-frequency measurement noise from intrinsic resist LWR and validating spatial correlation length within PDK design window.

**Deliverable Artifacts Checklist**:
- [ ] `PSD_Spectral_Analysis_Report_DieMap.pdf`
- [ ] `Raw_Line_Edge_Coordinates_1nm_Grid.csv`
- [ ] `Unbiased_LWR_Spatial_Frequency_Cutoff.tiff`

**Quantitative Completion Assertions**:

| Assertion ID | Metric / Physical Assertion | Target Value | Acceptable Tolerance | Verification Instrumentation |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `ASSERT-01` | **Unbiased 3-sigma Line Width Roughness (LWR)** | `4.8 nm` | +/- 0.6 nm | FFT-based PSD noise floor subtraction across 100 um^-1 bandwidth |
| `ASSERT-02` | **Spatial Frequency Correlation Length (xi)** | `24.0 nm` | +/- 5.0 nm | Non-linear least squares fit using Palasantzas self-affine fractal model |
| `ASSERT-03` | **SEM-induced Critical Dimension Resist Shrinkage** | `0.35 nm` | <= 0.50 nm | 10-scan repeated exposure monitoring on dedicated dummy gate tracks |

**Lead Researcher Exit Sign-Off Criteria**:
> All 5 wafer sampling points demonstrate unbiased 3-sigma LWR <= 5.4 nm, noise floor PSD_floor <= 1.2 nm^2*nm, correlation length xi between 15 nm and 35 nm, with zero automated edge-detection pattern tracking loss across a 2.0 um scan track.

# Standard Operating Procedure: Gate Poly-to-Active Overlay Metrology & Vector Map Error Budget Verification (<=35nm)

**Category**: Metrology | **Generation**: Gen 3 (nm)


---

### Multi-Agent Council Critics & Risk Analysis (FMEA)

- **Systems Engineer Critic**: Topological check: Bondwire loop height (< 150 um) and parasitic bondwire inductance (target < 1.2 nH) must not degrade DDR power distribution network (PDN) or induce simultaneous switching noise (SSN). Pinout strictly conforms to JEDEC TSOP-54 / FBGA-60.
- **Domain Physicist Critic**: Physical constraint: Wafer backgrinding to 150 um must maintain total thickness variation (TTV) < 5 um with zero micro-cracking. Thermosonic gold/copper wirebond ball shear force must exceed 18 gf. Epoxy mold compound (EMC) CTE must match silicon (~3 ppm/K).
- **Supply Chain Critic**: Supply Chain veto: Leadframes, ceramic carrier substrates, and Sumitomo/Henkel certified mold compound are COTS. Wafer saw dicing and thermosonic ball bonding can be performed on local lab bonder or contracted to regional OSAT partner.
- **Project Manager Critic (Laya PM)**: Scope & Risk: Scoped within 40-80 engineer-hours. FMEA Priority: HIGH (Die dicing micro-chipping or thermosonic pad delamination causes open circuit or moisture ingress popcorning during 260°C solder reflow).

**Critical Failure Modes & Mitigation**:
1. Dicing blade vibration inducing micro-cracks penetrating active guard ring, leading to moisture degradation.
1. Intermetallic compound (IMC) voiding (Kirkendall effect) at wirebond pad interface causing open circuits.
1. Package delamination / popcorning during surface-mount reflow soldering due to mold compound moisture absorption.

### Machine-Measurable Acceptance Test Cases (Bits-to-Atoms Testbench)

| Test ID | Objective | Test Apparatus / Fixture | Procedure & Condition | Pass / Fail Criteria |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-3-01` | **Thermosonic Ball Wirebond Shear & Wire Pull Mechanical Strength Test** | Dage 4000 / Nordson Microtester Bond Pull & Ball Shear Test System | 1. Position shear chisel 3.0 um above bond pad aluminum metallization. 2. Perform destructive lateral ball shear test on 30 randomly selected bond balls across peripheral pads. 3. Hook bondwire loop at mid-span and execute vertical pull test to wire rupture according to MIL-STD-883 Method 2011. | `Ball shear force >= 18.0 gf with > 75% ductile residual aluminum coverage (Pass); Wire pull strength >= 5.0 gf (Pass).` |
| `TC-EBDW-GATE-PATTERNING-3-3-02` | **Electrical Die Sort (EDS) Cold/Hot Wafer Sort Array Pattern Test** | Advantest / Teradyne Automated Wafer Prober with Multi-Contact Epoxy Probe Card | 1. Step probe card pins to die contact pads with 50 um probe overdrive. 2. Execute JEDEC parametric DC continuity, leakage, and standby IDD current tests. 3. Run algorithmic March C- memory test across all rows and columns to map functional bit yield. | `Parametric DC continuity pass (Pass); Standby current IDD2N <= 150 uA (Pass); Array yield >= 90% functional dies (Pass).` |

### Environmental Health & Safety (EHS) & Hazmat Envelopes

- **Hazard Classification**: `Moderate`
- **Mandatory PPE**: Conductive ESD grounding wrist strap and heel grounders, Nitrile chemical-resistant gloves (for die-attach epoxy dispensing), Safety glasses with side shields, Particulate N95 respirator during wafer sawing wheel changes and dicing sludge cleanup
- **Antidote & Immediate Action**: Skin contact with uncured epoxy: Wash with copious soap and warm water (do not use solvents like acetone which increase dermal absorption). Eye contact with silica dicing slurry: Flush at eyewash for 15 minutes.
- **Ventilation & Interlocks**: Dicing saw fully enclosed with continuous high-volume DI water mist shroud. Mold press and post-mold curing ovens vented through dedicated VOC thermal oxidizer exhaust stack.
